docs.title: NL2SQL Platform Documentation
docs.text: This documentation describes the current runtime behavior of NL2SQL as implemented in code, including the parts that are not implemented yet. It is written for engineers and contributors who need a precise mental model of the architecture, contracts, and operational behavior. Where a page states a limitation, the limitation is the fact; nothing here describes intent.

docs.title: Problem this system solves
docs.text:
NL2SQL converts natural language requests into validated SQL across one or more datasources. The model emits a typed AST, never SQL text; the AST is checked against the retrieved schema and the caller's RBAC policy before any SQL is generated. The system is built for multi-datasource environments where correctness and inspectable failure matter more than conversational flexibility.

Model output itself is not reproducible; see Determinism for exactly which parts of a run are stable and which are not.

docs.title: Design philosophy
docs.text:
• Determinism where it is achievable: stable content-hashed IDs, sorted DAG layering, and a fixed graph topology. The LLM's output is not part of that guarantee.
  • Schema grounding: planning is constrained by a schema snapshot retrieved via structured chunks.
  • Explicit validation gates: logical validation enforces schema and RBAC constraints before execution.
  • Modularity: adapters, subgraphs, and executors are capability-driven and replaceable.
  • Bounded waiting: a global timeout bounds how long the caller waits for a run, not how long the work runs (on expiry the caller gets PIPELINE_TIMEOUT and the worker thread winds down in the background); each run carries a per-run cancellation token, and the graph itself runs in-process on a thread pool.
  • Observability: structured logging always; OpenTelemetry metrics and audit events when a caller attaches the pipeline callback (today, only the CLI does). See Observability Stack.

docs.title: Non-functional goals
docs.text:
• Reliability under partial failures (a circuit breaker on vector retrieval, SQL-agent retry semantics, errors returned as state rather than raised).
  • Extensibility via plugins and registries (datasources, subgraphs, executors).
  • Cost awareness (a row limit is baked into every generated statement; max_bytes is reported, not enforced).
  • Authorization at planning time (RBAC policy-based table access). The role is supplied by the caller, so the deployer owns authentication; see Security Model.

docs.title: High-level flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    User[User Query] --> Resolver[DatasourceResolverNode]
    Resolver --> Decomposer[DecomposerNode]
    Decomposer --> Router[Scan Layer Router]
    Router --> Subgraph[SQL Agent Subgraph]
    Subgraph --> Router
    Router --> Aggregator[EngineAggregatorNode]
    Aggregator --> Synthesizer[AnswerSynthesizerNode]

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• ArtifactRef: Metadata reference to persisted query results (URI, backend, schema_version).
  • Chunk: Typed, vector-indexed schema slice used for retrieval (datasource, table, column, relationship).
  • ExecutionDAG: Deterministic logical DAG of scan/combine/post operations.
  • GraphState: Shared state across the control graph pipeline.
  • SchemaContract: Canonical schema structure for a datasource (tables, columns, foreign keys).
  • SchemaMetadata: Descriptive metadata and statistics for schema elements.
  • SchemaSnapshot: Pair of SchemaContract + SchemaMetadata.
  • SubQuery: Decomposed, datasource-scoped query intent from the decomposer.
  • Subgraph: LangGraph subgraph that handles a specific execution capability (e.g., SQL agent).
  • ResultFrame: Adapter response containing rows/columns, row_count, and error metadata.
  • VectorStore: Chroma-backed vector index for schema chunks.
  • RBAC: Role-based access control enforcing datasource/table permissions.

docs.title: Supported Adapters
docs.text: The NL2SQL Platform supports a variety of datasources through specialized adapters. Each adapter is designed to handle the specific idiosyncrasies of its underlying database engine, from connection strings to specialized EXPLAIN plans.

docs.title: SQL Adapters
docs.text:
We provide first-class support for the following SQL databases via SQLAlchemy.

Adapter Description Status PostgreSQL Full support including EXPLAIN, JSONB, and SSL. 🟢 Stable MySQL Support for 5.7+ and 8.0. Includes MAX_EXECUTION_TIME management. 🟢 Stable Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise support via pyodbc and T-SQL dialect. 🟡 Beta SQLite File-based local development. 🟢 Stable DuckDB In-process analytical engine over local files. 🟢 Stable

docs.title: Core Libraries
docs.text:
For developers building their own adapters, we provide detailed reference documentation for our core SDKs.

  • SDK Reference: The core interface (DatasourceAdapterProtocol, from nl2sql-sdk) that all adapters must implement.
  • SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference: The helper base class (BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter) for building SQL-based adapters.

docs.title: Missing your database?
docs.text: Can't find what you need? Check out the Building Adapters guide to see how to implement your own.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All adapters are configured in the datasources section of nl2sql.yaml, usually one file per datasource in datasources/ (see Datasources).

# datasources/sales_db.yaml   (id defaults to the file name)
type: postgres
connection:
  host: "${env:DB_HOST}"
  port: 5432
  # ... see specific adapter docs for full reference

docs.title: Plugin / Adapter Architecture
docs.text: Adapters integrate NL2SQL with external datasources. Each adapter implements a protocol contract, is found by name in the registry (nl2sql.registry, built from Python entry points), and is registered in the DatasourceRegistry.

docs.title: Discovery and registration
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Config["nl2sql.yaml: datasources"] --> Registry[DatasourceRegistry]
    Registry --> Lookup["Registry.load('adapter', type)"]
    Lookup --> EntryPoints["nl2sql.adapters entry points, or a class registered in code"]
    EntryPoints --> AdapterClass[Adapter Class]
    AdapterClass --> AdapterInstance[DatasourceAdapterProtocol instance]

docs.title: Core adapter contract
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class DatasourceAdapterProtocol {
        +capabilities() Set
        +connect()
        +fetch_schema_snapshot()
        +execute(AdapterRequest) ResultFrame
        +get_dialect() str
    }
    class AdapterRequest {
        +plan_type
        +payload
        +limits
    }
    class ResultFrame {
        +success
        +columns
        +rows
        +row_count
        +error
    }

See sdk.md for the authoritative adapter interface reference and required fields/methods.

docs.title: Capability-driven routing
docs.text:
Adapters expose capabilities (supports_sql, supports_rest). The registry reads them once, at registration, and DatasourceRegistry.supports(datasource_id, *capabilities) is the one check every consumer asks. It fails closed: an unknown datasource, or an adapter whose capabilities() is missing or raises, supports nothing. These capabilities drive:

  • Subgraph selection (resolve_subgraph() in routing).
  • Executor selection (ExecutorNode._supports_sql() and SqlExecutorService.validate_request(), gating the SQL executor).
flowchart TD
    Adapter[DatasourceAdapterProtocol] --> Caps["capabilities(), read once"]
    Caps --> Check["DatasourceRegistry.supports() (fails closed)"]
    Check --> Exec[ExecutorNode capability gate]
    Check --> Subgraph[resolve_subgraph()]
    Exec --> Service[SqlExecutorService]
    Subgraph --> Graph[Subgraph Selection]

docs.title: Multi-datasource routing
docs.text: The control graph can resolve multiple datasources for a single user query. DecomposerNode produces sub-queries scoped to individual datasources. Each sub-query is then routed to a subgraph that matches its adapter capabilities.

docs.title: Extensibility model
docs.text:
To add a new adapter:

  1. Implement DatasourceAdapterProtocol (or extend a base adapter).
  2. Publish the adapter class as an nl2sql.adapters entry point, or register it in code (see Adding a New Adapter).
  3. Configure the datasource in the datasources section of nl2sql.yaml, with type: set to the adapter's name.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Adapter protocol: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/protocols.py
  • Registry: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/registry.py
  • Datasource registry: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/datasources/registry.py
  • Example adapter: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/adapters/sqlalchemy_base/adapter.py

docs.title: Building Adapters Guide
docs.text: The NL2SQL Platform is designed to be extensible. You can build adapters for any datasource, from SQL databases to REST APIs.

docs.title: Implementation Path
docs.text:
There are two primary ways to build an adapter. Choose the one that fits your target:

If you are checking... Use... Reference A standard SQL Database (Postgres, Oracle, Snowflake) nl2sql.adapters.sqlalchemy_base SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference A NoSQL DB, REST API, or custom driver Core adapter protocol Adapter Interface Reference

docs.title: Option 1: The "Fast Lane" (SQLAlchemy)
docs.text:
For 95% of use cases, you are connecting to a SQL database that already has a Python SQLAlchemy dialect.

Use BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter. It handles:

  • Automatic Schema Introspection (Tables, PKs, FKs)
  • Connection Pooling
  • Statistic Gathering
  • Transaction-based Dry Runs

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from sqlalchemy import URL
from nl2sql.adapters.sqlalchemy_base import BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter

class PostgresAdapter(BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter):
    interface_version = 1
    driver_modules = ("psycopg2",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]"'

    def construct_uri(self, args: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        # URL.create escapes the credentials; an f-string breaks on a password
        # containing @ : / # or %.
        return URL.create(
            "postgresql+psycopg2",
            username=args["user"],
            password=args["password"],
            host=args["host"],
            database=args["database"],
        ).render_as_string(hide_password=False)

Enforce statement_timeout_ms in connect() too: the base class records it but does not apply it (see the reference).

See the SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference for full API details.

docs.title: Option 2: The "Custom" Path (Protocol)
docs.text:
If you need to connect to something else (e.g., ElasticSearch, a CRM API, or a raw SQL driver), implement the core adapter protocol.

Implement DatasourceAdapterProtocol. You must manually handle:

  • Fetching and normalizing schema metadata.
  • Executing queries and formatting results.
  • Implementing safety breakers (row_limit).
  • Accepting the keyword arguments the engine builds every adapter with: datasource_id, datasource_engine_type, connection_args (the datasource's connection, references resolved), statement_timeout_ms, row_limit and max_bytes (its limits), and base_dir (the folder of nl2sql.yaml, or None). Take **kwargs so a later one does not break you. Do not connect in the constructor: engine.check() calls test_connection().
  • Optionally, a close() that releases connections; engine.close() calls it once.
  • Declaring interface_version = 1, the driver_modules it imports to connect, and an install_hint (see Class attributes).
  • Optionally, a default_schema attribute naming the schema an unqualified table resolves to. RBAC reads a two-part datasource.table policy entry as that table in this schema; without it, main is assumed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from nl2sql_sdk.protocols import DatasourceAdapterProtocol
from nl2sql_sdk.contracts import AdapterRequest, ResultFrame
from nl2sql_sdk.capabilities import DatasourceCapability

class MyRestAdapter(DatasourceAdapterProtocol):
    interface_version = 1
    driver_modules = ("httpx",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-my-rest"'

    def capabilities(self):
        return {DatasourceCapability.SUPPORTS_REST}

    def fetch_schema_snapshot(self):
        # call API, return schema
        pass

    def execute(self, request: AdapterRequest) -> ResultFrame:
        # run request, return rows
        pass

See the Adapter Interface Reference for the method signatures and compliance guide.

docs.title: Compliance Testing
docs.text:
Regardless of which path you choose, your adapter MUST pass the compliance test suite to ensure it handles types and errors correctly.

# See Adapter Interface Reference for test setup

docs.title: DuckDB Adapter
docs.text:
In-process analytical adapter for local files and ad-hoc analysis.

Implementation

This adapter extends BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter. It overrides connect() only to enforce statement_timeout_ms: DuckDB runs in-process and has no statement timeout setting, so the adapter interrupts a statement that runs too long.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The SQLAlchemy dialect lives in duckdb-engine, which ships in its own extra:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[duckdb]"

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: duckdb

connection:
  type: "duckdb"
  database: "./warehouse.duckdb" # File path, or ":memory:"

Persistence

:memory: databases live for the lifetime of the process. Use a file path for anything that must survive a restart, and an absolute path under a mounted volume when running in Docker.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: duckdb-engine (the duckdb:/// SQLAlchemy dialect) over the duckdb package.
  • URI Constructed: duckdb:///{database} — for example duckdb:///./warehouse.duckdb or duckdb:///:memory:.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Timeout interrupt() on a timer See Statement Timeout. Dry Run EXPLAIN Plans the query without executing it. Explain EXPLAIN Returns DuckDB's rendered operator tree as text. Costing Stubbed Returns a fixed cost of 1.0; see below.

docs.title: Statement Timeout
docs.text: When statement_timeout_ms is set, each statement starts a timer that calls the DuckDB connection's interrupt() once the limit passes. DuckDB stops the query and raises InterruptException, which the adapter reports as a refusal (QUERY_REFUSED) that the engine does not retry. The timer is cancelled as soon as the statement finishes or fails, so it never touches a later query. The limit covers running the statement; DuckDB materialises the result while it runs, so fetching rows afterwards is not timed.

docs.title: Optimization Details
docs.text:
• Dry Run: Uses EXPLAIN {sql}. DuckDB binds and plans the statement without running it, so success means the SQL parses and every referenced table and column resolves.
  • Explain: Returns the physical_plan text of EXPLAIN {sql} — DuckDB's box-drawn operator tree. It is human-readable, not machine-parsable.
  • Cost Estimate: Stubbed. DuckDB's EXPLAIN prints an operator tree carrying no cost or cardinality figures, so there is nothing real to report. The adapter validates the query and then returns a fixed estimated_cost=1.0 / estimated_rows=10, exactly as the SQLite adapter does. Do not use these numbers for planning or budgeting; a failed validation is signalled by estimated_cost=-1.0.

docs.title: Schema Introspection
docs.text: DuckDB qualifies schema names with their catalog (memory.main, warehouse.main). The adapter excludes system.main, system.information_schema and temp.main, leaving the schemas of the attached database.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
• Analytics: DuckDB is columnar and vectorized, which suits aggregation-heavy generated SQL. It reads Parquet and CSV directly via read_parquet() / read_csv().
  • Concurrency: A DuckDB file allows a single writing process. Treat it as a single-writer analytical store, not a shared OLTP database.

docs.title: Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) Adapter
docs.text:
Support for SQL Server 2017+ and Azure SQL.

This adapter extends BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter but provides specialized dry_run logic using SET NOEXEC ON to safely validate T-SQL.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: mssql

connection:
  type: "mssql"
  host: "localhost"
  port: 1433
  user: "sa"
  password: "${env:DB_PASS}"
  database: "my_db"
  driver: "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server" # Default
  trusted_connection: false

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: pyodbc. Requires system ODBC headers installed.
  • URI Constructed: mssql+pyodbc://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/{db}?driver={driver}. Built with SQLAlchemy's URL.create, so the user name and password are percent-escaped: a password containing @ : / # % works as written.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Timeout pyodbc Connection.timeout Client-side query timeout, in whole seconds. Dry Run SET NOEXEC ON Validates syntax without execution. Costing SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON Parses XML for StatementSubTreeCost.

docs.title: Statement Timeout
docs.text: SQL Server has no session setting for a statement timeout, so the adapter sets pyodbc's query timeout (Connection.timeout) on every new pooled connection. pyodbc counts whole seconds, so statement_timeout_ms is rounded up: 1500 becomes 2 seconds, and anything from 1 to 1000 becomes 1 second. When the limit passes, the driver cancels the query and the adapter reports it as a refusal (QUERY_REFUSED), which the engine does not retry.

docs.title: Optimization Details
docs.text:
• Dry Run: Uses SET NOEXEC ON. This is a native T-SQL session setting that compiles the query but ensures it is not executed. This is extremely safe and accurate for validation.
  • Explain: Uses SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON to retrieve the execution plan in XML format.
  • Cost Estimate: Parses the XML plan to find StatementSubTreeCost (estimated cost) and StatementEstRows (estimated rows).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
You must have the MS ODBC Driver installed in your Docker image or local environment.

Download ODBC Driver for SQL Server

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install unixodbc-dev

docs.title: MySQL Adapter
docs.text:
Support for MySQL 5.7+ and 8.0+.

Implementation

This adapter extends BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter. It overrides connect() to handle MAX_EXECUTION_TIME session variables.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: mysql

connection:
  type: "mysql"
  host: "localhost"
  port: 3306
  user: "root"
  password: "${env:DB_PASS}"
  database: "my_db"
  options:
    charset: "utf8mb4"

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: pymysql (Pure Python).
  • URI Constructed: mysql+pymysql://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/{db}?{options}. Built with SQLAlchemy's URL.create, so the user name and password are percent-escaped: a password containing @ : / # % works as written.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Timeout SET MAX_EXECUTION_TIME={ms} Session-level enforcement. Dry Run Transaction Rollback Starts transaction, runs SQL, rolls back. Costing EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON Extracts query_cost. Stats SELECT count(*), min(), max() Standard aggregation.

docs.title: Optimization Details
docs.text:
• Dry Run: Uses a Transaction Rollback strategy. It starts a transaction (BEGIN), executes the query, and immediately rolls back (ROLLBACK). Note: This means the query is technically executed, but its effects are reversed.
  • Explain: Uses EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON {sql} to get the execution plan.
  • Cost Estimate: Parses the JSON output to extract query_cost. MySQL does not reliably provide a global "estimated rows" count for complex queries, so this is often returned as 0.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • Row Estimation: MySQL's EXPLAIN does not always provide a reliable "Total Rows" estimate for complex joins compared to Postgres.

docs.title: PostgreSQL Adapter
docs.text:
The Postgres adapter is the Gold Standard adapter for the platform. It supports the full set of optimization features including EXPLAIN-based dry runs and cost estimation.

This adapter extends BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter, leveraging automatic schema reflection and statistics gathering.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: postgres

connection:
  type: "postgres"
  host: "localhost"
  port: 5432
  user: "postgres"
  password: "${env:DB_PASS}"
  database: "my_db"
  options:
    sslmode: "require" # Optional: passed to query string

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: psycopg2 (via sqlalchemy).
  • URI Constructed: postgresql+psycopg2://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/{db}?{options}. Built with SQLAlchemy's URL.create, so the user name and password are percent-escaped: a password containing @ : / # % works as written.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Timeout Native -c statement_timeout={ms} Enforced server-side. Dry Run EXPLAIN {sql} Highly accurate validation. Costing EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) {sql} Returns "Total Cost" and "Plan Rows". Stats Optimized Queries Fetches null_perc, distinct, min/max (no min/max for boolean, uuid; none for jsonb, bytea, arrays). A column that fails is skipped without aborting the transaction; see Column statistics.

docs.title: Optimization Details
docs.text:
The Postgres adapter leverages native EXPLAIN capabilities for robust validation and estimation:

  • Dry Run: Implemented via EXPLAIN {sql}. This validates the SQL syntax and ensures that all tables/columns exist without actually executing the query.
  • Explain: Uses EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) {sql} to retrieve the full query execution plan in structured JSON format.
  • Cost Estimate: Uses the same EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) {sql} command. It parses the root Plan object to extract:
  • Total Cost: Used as the query cost proxy.
  • Plan Rows: Used as the estimated result size.

docs.title: SSL Verification
docs.text: If connecting to Azure or AWS RDS with strict SSL, ensure you pass the CA certificate path in options or standard libpq environment variables, or use sslmode: disable for testing.

docs.title: SDK Interface Reference
docs.text:
The SDK, nl2sql-sdk (imported as nl2sql_sdk), holds the interfaces an extension implements. It depends on pydantic and the standard library only.

  • Adapters: nl2sql_sdk.protocols.DatasourceAdapterProtocol, with nl2sql_sdk.contracts.AdapterRequest and nl2sql_sdk.contracts.ResultFrame
  • Secret providers: nl2sql_sdk.secrets.SecretProvider

Everything is also exported from nl2sql_sdk itself.

docs.title: Interface: DatasourceAdapterProtocol
docs.text:
Adapters expose a capability-driven interface:

from nl2sql_sdk.protocols import DatasourceAdapterProtocol
from nl2sql_sdk.contracts import AdapterRequest, ResultFrame
from nl2sql_sdk.capabilities import DatasourceCapability

docs.title: Class attributes
docs.text:
Three class attributes let the engine check an adapter before it builds one.

Attribute Type Description interface_version int The version of this interface the adapter was written for: 1. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for, and any other version is a load error. driver_modules tuple[str, ...] The modules the adapter needs to connect, for example ("psycopg2",). The engine looks for each one with importlib.util.find_spec before it builds the adapter. install_hint str What to install when a driver module is missing, for example pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]". 
class SnowflakeAdapter:
    interface_version = 1
    driver_modules = ("snowflake.connector",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-snowflake"'

The adapter module must import without its driver, so import the driver where it is used and not at the top of the module. The built-in adapters declare:

Adapter driver_modules Extra sqlite ("sqlite3",) none: sqlite3 ships with Python postgres ("psycopg2",) nl2sql-engine[postgres] mysql ("pymysql",) nl2sql-engine[mysql] mssql ("pyodbc",) nl2sql-engine[mssql], plus Microsoft's ODBC driver duckdb ("duckdb", "duckdb_engine") nl2sql-engine[duckdb]

docs.title: Mandatory Properties
docs.text: Property Type Description datasource_id str Unique identifier (e.g., "production_db"). datasource_engine_type str Engine type string (e.g., postgres, rest). row_limit int Safety breaker (limit returned rows). max_bytes int Safety breaker (limit payload size).

docs.title: capabilities() -> set[DatasourceCapability]
docs.text:
Declares supported capabilities (e.g., supports_sql, supports_rest, supports_bound_parameters).

supports_bound_parameters (DatasourceCapability.SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS) says the adapter binds AdapterRequest.parameters by name to the :name placeholders in the SQL, and never pastes a value into the SQL text. The engine sends parameters (for a verified query) only to an adapter that declares it. Every built-in SQLAlchemy adapter does.

docs.title: execute(request: AdapterRequest) -> ResultFrame
docs.text:
Executes a plan-specific request and returns a normalized ResultFrame.

  • Args: AdapterRequest with plan_type, payload, and parameters (values to bind; empty for generated SQL)
  • Returns: ResultFrame with columns, rows, row_count, and error metadata

A query the database rejects is a result, not an exception: return ResultFrame(success=False, error=ResultError(...)). Two fields of the ResultError decide what the engine does with it:

Field Meaning retryable True when the query itself was wrong and a different query could succeed: bad syntax, an unknown table, column or function, a type mismatch. The engine reports EXECUTION_FAILED and sends the sub-query back to the planner, with safe_message as the feedback, while retries remain. False (the default) for a refusal the engine cannot plan its way out of: permission, a timeout, a lost connection, a read-only database. The engine reports DB_EXECUTION_ERROR and ends the sub-query. safe_message Shown to the planner and the user. Keep it to one short line: no SQL echo, no stack trace, no driver dump, and for a refusal nothing that names a host or a user.

Only the adapter knows its driver, so the classification is the adapter's; the engine names no database. SQLAlchemy adapters inherit it from BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter (see SQLAlchemy adapters). An exception that escapes execute is still caught, as a non-retryable EXECUTOR_CRASH.

docs.title: fetch_schema_snapshot()
docs.text: Required by every adapter; there is no capability flag gating it.

docs.title: dry_run(sql: str)
docs.text: Validates SQL without executing it (or safely rolling back).

docs.title: explain(sql: str)
docs.text: Returns the execution plan.

docs.title: cost_estimate(sql: str)
docs.text: Returns cost/row estimates. The pipeline does not currently call it, and there is no capability flag for it: DatasourceCapability carries only what something queries.

docs.title: Optional hook: render_sql(expression)
docs.text:
nl2sql_sdk.protocols.SqlRenderingAdapterProtocol. The engine builds every query as a sqlglot expression tree and, when the adapter has render_sql, passes it the finished tree and executes the text it returns. Without the hook the engine renders expression.sql(dialect=adapter.get_dialect()), so an adapter written before the hook keeps working. BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter implements that same default.

Override it only for what sqlglot cannot express for your database. The SQLite adapter, for example, rewrites EXTRACT and date truncation with STRFTIME and DATE(x, 'start of month'). Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB use the default.

get_dialect() must return a sqlglot dialect name (postgres, tsql, mysql, duckdb, sqlite, ...), not the SQLAlchemy name.

docs.title: Optional hook: execute_batches(request, batch_size)
docs.text:
nl2sql_sdk.protocols.StreamingAdapterProtocol. When the adapter has execute_batches, the engine reads the result through it, RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE rows at a time (default 10,000), and writes each batch to the sub-query's result artifact as it arrives, so a large result is never held whole in memory (see Artifact Store). Without the hook the engine calls execute and writes its one ResultFrame, so an adapter written before the hook keeps working unchanged.

The contract:

  • It is a generator (or returns an iterator) of ResultFrame.
  • Every frame carries the result's columns and at most batch_size rows. An empty result is one frame with its columns and no rows.
  • A failure, before the first row or between batches, is one frame with success=False and an error, classified exactly as execute would (retryable, safe_message), and it is the last frame. The engine discards whatever it had written.
  • The request is the same AdapterRequest execute gets; refuse one you cannot run the same way.

BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter implements it with fetchmany on a result opened with stream_results, a server-side cursor on drivers that have one (see SQLAlchemy adapters).

The hook is an optional protocol rather than a required method, so an adapter without it needs no change.

docs.title: Result types every adapter returns
docs.text:
These are part of the contract, so the same plan gives the same values on every database:

Plan operation Result type Example DATE_PART(unit, date), unit year, quarter, month, day INTEGER 2011 DATE_TRUNC(unit, date), same units ISO date string YYYY-MM-DD '2011-04-01'

The engine already wraps a date part in CAST(... AS INT) and a truncation in a YYYY-MM-DD format; an adapter that rewrites the inner nodes keeps those wrappers.

docs.title: Interface: SecretProvider
docs.text:
A secret provider is where ${id:key} references are read from. The secrets config names one by type (see Secrets).

from typing import ClassVar, Optional, Self

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, SecretStr


class AcmeVaultConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    url: str
    token: SecretStr


class AcmeVaultSecretProvider:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] = AcmeVaultConfig

    def __init__(self, client):
        self.client = client

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: AcmeVaultConfig) -> Self:
        try:
            import acme_vault  # the client library, imported only here
        except ImportError:
            raise ImportError("Missing dependency 'acme-vault'. Install 'nl2sql-acme-vault'.") from None
        return cls(acme_vault.Client(cfg.url, cfg.token.get_secret_value()))

    def get_secret(self, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
        return self.client.read(key)
Member Description interface_version 1. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for. config_model A pydantic model for the provider's entry in the secrets config, apart from id and type. Set extra="forbid", so a misspelt key fails when the config loads, and hold credentials as SecretStr, so they never print. from_config(cfg) Builds the provider from a validated config_model instance, after the engine has resolved any ${env:...} in it. Raise ImportError naming what to install when the client library is missing. get_secret(key) Returns the secret stored under key, or None when there is none.

A provider reads its settings from its entry only, never from the environment. The module that defines it must import without its client library, so the engine can validate the entry before building anything.

docs.title: Compliance Testing
docs.text: All adapters should pass the compliance test suite (schema introspection, type mapping, error handling, and result contract validation).

docs.title: SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference
docs.text: The SQLAlchemy Adapter (nl2sql.adapters.sqlalchemy_base, shipped in the nl2sql package) provides a helper base class for building adapters for any SQL database supported by SQLAlchemy.

docs.title: Base Class: BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter
docs.text:
Constructs a robust adapter by wrapping standard SQLAlchemy components.

from nl2sql.adapters.sqlalchemy_base import BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Automatic Schema Uses sqlalchemy.inspect to reflect tables, columns, and foreign keys automatically. Automatic Stats Runs optimized generic SQL queries to fetch min, max, null_percentage, and distinct_count (see Column statistics). Connection Pooling Manages engine lifecycle and connection pools. Transaction Safety Implements generic dry_run using transaction rollbacks. Default Schema default_schema reports the schema an unqualified table resolves to (inspect(engine).default_schema_name); RBAC reads a two-part datasource.table policy entry as that table in this schema.

docs.title: Column statistics
docs.text:
fetch_schema_snapshot() profiles every column of every table and view on one connection, one column at a time, so one column the database cannot profile does not fail the datasource's index:

  • Type-aware. The reflected SQLAlchemy type decides what is asked for. Boolean and Uuid (and the dialect types built on them: Postgres uuid, SQL Server bit and uniqueidentifier) get null and distinct counts but no MIN/MAX, which Postgres and SQL Server reject for them. JSON (and jsonb), LargeBinary (bytea, blob), ARRAY and any type whose name says json, blob, binary, bytea, xml or array get no statistics at all. min_max_skip_reason(type) in nl2sql.adapters.sqlalchemy_base.adapter gives the reason. Dates, times, decimals and UUIDs a driver returns for MIN/MAX are stored as ISO strings, floats and text.
  • Isolated. A statement that fails, for one column, a table's row count or a whole table, is caught and the connection's read-only transaction is rolled back, so on Postgres the aborted transaction does not fail every query after it. A rollback rather than a savepoint per column: profiling only reads, so it loses nothing, and it works on every dialect (pysqlite and DuckDB savepoints do not) without a round trip per column.
  • Recorded. A column whose statistics failed keeps its description with statistics: None; a failed row count is recorded as 0; a table that could not be profiled at all has no column metadata. Each table with failed columns logs one warning naming them with the driver's error, and the columns that skipped MIN/MAX by type; a table that only skipped by type logs at debug.

docs.title: Required class attributes
docs.text: interface_version = 1, driver_modules (the DBAPI driver your URL names, for example ("psycopg2",)) and install_hint. See Class attributes.

docs.title: construct_uri(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> str
docs.text:
Converts a configuration dictionary into a SQLAlchemy connection string.

  • Args: args - The connection dictionary from datasources.yaml.
  • Returns: A valid URL (e.g., postgresql://...).

docs.title: connect()
docs.text:
Override to provide custom connection arguments (e.g., timeouts, isolation levels).

The base class keeps statement_timeout_ms but does not enforce it: SQLAlchemy has no generic statement timeout and silently ignores an execution_options["timeout"]. Each adapter enforces it in connect() the way its driver allows: Postgres with statement_timeout, MySQL with MAX_EXECUTION_TIME, SQL Server with pyodbc's query timeout, DuckDB by interrupting the connection. An adapter that does nothing here has no statement timeout.

docs.title: close()
docs.text: Disposes the connection pool. The engine calls an adapter's close(), when it has one, once, from engine.close(). Building an adapter never connects: create_engine opens no connection until the first query or test_connection().

docs.title: local_path(path) -> str
docs.text: For a file-based database. The engine passes each adapter base_dir, the folder of the nl2sql.yaml the datasource came from (None when the config was built in code). local_path reads a relative path from there, and leaves an absolute path and :memory: as they are. The SQLite and DuckDB adapters call it in construct_uri.

docs.title: get_dialect() -> str
docs.text: Returns the sqlglot dialect name the engine renders SQL in: postgres, tsql, mysql, duckdb, sqlite, or any other name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts. It is not the SQLAlchemy dialect name (postgresql, mssql), which sqlglot rejects. The base class raises NotImplementedError, so every adapter must implement it. tests/adapters/unit/test_adapter_dialect_names.py checks every adapter registered under the nl2sql.adapters entry point.

docs.title: explain(sql: str) / cost_estimate(sql: str)
docs.text: The base class provides stubs. Override these to implement database-specific optimization logic (e.g., EXPLAIN ANALYZE).

docs.title: execute_batches(request, batch_size)
docs.text: Implements the SDK's optional StreamingAdapterProtocol (see the SDK). It opens the result with stream_results=True and yields it in frames of fetchmany(batch_size) rows, each with the columns, so no more than one batch is held as Python rows. stream_results is a server-side cursor on drivers that have one (psycopg2, the MySQL drivers); the others ignore it and buffer in the driver, which is still not a Python row list. A SQLAlchemyError, before the first row or between batches, is yielded as query_failed(exc), the same failed frame execute returns. execute itself still reads the whole result with fetchall.

docs.title: is_retryable_error(exc) -> bool
docs.text:
execute() catches every SQLAlchemyError the query raises and returns it as a failed ResultFrame (query_failed(exc)), with retryable from this method (see the SDK). The default reads the driver's SQLSTATE when there is one: class 42 (syntax or an unknown name) and 22 (a data or type error) are the query's fault, except 42501, insufficient privilege. With no SQLSTATE it falls back on the error's kind: ProgrammingError and DataError are retryable unless the message says permission or access was denied; OperationalError (timeouts, connections, locks) is not. The message the engine sees is the driver's first line, at most 200 characters, prefixed "The database rejected the query:"; a refusal gets a generic message instead, and the full error goes to the log.

Override it when your driver reports a query mistake another way. SQLite does: it raises OperationalError with no SQLSTATE for no such column as well as for a read-only database, so SqliteAdapter reads the message.

docs.title: SQLite Adapter
docs.text:
Simple file-based adapter for local development and testing.

Implementation

This adapter extends BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter. Note that timeout configurations apply to the database lock, not query execution time.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: sqlite

connection:
  type: "sqlite"
  database: "./my_data.db" # Absolute or relative path

A relative database is read from the folder of nl2sql.yaml when the config was loaded from a file (so nl2sql init --demo can write data/chinook.sqlite), and from the working directory when it was built in code. The DuckDB adapter does the same.

Persistence

If using Docker, avoid relative paths like ./my_data.db as they will be lost on container restart. Use an absolute path mapped to a volume, e.g., /app/data/my_data.db.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: Built-in sqlite3.
  • URI Constructed: sqlite:///{database}

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Timeout connect_args["timeout"] Controls Locking timeout, not execution. Dry Run EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN Validates parsing (rudimentary). Costing Stubbed Returns default cost=1.0.

docs.title: Optimization Details
docs.text:
• Dry Run: Uses EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN {sql}. If this command succeeds, the SQL syntax is valid.
  • Explain: Currently stubbed (returns a simple message) as SQLite's explain output is not in a standardized, easily parsable format like JSON or XML.
  • Cost Estimate: Stubbed. Returns a fixed cost of 1.0 and 10 estimated rows, as SQLite does not expose cost metrics comfortably.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text: • Concurrency: SQLite is poor at high concurrency. Use for Lite Mode or single-user testing only.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: NL2SQL exposes two API surfaces: a Python Core API for in-process use and a REST API for remote clients. Use the links below for the full technical references.

docs.text:

docs.text:

  • ExecutorRequest / ExecutorResponse (nl2sql.execution.contracts)

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
