  • Running the graph: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/runtime.py
  • Public API: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py, with the namespaces in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/
  • API Package: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.datasources: the engine's datasources, listed with their status, added and removed at runtime, tested, and their indexed schema.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• List every configured datasource with its status, capabilities and masked connection.
  • Add a Datasource (built, not connected) and remove one.
  • Connect to one datasource on demand, as check() does.
  • Return the indexed schema as the planner is given it.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/datasource_api.py (DatasourcesAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/types.py (DatasourceInfo)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/datasources/registry.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/models.py (Datasource)

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
method returns meaning list() list[DatasourceInfo] Every configured datasource, in config order, failed ones included. get(datasource_id) DatasourceInfo One configured datasource. Raises ValueError for an unknown id. add(datasource) None Builds the adapter without connecting, registers it, and adds the Datasource to engine.config; its description and sample questions are what indexing reads. Raises ValueError if the id is taken, the type is unknown, a reference does not resolve or the adapter rejects its connection settings (with every secret masked). Index it next: engine.index.build([datasource.id]). remove(datasource_id) None Takes the datasource out of routing and out of engine.config, and closes its adapter's pool. Its index entries stay until the next full index.build or index.clear. Raises ValueError for an unknown id. schema(datasource_id) dict The indexed schema as the planner is given it: {"datasource_id", "tables": [...]}, tables sorted by name, each with name, schema, row_count, description, columns (name, type, nullable, primary_key, description) and foreign_keys (columns, references_table, references_columns). Read from the latest schema snapshot, not the database; before the first index tables is empty. test(datasource_id) DatasourceStatus Connects to one datasource, as check() does: ready puts it back in routing, failed (stage connect, the reason and a fix) keeps it out. Raises ValueError for an unknown id.

DatasourceInfo is a frozen dataclass, exported from nl2sql:

field meaning id The datasource id. type Its type (the adapter's engine type for an adapter object). description Its description, or None. status ready once check() or test() connected to it, failed when one did not, unchecked before either ran. capabilities The capabilities its adapter declares, sorted. Empty for a failed datasource: nothing is routed to it. connection The configured connection, with every secret field masked as ***. References (${env:...}) are shown masked too. reason Why it failed, or None. 
from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Datasource

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
engine.check()
[(d.id, d.status) for d in engine.datasources.list()]   # [('shop', 'ready'), ('hr', 'failed')]
engine.datasources.get("hr").reason

engine.datasources.add(Datasource(id="ledger", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "ledger.db"}))
engine.datasources.test("ledger").status                 # 'ready'
engine.index.build(["ledger"])

To add every datasource of another nl2sql.yaml:

from nl2sql import load_config

for datasource in load_config("other/nl2sql.yaml").datasources:
    engine.datasources.add(datasource)

See Datasources for the Datasource fields, and When a datasource fails to start for running degraded.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.index: build the vector index that retrieval and grounding read, report its health, clear it, and inspect one search of it.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Build the index for some or every datasource, beside the live entries.
  • Report each datasource's progress as it goes, for a console or a job.
  • Report the index's health, clear it, and run one inspected search (and say what that search uses by default).

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/indexing_api.py (IndexAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/types.py (IndexProgress)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/rebuild.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/orchestrator.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/vector_store.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/enrichment_service.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/schema/store.py

docs.title: index.build
docs.text:
Signature: build(datasource_ids=None, *, full=False, curated_only=False, enrich=False, on_progress=None, on_datasource=None, switch_guard=None) -> RebuildResult

name meaning datasource_ids Only these datasources; every configured one when None. Ignored with full. full Rebuild every datasource into a new collection and swap it in when all succeed. Needed after changing the embedding model. curated_only Re-index only the verified queries, keeping each datasource's schema entries: no schema read, no model call. Not with full. enrich Ask the indexing_enrichment LLM for table and column descriptions. Off by default: it spends tokens. on_progress Called with a sentence before each step. on_datasource Called with an IndexProgress as each datasource starts, is done or fails. switch_guard A context manager factory held around each switch (the playground holds questions in flight back with it).

Returns a RebuildResult: ok (every requested datasource's new entries are live), stats (one dict per indexed datasource: datasource_id, schema_version and the entry counts), empty and errors (datasource_id, error).

IndexProgress is a frozen dataclass, exported from nl2sql, that serves a console line and a job's status record alike:

field meaning datasource_id The datasource. state started, then done or failed. A datasource that is unavailable or not configured is failed without started. counts With done: the entries written, by kind. reason With failed: why. 
from nl2sql import IndexProgress

def show(progress: IndexProgress) -> None:
    print(progress.datasource_id, progress.state, progress.counts or progress.reason or "")

result = engine.index.build(["shop"], on_datasource=show)

Raises: - ValueError with both full and curated_only. - EmbeddingModelMismatchError without full, when the collection records a different embedding model (rebuild with full=True, nl2sql index --full).

A failure of one datasource never raises: it is in errors, and that datasource keeps its previous entries. Enrichment errors are never raised: enrichment is best-effort and degrades to the unenriched snapshot.

Each datasource's new entries are written under a new build id, switched in when all are written, and the previous ones deleted. Other datasources' entries are never touched.

docs.title: index.health
docs.text:
Signature: health() -> dict

status (ok, empty, stale, missing), total, counts by entry type, built_at, embedding_model, one entry per registered datasource (entries, index_version, snapshot_version, built_at), problems and warnings. missing when no vector store is configured. A datasource that failed to start is a warning: "Datasource 'x' is unavailable: ". check() reports its status.

docs.title: index.clear
docs.text:
Signature: clear() -> None

Deletes and reinitializes the vector store collection, for every datasource. Every question fails at the resolver until the index is built again; to refresh an index, build it instead, which never leaves it empty.

docs.title: index.inspect
docs.text:
Signature: inspect(query, k=8, lambda_mult=None, types=None, datasource_id=None) -> dict

One MMR search of the live index, as the engine runs it: the candidate pool with scores, the picks in order and what was dropped. types limits the entry types (schema.table, ...). It reads index metadata only and needs no LLM. Raises LookupError when no vector store is configured.

docs.title: index.inspect_defaults
docs.text:
Signature: inspect_defaults() -> dict

What inspect searches with when not told otherwise, which is what the pipeline's own retrieval uses: k (8 picks), lambda_mult (1 is relevance only, 0 is difference only), fetch_multiplier (the candidate pool is k times it) and types, every entry type the index holds (schema.datasource, schema.table, schema.column, schema.relationship, schema.metric). The playground's Retrieval inspector starts from it.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Fetch schema via adapter.
  • Only with enrich=True: enrich schema metadata using the indexing_enrichment LLM. Enrichment fills blanks only: a table or column comment read from the database is never replaced. If the client cannot be built (no API key), the endpoint is unreachable, or the call fails, the unenriched snapshot is used and indexing continues.
  • Register schema snapshot and version.
  • Build schema chunks and refresh vector store.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.llm: the model each agent runs on, and replacing them at runtime.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• List each agent and the provider and model it runs on (list, get).
  • Replace the engine's whole llm section at runtime (replace).

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/llm_api.py (LLMAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/registry.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/llm_set.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/client_cache.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/models.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/models.py (LLM, AgentLLM: the llm section)

docs.title: AgentConfig
docs.text:
One agent's resolved settings, as LLMRegistry builds a client from them. agents_from_config(llm) (llm/registry.py) makes one per agent from the config's llm section (LLM configuration).

Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/models.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | provider | str | yes | Provider name: openai, anthropic, openrouter or ollama. | | model | str | yes | Model identifier. | | temperature | Optional[float] | no | Sampling temperature (default 0.0). None (null in YAML) sends no temperature parameter, for models that accept only their default. | | api_key | Optional[SecretStr] | no | API key or secret reference. Masked in repr, str and JSON dumps. None reads the provider's standard variable. | | base_url | Optional[str] | no | Endpoint override; defaults to the provider preset (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 for openrouter, http://localhost:11434/v1 for ollama). | | name | str | no | Agent name (default default). |

docs.title: LLMFileConfig
docs.text:
A set of agents the benchmark compares, one config at a time: LLMFileConfig.from_llm(llm) turns an llm section into it.

Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/models.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default | AgentConfig | yes | The top level of the llm section. | | agents | Dict[str, AgentConfig] | no | The agents that set their own fields. |

docs.title: llm.list
docs.text:
Signature: list() -> dict

Returns each agent by its name in the llm section, default first: its provider, model, temperature and inherited (True when the agent sets nothing of its own and runs on default). An agent given a model object shows its class as model and no provider. Never a key.

engine.llm.list()["ast_planner"]
# {'provider': 'openai', 'model': 'gpt-5.5', 'temperature': 0.0, 'inherited': False}

docs.title: llm.get
docs.text:
Signature: get(agent: str) -> dict

One agent's entry from list(). Raises ValueError for a name that is not an agent, listing the agents.

docs.title: llm.providers
docs.text:
Signature: providers() -> list[dict]

Each LLM provider this engine can use: the built-ins whose client library is installed, and any a plugin or Registry.add_llm registered. Each has name, label, key_variable (the environment variable it reads its key from; None for one that needs no key, such as ollama) and key_present (whether that variable is set). Never the key.

engine.llm.providers()[0]
# {'name': 'anthropic', 'label': 'Anthropic', 'key_variable': 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'key_present': False}

docs.title: llm.replace
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/llm_api.py (Runtime.replace_llm in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py)

Signature: replace(llm: LLM | Mapping, *, by: Optional[UserContext] = None, via: str = "python") -> LLMChange

Parameters: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | llm | LLM or a mapping | yes | The whole llm section: an LLM, or the section as written in nl2sql.yaml (a mapping, such as a request body). A mapping is checked exactly as the file is: strict keys with "did you mean", the model's validators, references kept in secret fields. A ${...} reference outside a secret field is an error rather than read, since the data did not come from the operator's file. | | by | Optional[UserContext] | no | Who is making the change; its user_id and roles are logged. | | via | str | no | The entry point making the change (python, api, playground). |

Returns: LLMChange (exported from nl2sql): by (via, and user_id and roles when by was given) and changes, each agent whose effective provider or model changed as {"old": "provider/model", "new": "provider/model"}. It holds no key.

Raises: - ConfigError for a section that does not validate, a provider that is not registered or not installed, or an agent whose API key does not resolve. Nothing changes. nl2sql-api answers it as HTTP 422 with the same text (PUT /api/v1/settings/llm).

Side Effects: - Builds the new clients (no model call), then swaps the engine's LLMSet and engine.config.llm together under the engine's lock. Runs already in flight finish on the old set. - One INFO line on the nl2sql.llm logger and one llm.changed audit record. Nothing is written to disk.

To use the llm section of a file: engine.llm.replace(load_config(path).llm).

See LLM configuration → Replacing the LLM at runtime.

docs.title: Internals: AgentConfig and LLMFileConfig
docs.text: AgentConfig (llm/models.py) is one agent's resolved settings, as LLMRegistry builds a client from them; agents_from_config(llm) (llm/registry.py) makes one per agent from the llm section. Its fields are provider, model, temperature (None sends no temperature parameter), api_key (masked in repr, str and JSON dumps; None reads the provider's standard variable), base_url and name. LLMFileConfig is a set of agents the benchmark compares, one config at a time (LLMFileConfig.from_llm(llm)). Neither is part of the public API.

docs.title: Behavioral Contracts
docs.text:
• Providers supported in the core registry are openai, anthropic, openrouter and ollama, held in PROVIDER_PRESETS in llm/registry.py; anything else raises ValueError: Unsupported LLM provider, naming the valid ones.
  • Each preset names a wire type (ProviderPreset.wire), and the client is built by that wire's adapter in llm/wires/ (WIRES[preset.wire].build_client). The Wire protocol (llm/wires/base.py) is build_client(model, temperature, **kwargs), structured_output_method, mark_cache(payload) and read_usage(response). wires.structured(llm, schema) is how every node asks for structured output; wires.wire_of(llm) picks the adapter from the client. See LLM configuration → Providers and wire types.
  • openai, openrouter and ollama are on the openai wire, served by ConfiguredChatOpenAI (llm/wires/openai.py), and differ only by preset: openai uses the client's own default endpoint, openrouter defaults to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, ollama to http://localhost:11434/v1. A config-supplied base_url overrides the preset, which also lets the same path serve any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, LiteLLM, a local proxy).
  • anthropic is on the anthropic wire, served by CachingChatAnthropic (llm/wires/anthropic_client.py), a langchain-anthropic ChatAnthropic whose requests go through the adapter's mark_cache (a cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"} breakpoint on the last system block), with max_tokens=16000, and whose tool calls go through the adapter's repair_tool_calls (arguments Claude nested under a single key the schema does not declare -- input, query, ... -- are unwrapped). It needs the nl2sql-engine[anthropic] extra; without it get_llm() raises a ValueError naming the extra. See LLM configuration → Anthropic.
  • openai, anthropic and openrouter require an API key (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY); ollama does not, and its preset supplies the placeholder key ChatOpenAI insists on.
  • The engine's LLM is one immutable LLMSet (each agent's settings and client), built when the engine is created and on every replace, without a model call. A run reads it once, when it starts (LLMRegistry.begin_run), so a run never mixes two sets.
  • Clients come from the engine's LLMClientCache, an LRU of 16 keyed on the agent's resolved settings with the API key only as a SHA-256 digest. Agents with equal settings share one client, and swapping back reuses cached clients. A client that falls out of the cache is closed (its close(), when it has one) once no set in use holds it; engine.close() closes them all.
  • A provider that needs a key and cannot resolve one does not stop the engine being built: check() reports it (missing_keys()), and get_llm() for that agent raises a ValueError naming the agent, the provider and the environment variable to set - not the raw openai.OpenAIError: Missing credentials.
  • Ollama is supported at the transport level. The pipeline calls with_structured_output (including the recursive PlanModel in the AST planner), so results depend on the chosen local model's structured-output capability.
  • LLMRegistry.get_llm() falls back to default if the name is missing, and raises ValueError naming the missing agent when no default is registered either.
  • Embeddings are not routed through LLMRegistry: each engine builds one embedder from its embeddings section, through the registry's embeddings providers (openai, which needs an OpenAI key even when chat runs through OpenRouter, or local, the key-free ONNX model bundled with chromadb), or uses the Embeddings(instance=...) it is given. Two engines never share one.
  • Determinism: every OpenAI-protocol client is built with seed=42 (Anthropic has no seed parameter), and every client with the agent's configured temperature, or none when it is null (see LLM configuration → Temperature).
  • A provider's HTTP 400 rejecting temperature is re-raised as a ValueError naming the model and agent and telling you to set temperature: null.
  • LLMRegistry.register_llms (internal) registers each agent under its key in the mapping, whatever its name field says.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.policies: who may read what. The roles, whether a caller may read a table, what a caller may read, and whether the rules match the datasources.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• List the configured roles.
  • Check one table for a user context, and list what a user context may read.
  • Check that every rule names a datasource the engine has.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/policy_api.py (PoliciesAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/auth/models.py (UserContext)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/auth/rbac.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/models.py (Policies, Role)

docs.title: UserContext
docs.text:
Exported from nl2sql. Fields: user_id (optional), tenant_id (optional) and roles (the RBAC roles, a list).

method returns meaning roles() dict[str, Role] The configured roles by id: each one's description, allowed_datasources and allowed_tables. Empty with allow_all. allows(user_context, datasource_id, table, schema=None) bool Whether user_context may read table. schema defaults to the datasource's default schema. allowed(user_context) dict What user_context may read, as the rules say it: {"datasources": [...], "tables": [...]}. validate() PolicyValidationReport Every datasource and table rule checked against the engine's datasources: one entry per rule (role, target, status -- OK, MISSING, UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_DS -- and details), and ok. The policies' own shape was checked when the config loaded. nl2sql policy validate prints it. 
from nl2sql import UserContext

analyst = UserContext(roles=["analyst"])
engine.policies.allows(analyst, "shop", "customers")   # True
engine.policies.allowed(analyst)                       # {'datasources': ['shop'], 'tables': ['shop.customers']}
engine.policies.roles()["analyst"].description

docs.title: Behavioral Contracts
docs.text:
• Policies enforce table namespacing (datasource.*, datasource.schema.*, datasource.schema.table, or datasource.table, read as the datasource's default schema only). See Policies.
  • Unknown roles yield empty permissions, and an empty roles list does too; neither raises. An unknown role beside a known one is ignored.
  • table_allowed(allowed_tables, datasource_id, table, schema, default_schema) is the single matching rule used by the logical validator (to refuse), the schema retriever (to strip a forbidden table's statistics), the executor's value check and the curated matcher. default_schema(ds_registry, datasource_id) reads the default schema from the adapter; main stands in when the adapter cannot report one.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provide one entry point: NL2SQL is built from one Config, owns everything it builds (its Runtime), and is the only thing an application talks to. Questions are top-level methods; everything else is a namespace.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Build the engine from a Config, resolving every name through a Registry.
  • Connect, and report what is ready, only when asked (check()).
  • Release what it opened (close()).
  • Answer questions (run_query, stream_query) and group the rest by subject (engine.datasources, engine.index, ...).

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py: the facade
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py: Runtime.from_config, what one engine builds
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/check.py: CheckReport, DatasourceStatus, EngineNotReady

docs.title: Creating an engine
docs.text:
Every way builds the same Config (see Configuration v2, section 4). Names in it (type: postgres, provider: anthropic) are resolved through a Registry; Registry.default() is used when none is passed.

constructor meaning NL2SQL(config, *, registry=None) Loads and validates: resolves every name, imports only the components the config uses, checks interface versions and driver modules, builds the secret manager, the adapters (not connected), the LLM settings (no model call), the embedder and the stores under storage.path. Raises one ConfigError listing every problem. It never connects to a datasource or calls a model. NL2SQL.from_config(path=None, *, registry=None) NL2SQL(load_config(path), registry=registry). path defaults to $NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml. NL2SQL.demo(*, llm=None, path=".nl2sql-demo") The demo: the three bundled SQLite databases, opened read-only from the installed package, with the demo roles and verified queries. Without llm, the first provider whose key variable is set is used with its default model; with none set, a ConfigError names the variables. 
from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Config, Datasource, Embeddings, LLM, Policies, Storage, load_config

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")

engine = NL2SQL(Config(
    datasources=[Datasource(id="shop", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "shop.db"})],
    llm=LLM(provider="anthropic", model="claude-sonnet-5-5"),
    embeddings=Embeddings(provider="local"),
    policies=Policies.allow_all(),
    storage=Storage(path=".nl2sql"),
))

cfg = load_config("nl2sql.yaml").with_datasource(
    Datasource(id="hr", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "hr.db"}))
engine = NL2SQL(cfg)

What one engine builds belongs to it alone: its secret manager (resolving ${provider:key} references through the providers in secrets), its embedder (from embeddings, or the instance given), and its stores:

store location Vector index <storage.path>/index/ Schema snapshots, plan cache, feedback <storage.path>/state.db Run traces <storage.path>/traces/ Result files <storage.path>/results/ (see Artifact Store)

A relative storage.path, and a relative SQLite or DuckDB file in a datasource's connection, are read from the folder of nl2sql.yaml when the config was loaded from a file, and from the working directory when it was built in code. engine.config is the current frozen Config, with secrets as references only; datasources.add, datasources.remove and llm.replace are the calls that change it.

Each engine owns its config: nothing is process-global and nothing writes the environment, so two engines in one process share nothing. The CLI, nl2sql-api and the playground build their engine from nl2sql.yaml and call check() at startup.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
with NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml") as engine:
    report = engine.check()
    if not report.ok:
        print(report)
    result = engine.run_query("Top 5 customers by revenue")
# close() ran: pools disposed, stores closed
method meaning check() -> CheckReport Connects to each datasource and records it ready, or failed with the stage (connect), the reason and a fix. A failed datasource is marked unavailable and left out of routing: the engine runs degraded, and a query that targets it fails with the reason. It also reports each agent whose API key does not resolve (no model is called) and the index status from index.health(). Raises EngineNotReady if a required: true datasource fails, or if datasources are configured and none is ready; the error carries the report. Safe to call again: a datasource that connects on a later call is routed to again. close() Disposes each adapter's connection pool (an adapter's optional close()) and closes the state store and the vector store client. run_query, stream_query and check raise afterwards. Calling it twice is fine. with NL2SQL(...) as engine: __exit__ calls close(). config The current frozen Config. closed Whether close() ran.

CheckReport has datasources (one DatasourceStatus each: id, status, required, stage, reason, fix), llm (agent to reason, for each key that does not resolve), index, and ok, true when every datasource is ready, every key resolves and the index is built. str(report) is a readable summary.

Building an engine is cheap and has no side effects outside storage.path, so it suits tests and notebooks. Startup policy belongs to the entry point: call check() straight after building the engine, refuse to start on EngineNotReady, and start degraded, printing the report, when an optional datasource fails.

docs.title: The shape
docs.text:
engine.run_query(question, *, datasource_id=None, execute=True, user_context=None, cancellation_token=None)
engine.stream_query(question, *, datasource_id=None, execute=True, user_context=None, cancellation_token=None)
engine.check(); engine.close(); engine.config; engine.about()

engine.datasources   # list, get, add, remove, schema, test
engine.index         # build, health, clear, inspect, inspect_defaults
engine.llm           # list, get, providers, replace
engine.policies      # roles, allows, allowed, validate
engine.curated       # validate, test
engine.results       # manifest, page, csv
engine.feedback      # record, list, stats, export, clear
engine.traces        # get, replay
engine.benchmark     # run_matrix, run_tier1, run_retrieval, tier2_configs, run_tier2
namespace reference run_query, stream_query, results Query API datasources Datasource API index Indexing API llm LLM API policies Policies API curated Curated answers → Checking them feedback below, and Feedback and signals traces, about() below benchmark Benchmarks

The namespace classes are internal: reach them through the engine, never by importing them. Each is built on first use.

The CLI, the playground and nl2sql-api are callers like any other: they use only these methods and namespaces, never the runtime behind them. test_the_cli_the_playground_and_the_api_use_only_the_public_api in tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py holds them to that, and test_the_playground_the_demo_command_and_the_api_import_only_the_public_nl2sql holds the playground, nl2sql demo and nl2sql-api to importing from the top-level nl2sql only (the playground and nl2sql demo keep a short, named list of exceptions in that test, each with the reason and the change that removes it).

docs.title: About
docs.text:
engine.about() describes the engine and its pipeline: version (of nl2sql-engine), git_sha (when running from a checkout, else None), python, and steps, one dict per step of a run in the order a run takes them. Each step has its node (the name usage and timings are recorded under), label, what it does, its kind (model when a model decides it, code otherwise) and its parent (sql_agent for the steps nested in the SQL agent). A model step also has its agent and the provider and model it is configured to run on; never a key. The playground's Pipeline page reads it.

about = engine.about()
[(s["node"], s["model"]) for s in about["steps"] if s["kind"] == "model"]
# [('curated_matcher', 'gpt-5.4'), ('datasource_resolver', 'gpt-5.4'), ...]

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text:
Ratings of answered runs, and the guardrail rates over recorded runs. They live in the feedback table of <storage.path>/state.db; the rates also read the traces in <storage.path>/traces. nl2sql feedback and the playground's thumbs up and down are built on it. See Feedback and signals for what is stored.

method does record(result, *, question, role, rating, note=None) -> dict Rate one run, "up" or "down", with an optional note (cut to 280 characters). result is the run's QueryResult or its JSON. The stored row is built from it and from the run's trace when one was kept; never rows, the answer, error messages or keys, and a run refused for the role keeps no SQL. A later rating of the same run replaces the earlier one. Returns the row; raises ValueError for another rating or a result with no trace_id. list(limit=None) -> list[dict] Every rating, newest first. stats(*, traces=None) -> dict Rates over the ratings plus the traces in traces (default: the engine's traces folder): feedback, refusals, refiner retries, validator failures, errors, and the plan cache's hit rate. export(path) -> dict Write the thumbs-up runs to path as draft gold entries for review; {"written", "skipped"}. Raises ValueError for the gold set's own path. clear() -> int Delete every rating; returns how many. 
result = engine.run_query("How many customers are there?")
engine.feedback.record(result, question="How many customers are there?", role="admin", rating="up")
engine.feedback.stats()["feedback"]   # {'up': 1, 'down': 0, 'up_rate': 1.0, 'down_rate': 0.0}

docs.title: Traces
docs.text:
engine.traces.get(trace_id) returns one recorded run's trace document, or None when none was kept (which runs are kept is settings.traces.mode). It reads only <storage.path>/traces, and the id must be a plain token (letters, digits, - and _), so no id can name a file elsewhere: anything else raises ValueError, as does a file in another trace format.

engine.traces.replay(trace) re-runs a recorded question, answering every LLM call from the trace document (no model is called), on a runtime of its own so the engine's config and LLMs never change. It returns a ReplayReport: the replayed result, how many recorded calls were served, the divergence (where the replay asked for a call the recording does not have) and the differences from the recorded result. It raises LookupError when a datasource the trace used is not configured here or does not answer; the message names each one and why. nl2sql trace replay is built on it (see Debugging).

engine = NL2SQL.demo()
engine.datasources.schema("chinook")["tables"][0]["name"]   # 'Album'
engine.index.health()["status"]                              # 'ok'
engine.index.inspect("top customers", k=4)["picks"]

docs.title: Top-level exports
docs.text: Clients import everything they need from nl2sql itself, never from an engine submodule: NL2SQL, QueryResult, SubQueryResult, RowSample, AnswerSource, ResultSummary, ResultManifest, ResultPage, ResultNotFound, MAX_RESULT_PAGE_SIZE, QuestionUsage, QueryEvent, UserContext, CancellationToken, configure_logging, what the namespaces return (DatasourceInfo, IndexProgress, LLMChange), the config (Config, load_config, load_env_file, ConfigError, Registry and the section classes Datasource, Limits, LLM, AgentLLM, Embeddings, Policies, Role, Storage, Secrets, Curated, Settings), what check() reports (CheckReport, DatasourceStatus, EngineNotReady), the error types (PipelineError, ErrorCode, ErrorSeverity), and the benchmark's BenchmarkAPI and BenchmarkConfig. The list is fixed by tests/unit/test_public_surface.py: adding or removing a name is a semver decision. The REST API (nl2sql-api) is held to importing only from nl2sql by an architecture test.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Answer a question with the NL2SQL pipeline: engine.run_query, engine.stream_query, and engine.results to read back what a run saved.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Invoke pipeline graph runtime.
  • Return a structured QueryResult, or the run as events.
  • Read a run's saved results by its trace_id.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py (NL2SQL.run_query, NL2SQL.stream_query)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py (QueryResult, result_from_state)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/results_api.py (ResultsAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/runtime.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/graph.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/state.py

docs.title: NL2SQL.run_query
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py, packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py

Signature: run_query(question: str, *, datasource_id: Optional[str] = None, execute: bool = True, user_context: Optional[UserContext] = None, cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = None) -> QueryResult

Every argument after the question is keyword-only. run_query passes the runtime's artifact store to result_from_state, so each sub-query carries a capped row sample alongside its artifact reference.

Parameters: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | question | str | yes | The question, in plain language. | | datasource_id | Optional[str] | no | Datasource override; otherwise resolved. | | execute | bool | no | Whether to execute SQL against datasource. | | user_context | Optional[UserContext] | no | RBAC context. Omitted (or None), the run starts with an empty UserContext, a caller with no roles, and RBAC treats it exactly as it treats any roles list it has no policy for. Pass one with a role to be granted anything. | | cancellation_token | Optional[CancellationToken] | no | A token (from nl2sql import CancellationToken) the caller cancels from another thread to stop the run. No further step and no further model call starts once it is cancelled; the step in flight finishes, and the result carries one CANCELLED error. The playground cancels it when the browser drops the request. |

Returns: QueryResult, built from the pipeline graph state by result_from_state.

Raises: No exceptions are raised by run_query; errors are returned in QueryResult.errors.

Side Effects: - Pipeline execution, LLM calls, optional database execution.

Idempotency: - Not guaranteed; execution can depend on external systems and time.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Use the caller's CancellationToken, or create one per run, and install signal / Ctrl+X handlers bound to it.
  • Pass the graph a callback that raises RunCancelled at the next node start or model call once the token is cancelled.
  • Build LangGraph pipeline from build_graph.
  • Execute graph in thread pool with timeout.
  • On timeout/cancel, return PipelineError with appropriate ErrorCode.

docs.title: QueryResult
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sub_queries | List[SubQueryResult] | no | One entry per decomposed sub-query. | | final_answer | Optional[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Answer synthesizer payload (summary, format_type, content, warnings, and truncated: True when a result was cut at the row limit). | | errors | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Pipeline errors (node, message, error_code, severity, provider, provider_response). provider and provider_response are set for a PROVIDER_* code and null otherwise; see provider failures. | | trace_id | str | no | Trace identifier. | | reasoning | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Reasoning events/logs. | | warnings | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Warning events/logs. | | artifact_refs | Dict[str, ArtifactRef] | no | Result artifact references keyed by execution node id. | | status | str | no | "success", "error", "plan_only", or "" when nothing ran. | | timings | Dict[str, float] | no | Wall-clock seconds per graph node, plus LangGraph for the whole run. | | usage | QuestionUsage | no | LLM calls, tokens and model time per node and for the whole question. See below. | | trace_path | Optional[str] | no | Where this run's trace file was written, or None when TRACE_MODE did not write one. See Debugging a Run. | | truncated | bool | no | True when any sub-query's result reached its row limit, so rows may be missing. See sub_queries[].truncated. | | result_manifest | List[ResultSummary] | no | The run's saved results, one per terminal DAG node (node_id, columns, row_count, truncated): the manifest the aggregator writes beside them. Never the rows; see Reading a run's saved results. Empty when nothing was saved. | | source | AnswerSource | no | Where the answer came from: type "verified" with the verified query's id, datasource_id and the params it ran with, or type "generated" with the other fields None. See Curated answers. |

errors holds only ERROR and CRITICAL entries; WARNING-severity pipeline errors are appended to warnings as the same summary dict.

A sub-query that succeeded contributes nothing to errors: the errors of the attempts it recovered from, and its warnings, are in warnings with their original severity and a sub_query_id. The run trace and subgraph_outputs[<id>].errors keep every attempt's errors for debugging. A sub-query that failed without a blocking error of its own (it ended with no SQL on warnings alone) adds a MISSING_SQL error, so the run reports "error".

status is derived: "error" when any blocking error is present, otherwise "plan_only" when no sub-query produced rows or an artifact (an execute=False run), otherwise "success". A state with no sub-queries and no errors leaves it empty.

Only a capped sample of the rows is inlined, in sub_queries[].rows. The full result set lives in artifact storage, addressed through artifact_refs; each combined result is listed in result_manifest and read back by the run's trace_id with the methods below.

docs.title: NL2SQL.stream_query
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py, events in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/events.py

Signature: stream_query(question: str, *, datasource_id: Optional[str] = None, execute: bool = True, user_context: Optional[UserContext] = None, cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = None) -> Iterator[QueryEvent]

The same run as run_query, with the same parameters, yielded as it happens. nl2sql run shows its live progress from these events.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
for event in engine.stream_query("Which genre sells the most tracks?",
                                 user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"])):
    if event.type == "node_finished":
        print(f"{event.data['node']} took {event.data['seconds']} s")
    elif event.type == "answer_delta" and event.data["field"] == "summary":
        print(event.data["text"], end="", flush=True)
    elif event.type == "final":
        result = event.data          # run_query's QueryResult, as JSON

A QueryEvent has a type and a JSON-ready data dict; event.sse() is the event as one Server-Sent Event (event: <type> and data: <json>), which is how nl2sql-api and the playground send it.

type data when node_started node A pipeline step began (the SQL agent's steps once per sub-query, and again on a retry). node_finished node, seconds, ok The step ended; ok is False when it raised. result_manifest trace_id, results The aggregator saved the results: results is the run's result_manifest and trace_id its request_id, so engine.results.page can be called before the answer is written. answer_delta field, text The next piece of final_answer.summary or final_answer.content, as the answer model writes it. final QueryResult.model_dump(mode="json") The run finished: exactly what run_query returns. A refusal, a provider failure, a timeout or a cancel is a final with status: "error", as run_query returns it. error message, error_code The run could not start or finish (an exception outside the pipeline, such as a missing API key when the graph is built).

Every stream ends in exactly one final or error.

How it works:

  • The run goes on a thread of its own, started on the first next(); the caller's context goes with it, so request-scoped keys (nl2sql.llm.request_key) reach the graph as they do in run_query.
  • run_with_graph is given a RunEvents callback, the same kind of LangChain callback as the timing and usage ones. A node's own run (its name is its langgraph_node) is a node_started / node_finished; the runnables inside a node are not events. The aggregator's end carries the manifest.
  • run_with_graph(stream_answer=True) asks the answer synthesizer to stream: its chain is streaming_structured (nl2sql.llm.wires) instead of structured, the same request with stream on. Each piece of the answer's tool call reaches on_llm_new_token; RunEvents parses the arguments so far as partial JSON and emits what summary and content gained. The pieces are joined into one message before the parser sees it, so the answer, and the token usage the call reports, are the unstreamed call's. On the Anthropic wire the joined message gets the same tool-call repair as an unstreamed one.
  • Closing the iterator before the last event (a client that went away) cancels the run's token, so it stops before its next step or model call.

Token by token, per wire: both the OpenAI wire (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and the Anthropic wire stream the answer's forced tool call, so the answer streams on every provider; how finely is the provider's choice, and one that sends the whole answer at once gives one answer_delta per field. The other model steps return a typed object the next step needs whole, and are not streamed. FakeLLMServer streams both wires, a word at a time, so replay mode and the keyless tests stream too.

docs.title: Reading a run's saved results
docs.text:
The aggregator saves each terminal result of a run as <tenant_id>/<request_id>/result_<node_id>.parquet and writes manifest.json beside them (see Artifact Store → The result manifest). engine.results reads them back by the run's trace_id (its run_id, the request_id of the REST routes). They read lazily from the parquet file: a page reads only its slice, and the CSV export reads and yields a slice at a time (CSV_CHUNK_ROWS, 10,000 rows), so neither holds the whole result in memory.

method returns meaning results.manifest(run_id, tenant_id=None) ResultManifest request_id and results: List[ResultSummary], the same entries as QueryResult.result_manifest. results.page(run_id, result_id, offset=0, limit=100, tenant_id=None) ResultPage Rows offset to offset + limit of the result whose node_id is result_id. limit above MAX_RESULT_PAGE_SIZE (1,000) is cut to it, and the page's limit says so. A page past the end has no rows. next_offset is where the next page starts, None at the end. A negative offset or a limit below 1 raises ValueError. results.csv(run_id, result_id, tenant_id=None) Iterator[bytes] The whole result as UTF-8 CSV, header first, one chunk per slice. The ids are checked before the iterator is returned, so a missing result raises before any byte is sent.

ResultPage has request_id, result_id, columns, rows (rows[i] is row offset + i), offset, limit, total_rows and next_offset.

Scope: results are read from one tenant's folder, tenant_id or else the engine's own TENANT_ID, the tenant every run of this engine writes under. Each of these raises ResultNotFound (a LookupError, exported from nl2sql): an unknown run_id, a run in another tenant's folder, a result_id the run's manifest does not list, and an id that is not a plain token (letters, digits, _, -; at most 128 characters). Ids are checked before any path is built, and the parquet path is rendered from the artifact template, never read from the manifest, so no id reaches a file outside the run's folder. Nothing else guards a result yet: any caller who knows a trace_id can read it.

result = engine.run_query("List every genre.", user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"]))
[saved] = result.result_manifest                   # node_id, columns, row_count, truncated
page = engine.results.page(result.trace_id, saved.node_id, offset=0, limit=20)
with open("genres.csv", "wb") as out:
    for chunk in engine.results.csv(result.trace_id, saved.node_id):
        out.write(chunk)

nl2sql-api serves these as GET /api/v1/query/{request_id}/results/{result_id} and .../{result_id}.csv; the playground serves the same two under /api/query/....

docs.title: SubQueryResult
docs.text: name type required meaning id str no Sub-query identifier. intent str no Semantic intent of the sub-query. sql str no SQL generated for the sub-query (subgraph_outputs[<id>].sql_draft). datasource_id str no Datasource the sub-query targets. schema_version str no Schema version used for planning. plan Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no The validated PlanModel, dumped. validation List[ValidationCheck] no name, passed, message per validation gate. rows Optional[RowSample] no Capped row sample; None when nothing executed or the artifact could not be read. status str no "success" or "error" for this sub-query, from its final attempt: "success" when it ended with SQL and, if executed, a result; otherwise "error". A retry that recovers reports "success". retry_count int no Plan/SQL refinement attempts made. plan_source str no "cache" when the plan came from the plan cache (no planner LLM call; still validated, generated and executed), "verified" when a verified query answered (no plan; sql is the verified query's own), otherwise "llm". See Determinism → The plan cache. row_cap Optional[int] no The row limit that bounded this sub-query's SQL (the datasource's row_limit, bounded by RESULT_ROW_LIMIT), or None when the plan's own LIMIT was smaller. truncated bool no True when the result has row_cap rows: it was cut at the limit and may be missing rows. A result of exactly row_cap rows may be whole; it is counted as cut.

docs.title: RowSample
docs.text: name type required meaning columns List[str] no Column names, in result order. rows List[List[Any]] no At most sample_rows rows (default 50). total_rows int no Row count of the whole result, not of the sample.

docs.title: State mapping
docs.text:
result_from_state normalises the raw graph state (LangGraph may return dicts or model instances for nested values):

QueryResult field Graph state source sub_queries[].sql subgraph_outputs[<id>].sql_draft sub_queries[].id / .intent / .datasource_id / .schema_version subgraph_outputs[<id>].sub_query sub_queries[].plan / .validation / .status / .retry_count / .plan_source / .row_cap / .truncated subgraph_outputs[<id>] usage.plan_cache_hits count of sub_queries[] with plan_source == "cache" sub_queries[].rows artifact_store.read_result_frame(subgraph_outputs[<id>].artifact) final_answer answer_synthesizer_response.final_answer source verified_match (set by the curated matcher on a verified answer; absent means generated) errors, reasoning, warnings, trace_id, artifact_refs, timings, usage top-level state

errors are projected onto a client-safe summary; stack_trace and details are deliberately not exposed.

result_from_state(state, artifact_store=None, sample_rows=50) reads rows only when an artifact store is supplied. A failed read is not fatal: rows stays None and a warning is appended.

timings is collected by NodeTimingCallback (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/timing.py), a LangChain callback handler that run_with_graph always attaches. It keys on metadata["langgraph_node"] where LangGraph provides it, so the keys are node names such as ast_planner, logical_validator, generator and executor.

docs.title: Usage: tokens, calls and model time
docs.text:
usage is collected by TokenUsageCallback (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/services/callbacks/token_handler.py), which run_with_graph attaches to every run, so the Python API, the REST API, the CLI and the demo playground all report it. It is also filled in, with whatever had been recorded, on a timed-out or cancelled run.

QuestionUsage:

name type meaning total UsageTotals The whole question. nodes Dict[str, UsageTotals] Keyed by graph node: datasource_resolver (the answerability check), decomposer, ast_planner, refiner, answer_synthesizer. calls List[LLMCallUsage] Every model call in order, with its node and model. plan_cache_hits int Sub-queries whose plan came from the plan cache. A hit makes no planner call, so it adds no ast_planner calls or tokens; a question answered entirely from the cache has no ast_planner entry in nodes.

UsageTotals:

name type meaning calls int LLM calls. The planner and refiner run once per retry, so a sub-query retried once shows ast_planner.calls == 2. input_tokens int Prompt tokens, including cached ones. cached_input_tokens int Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache (a subset of input_tokens). cache_write_input_tokens int Input tokens written to the prompt cache (Anthropic reports these; OpenAI does not). output_tokens int Completion tokens, including reasoning ones. reasoning_tokens int Reasoning ("thinking") tokens (a subset of output_tokens). total_tokens int As the provider reports it; input + output if it does not. latency_s float Seconds spent waiting on the model, summed over calls. The node's wall-clock time, which includes its non-LLM work, is in timings. cost Optional[float] Only when LLM_PRICES prices every call counted here; otherwise null. Cache reads are billed at cached_input, cache writes at cache_write (by default input x 1.25 on Claude, input on the OpenAI wire), the rest of input_tokens at input and output_tokens at output; see System configuration.

LLMCallUsage has the same token fields plus node, model (the model the provider says served the call, e.g. gpt-4o-2024-08-06), latency_s, cost, usage_reported and error.

Tokens are read by the adapter of the wire type that served the call (read_usage in nl2sql/llm/wires/openai.py or anthropic.py), picked by the model_provider the client stamps on the response; TokenUsageCallback only asks it. Both read LangChain's AIMessage.usage_metadata (input_token_details.cache_read, input_token_details.cache_creation, output_token_details.reasoning) into the same fields, and differ where their providers differ, as below. A detail the provider did not report is 0. A call whose result carried no usage at all is recorded with zero tokens and usage_reported: false; a failed call is recorded with its latency and error.

For OpenAI through langchain-openai (verified against the pinned 1.6.x by packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_fake_llm_server.py): prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens all arrive. OpenAI's chat completions API reports no cache-write count, so cache_write_input_tokens is 0 there.

For Claude through langchain-anthropic (provider: anthropic; verified against the fake Anthropic endpoint by packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_llm_wire_contract.py, which runs the same usage tests against both wires), Anthropic's usage maps as follows:

Anthropic usage field here cache_read_input_tokens cached_input_tokens cache_creation_input_tokens, or its per-TTL split cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens + ephemeral_1h_input_tokens cache_write_input_tokens input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens input_tokens output_tokens output_tokens

Anthropic's own input_tokens counts only the uncached tail of the prompt; langchain-anthropic adds the cache reads and writes back, so input_tokens here is the whole prompt, counted once, and both cache fields stay subsets of it. When the write is reported per TTL, langchain-anthropic sets the generic cache_creation detail to 0 and puts the tokens under the TTL keys, which are summed here.

Cost is (input - cached) * input_price + cached * cached_input_price + output * output_price, per million tokens. Prices are looked up by the served model name, then by the configured one, by exact match only, so a gpt-4o price never prices gpt-4o-mini. Cache writes are charged at the input price.

docs.title: REST API (FastAPI)
docs.text: This section documents the nl2sql-api FastAPI package that exposes the core engine over HTTP. Implementation lives in packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/.

docs.title: Application lifecycle
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/main.py

  • lifespan configures logging, loads the .env next to nl2sql.yaml (never overriding a variable already set), builds one engine with NL2SQL.from_config() (the file NL2SQL_CONFIG names, else ./nl2sql.yaml) and calls engine.check() before it serves. A required datasource that fails, or no datasource ready at all, raises EngineNotReady and the server does not start; an optional one that fails leaves it serving the others. The engine is stored in app.state.engine and closed at shutdown. When settings.observability.exporter is otlp, logs switch to JSON.
  • The package imports the engine only through the top-level nl2sql namespace (from nl2sql import NL2SQL, QueryResult, UserContext, configure_logging, ...), never an engine submodule. packages/api/tests/test_architecture.py enforces it.
  • Routers are included under /api/v1.
  • CORS is restricted to the origins in api.cors_origins (see CORS origins); with none configured, no cross-origin browser access is allowed.

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/dependencies.py

  • get_engine(request) returns the singleton NL2SQL instance.
  • Service providers (DatasourceService, QueryService, LLMService, IndexingService, HealthService) are created per-request with the engine.
  • get_user_context(request) (in nl2sql_api/auth.py) returns the caller's UserContext; see Caller role.
  • require_admin(request) (same module) guards the routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index; see Admin routes.

docs.title: Interactive docs
docs.text:
FastAPI serves Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc and the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json, with a summary, description and tag on every route. Start the server on a config:

NL2SQL_CONFIG=nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml nl2sql-api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000   # then open http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: API Index
docs.text: API Router Path Purpose Health routes/health.py Liveness/readiness checks. Query routes/query.py Execute natural language queries, whole or streamed as Server-Sent Events; page through or download a run's saved result. Datasource routes/datasource.py Manage datasource configs. LLM routes/llm.py Replace the LLM (PUT /settings/llm) and inspect each agent's model. Indexing routes/indexing.py Index management and status.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
FastAPI routers wrap most failures in HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)). Datasource and delete endpoints, and GET /api/v1/llm/{agent}, map ValueError to HTTP 404. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm answers a config error as HTTP 422 with its text.

POST /api/v1/query is the exception: pipeline errors are returned as a normal HTTP 200 inside QueryResponse.errors, and an unexpected failure returns a generic HTTP 500 with the traceback logged server-side rather than returned. POST /api/v1/datasource does the same: its exception can carry a connection string, password included, so the response says only that it failed and the cause goes to the server log.

Route handlers that call blocking engine code are declared with def rather than async def, so Starlette runs them in its threadpool instead of blocking the event loop.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The REST API is configured by the same nl2sql.yaml as the engine. Beyond the runtime server options in nl2sql_api.server (--host, --port, --reload), its own settings are the api section of that file (see The api section), and the admin roles are policies.admin_roles. The engine validates the api section and never reads it.

docs.title: CORS origins
docs.text:
api.cors_origins lists the browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Each entry is a full origin (scheme, host and, if non-default, port).

# api.yaml
cors_origins: [https://bi.corp.example, http://localhost:3000]

With one or more origins configured, only those origins are accepted and credentialed requests (cookies, Authorization) are permitted.

With none, no origins are allowed and credentials are disabled. That is the intended default, not a misconfiguration: a browser page served from another origin cannot call the API until you opt it in. The list is read from the engine's config, which is loaded at startup, so changing it requires restarting the server.

This setting governs the browser same-origin policy only. Non-browser clients -- curl, server-side callers, the Python SDK -- do not send an Origin header and are unaffected by it; use authentication and network controls to restrict those.

docs.title: Caller role
docs.text:
The engine enforces RBAC; the API only decides which role a request carries. It does not authenticate callers, and it never takes the role from the request body unless a dev flag says so. The get_user_context dependency reads, first match wins:

api key Role source role_header The name of a header a trusted proxy sets, e.g. X-NL2SQL-Role. Comma-separated values are several roles. Configure it only when the proxy authenticates the caller and overwrites the header on every request; otherwise any client can pick its own role. role One static role for every request, e.g. admin for a single-tenant deployment or the demo. trust_body_role true takes user_context from the request body. For local testing only: any client can choose any role. The server logs a warning at startup when it is on.

With no role from any of them, POST /api/v1/query and the result routes answer HTTP 401 with a message naming these keys; the engine never runs.

# api.yaml for the demo: every request runs as admin.
role: admin

# api.yaml behind an authenticating proxy that sets X-NL2SQL-Role.
role_header: X-NL2SQL-Role

This is a seam, not an auth provider: to integrate one, override the get_user_context dependency (app.dependency_overrides[get_user_context] = ...) or put the provider in the proxy.

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text:
The routes that change the running process need an admin role, checked by the require_admin dependency in nl2sql_api/auth.py:

  • POST /api/v1/datasource and DELETE /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_id}
  • PUT /api/v1/settings/llm
  • POST /api/v1/index/{datasource_id}, POST /api/v1/index-all and DELETE /api/v1/index
Key Default Meaning policies.admin_roles [admin] The roles that may call the admin routes.

The roles come from the same sources as Caller role. A request whose roles include one in policies.admin_roles is let through; one with roles but none of them admin is HTTP 403; one with no role is HTTP 401.

With none of api.role_header, api.role or api.trust_body_role set, admin routes answer only clients on loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1) and return HTTP 403 to everyone else, with a message naming the keys to set. A fresh local install can still register and index datasources, and a port published by mistake does not hand them out. Two consequences:

  • In Docker, a request through a published port arrives from the bridge gateway, not loopback, so admin routes need a role setting there.
  • A reverse proxy on the same host makes every request look like loopback. Behind one, configure api.role_header.

The read-only routes (/health, /ready, GET /datasource, GET /llm, which never returns API keys, and GET /index/status) need no role.

# The proxy sets X-NL2SQL-Role; only "ops" may change datasources and the index.
# api.yaml
role_header: X-NL2SQL-Role
# policies.yaml (with the roles)
admin_roles: [ops]

docs.title: Request/Response Models
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/models/datasource.py

docs.title: DatasourceRequest
docs.text: field type required meaning config Dict[str, Any] yes One datasource, in the shape of a datasources entry of nl2sql.yaml: id, type, connection, and optionally description, limits, preferred_tables, sample_questions, required. See Datasources.

docs.title: DatasourceResponse
docs.text: field type required meaning success bool yes Operation status. message str yes Result message. datasource_id Optional[str] no Datasource ID.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/datasource
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/datasource.py

Request model: DatasourceRequest

Response model: DatasourceResponse

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Execution flow: - Validates config as a Datasource and delegates to engine.datasources.add(...): the adapter is built (not connected) and the datasource joins engine.config. Nothing is written to the config files and nothing is indexed.

Errors: - No role -> HTTP 401; a role not in policies.admin_roles -> HTTP 403. - A failure to add -> HTTP 500 with a generic message. The exception, which can hold the connection string, is logged server-side and never returned.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasource
docs.text:
Response: {"datasources": [...]}, engine.datasources.list(): every configured datasource with its id, type, description, status (ready, failed with a reason, or unchecked), capabilities and connection with every secret masked. No role needed.

{"datasources": [
  {"id": "shop", "type": "postgres", "description": "Orders and customers", "status": "ready",
   "capabilities": ["supports_sql"], "connection": {"host": "db", "user": "app", "password": "***"},
   "reason": null}
]}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Response: one datasource, as the list shows it (engine.datasources.get(...)).

Errors: - An unknown id -> HTTP 404.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Admin only: see Admin routes.

Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.datasources.remove(...): the datasource leaves routing and engine.config, and its connection pool is closed. Nothing is written to the config files, and its index entries stay until the next full index.

Response: {"success": true, "message": "...", "datasource_id": "..."}.

Errors: - An unknown id -> HTTP 404. - Other exceptions -> HTTP 500.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/health
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/health.py

Response model: SuccessResponse

Returns: {"success": true, "message": "NL2SQL API is running"}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/ready
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/health.py

Response model: SuccessResponse

Returns: {"success": true, "message": "NL2SQL API is ready"}

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: POST /api/v1/index/{datasource_id}, POST /api/v1/index-all and DELETE /api/v1/index are admin only (see Admin routes); GET /api/v1/index/status is open.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/index/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.build([datasource_id]): the new entries are written beside the live ones and switched in when all are written. No enrichment model call is made: enrichment is opt-in in the engine and these routes do not ask for it.

Response: {"success": true, "datasource_id": "...", "indexing_stats": {...}, "message": "..."}

Errors: - A datasource that fails to index (unknown, unavailable, unreadable) -> HTTP 500 naming the reason. It keeps its previous entries.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/index-all
docs.text:
Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.build(), every configured datasource, without enrichment.

Response: {"success": <every datasource indexed>, "indexing_results": {"stats": [...], "empty": [...], "errors": [...]}, "message": "..."}. A datasource that fails is in errors (datasource_id, error) and keeps its previous entries.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/index
docs.text: Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.clear().

docs.title: GET /api/v1/index/status
docs.text:
Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.health() (see Indexing API → index.health), the same report the playground's index panel shows.

Response (illustrative):

{
  "status": "ok",
  "total": 162,
  "counts": {"schema.column": 121, "schema.datasource": 3, "schema.relationship": 18, "schema.table": 20},
  "built_at": "2026-09-22T12:35:42+00:00",
  "embedding_model": "all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
  "datasources": [
    {"datasource_id": "chinook", "entries": 87, "index_version": "20260922123542_ceed8",
     "snapshot_version": "20260922123542_ceed8", "built_at": "2026-09-22T12:35:42+00:00"},
    {"datasource_id": "support", "entries": 36, "index_version": "...",
     "snapshot_version": "...", "built_at": "2026-09-22T12:35:42+00:00"},
    {"datasource_id": "webanalytics", "entries": 39, "index_version": "...",
     "snapshot_version": "...", "built_at": "2026-09-22T12:35:42+00:00"}
  ],
  "problems": []
}

status is ok, empty, stale (the index is behind a datasource's latest schema snapshot, or was built with another embedding model) or missing; problems says what is wrong and how to fix it.

docs.title: LLM API
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/llm.py

docs.title: PUT /api/v1/settings/llm
docs.text:
Replaces the engine's whole llm section in the running process, through engine.llm.replace (see LLM API → llm.replace).

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Request body: the llm section as JSON, the same shape as llm.yaml (see LLM configuration).

{
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-5.4",
  "api_key": "${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}",
  "agents": {"ast_planner": {"model": "gpt-5.5"}}
}

Execution flow: - The body is checked exactly as llm.yaml is: strict keys with "did you mean", the section's validators, and the providers resolved through the engine's registry. A ${provider:key} reference is kept in a secret field (api_key) and resolved by the engine's secret manager, so the body can name a variable or a secret rather than carry a key. A reference anywhere else is an error: the server's environment is never read into the config. - Every agent's API key must resolve. No model is called. - The new clients are built, then swapped in with engine.config.llm as one step. Questions already running finish on the old LLM. - The change is logged (one INFO line on nl2sql.llm) and audited, naming the caller's roles, via: "api", and each agent's old and new provider and model. Nothing is written to disk: a restart reads llm.yaml again.

Response (200): the change, never a key.

{
  "by": {"user_id": null, "roles": ["admin"], "via": "api"},
  "changes": {
    "default": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"},
    "ast_planner": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"}
  }
}

Errors: - No role -> HTTP 401; a role not in policies.admin_roles, or a remote client with no role source configured -> HTTP 403. - A section that is not valid, a provider that is not installed, or a key that does not resolve -> HTTP 422, whose detail is the config error's text. Nothing changes.

HTTP 422
{"detail": "LLM has 1 problem:\n\n  LLM → llm.agents.ast_planer\n    Unknown key. Did you mean 'ast_planner'?"}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm
docs.text: Response: {"llms": {...}}, engine.llm.list(): each agent by its name in the llm section (default first) with its provider, model, temperature and inherited (True when it sets nothing of its own). Never a key. No role needed.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm/{agent}
docs.text:
Response: one agent's entry, engine.llm.get(agent).

Errors: - An unknown agent -> HTTP 404, naming the agents.

docs.title: Request/Response Models
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/models/query.py

docs.title: QueryRequest
docs.text: field type required meaning natural_language str yes User query. datasource_id Optional[str] no Datasource override. execute bool no Execute SQL against datasource (default true). user_context Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no Ignored unless api.trust_body_role is true (local testing only); then an RBAC payload such as {"roles": ["admin"]}. See Caller role.

docs.title: SubQueryResponse
docs.text:
Derives from nl2sql.SubQueryResult, so it has exactly the engine's fields.

field type required meaning id str no Sub-query identifier. intent str no Semantic intent of the sub-query. sql str no SQL generated for the sub-query. datasource_id str no Datasource the sub-query targets. schema_version str no Schema version used for planning. plan Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no The validated plan, dumped. validation List[ValidationCheck] no Validation checks (name, passed, message). rows Optional[RowSample] no Capped row sample (columns, rows, total_rows). status str no "success" or "error" for this sub-query, from its final attempt: "success" when it ended with SQL and, if executed, a result; otherwise "error". A retry that recovers reports "success". retry_count int no Plan/SQL refinement attempts made. plan_source str no "cache" when the plan came from the plan cache (no planner call; still validated and executed), "verified" when a verified query answered (there is no plan; sql is the verified query's own, with its :name placeholders), otherwise "llm". row_cap Optional[int] no The row limit that bounded this sub-query's SQL, or null when the plan's own LIMIT was smaller. truncated bool no True when the result reached row_cap, so rows may be missing.

docs.title: QueryResponse
docs.text:
Derives from nl2sql.QueryResult (only sub_queries is narrowed to SubQueryResponse), so the HTTP response cannot drift from what the engine returns.

field type required meaning sub_queries List[SubQueryResponse] no One entry per decomposed sub-query, each with its SQL. final_answer Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no Answer synthesizer payload (summary, format_type, content, warnings, truncated). errors List[Dict[str, Any]] no Pipeline errors (node, message, error_code, severity, provider, provider_response). provider and provider_response are set for a PROVIDER_* code and null otherwise; see provider failures. trace_id str no Trace identifier. reasoning List[Dict[str, Any]] no Reasoning events/logs. warnings List[Dict[str, Any]] no Warning events/logs. artifact_refs Dict[str, ArtifactRef] no Result artifact references keyed by execution node id. status str no "success", "error" or "plan_only" for the run. timings Dict[str, float] no Wall-clock seconds per graph node. usage QuestionUsage no LLM calls, input/cached/output/reasoning tokens and model time per node (nodes) and for the question (total), plus every call (calls) and the number of plans served from the plan cache (plan_cache_hits). The same model as QueryResult.usage; see the core query API. trace_path Optional[str] no Where the run's trace file was written on the server, or null. See Debugging a Run. truncated bool no True when any sub-query's result was cut at its row limit. result_manifest List[ResultSummary] no The run's saved results, one per terminal DAG node: node_id, columns, row_count (the whole result's) and truncated (a sub-query feeding it was cut at its row limit). Never the rows: read those with the two result routes below, result_id being the node_id. Empty when nothing was saved (execute: false, or the run failed before aggregation). source AnswerSource no Where the answer came from: {"type": "verified", "id", "datasource_id", "params"} when a verified query from curated.yaml answered, with the values it ran with; {"type": "generated"} (the other fields null) otherwise. The last event of POST /query/stream carries it too.

Only a capped sample of the rows is inlined, in sub_queries[].rows. The full result set is written to artifact storage and addressed through artifact_refs (uri, format, row_count, columns). The run's combined results are listed in result_manifest and read back, a page at a time or as CSV, with GET /api/v1/query/{request_id}/results/{result_id} and .../{result_id}.csv.

docs.title: ResultPage
docs.text:
field type meaning request_id str The run's trace_id. result_id str The result's node_id from result_manifest. columns List[str] Column names, in row order. rows List[List[Any]] rows[i] is row offset + i of the result. offset int The first row returned, from 0. limit int The page size used, after the cap of 1,000. total_rows int Rows in the whole result. next_offset Optional[int] Where the next page starts, or null when this page reaches the end.

An errors[] entry for a key the provider rejected:

{
  "node": "datasource_resolver",
  "message": "OpenAI rejected the API key.",
  "error_code": "PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED",
  "severity": "ERROR",
  "provider": "OpenAI",
  "provider_response": "HTTP 401 (invalid_api_key): Incorrect API key provided: [redacted key]. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys."
}

Branch on error_code, show message, and keep provider_response for a "provider response" disclosure. The codes are listed under provider failures.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/query
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/query.py

Request model: QueryRequest

Response model: QueryResponse

Execution flow: - The get_user_context dependency supplies the caller's UserContext (see Caller role); with no role it answers HTTP 401 before the engine runs. - Delegates to engine.run_query(...), which returns a QueryResult. - Returns that QueryResult as a QueryResponse (its subclass); there is no field mapping.

The handler is declared with def, not async def: the pipeline performs blocking LLM and database calls, so Starlette runs it in its threadpool instead of on the event loop.

Errors: - Pipeline failures are a normal HTTP 200 carrying errors; they are not HTTP failures. - Genuinely unexpected failures return HTTP 500 with a generic detail; the traceback is logged server-side rather than returned to the client. - No role for the request returns HTTP 401 with a message naming the settings. - An invalid request body returns HTTP 422 (FastAPI validation).

Example response:

{
  "sub_queries": [
    {
      "id": "sq-1",
      "intent": "top customers by revenue",
      "sql": "SELECT s.customer, SUM(s.revenue) AS revenue FROM sales AS s GROUP BY s.customer ORDER BY SUM(s.revenue) DESC, s.customer LIMIT 5",
      "datasource_id": "warehouse",
      "schema_version": "v3",
      "plan": {"tables": [{"name": "sales", "alias": "s"}]},
      "validation": [
        {"name": "plan_present", "passed": true, "message": "Plan received from the planner"},
        {"name": "structure_and_schema", "passed": true, "message": "Tables, columns and joins resolve against the retrieved schema"},
        {"name": "policy", "passed": true, "message": "Role 'admin' may read every table in the plan"}
      ],
      "rows": {"columns": ["customer", "revenue"], "rows": [["acme", 42]], "total_rows": 5},
      "status": "success",
      "retry_count": 0,
      "plan_source": "llm",
      "row_cap": null,
      "truncated": false
    }
  ],
  "final_answer": {
    "summary": "Acme leads the top 5 customers by revenue, with 42.",
    "format_type": "text",
    "content": "Acme leads with 42. The full list of 5 customers is in the table.",
    "warnings": [],
    "truncated": false
  },
  "errors": [],
  "trace_id": "0f1c...",
  "reasoning": [],
  "warnings": [],
  "artifact_refs": {
    "sq-1": {
      "uri": "file:///artifacts/sq-1.parquet",
      "format": "parquet",
      "row_count": 5,
      "columns": ["customer", "revenue"]
    }
  },
  "status": "success",
  "source": {"type": "generated", "id": null, "datasource_id": null, "params": null},
  "timings": {"ast_planner": 0.02, "logical_validator": 0.001, "generator": 0.006, "executor": 0.038},
  "usage": {
    "total": {"calls": 3, "input_tokens": 13200, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "cache_write_input_tokens": 0,
              "output_tokens": 590, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 13790, "latency_s": 4.1, "cost": null},

                      "output_tokens": 300, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 11300, "latency_s": 2.2, "cost": null},
      "answer_synthesizer": {"calls": 1, "input_tokens": 300, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "cache_write_input_tokens": 0,
                             "output_tokens": 40, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 340, "latency_s": 0.6, "cost": null}
    },
    "calls": [
      {"node": "decomposer", "model": "gpt-4o-2024-08-06", "input_tokens": 1900, "cached_input_tokens": 0,
       "cache_write_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 250, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 2150,
