(Illustrative numbers. usage.calls is shortened to one entry; a real response lists all three.)

docs.title: POST /api/v1/query/stream
docs.text:
The same run as POST /api/v1/query, reported as it happens, as Server-Sent Events (Content-Type: text/event-stream). The request body, the caller role and the 401 are exactly those of /query. Delegates to engine.stream_query(...) (see the core query API).

Each event is an event: line naming its type and one data: line of JSON:

event data when node_started node A pipeline step began. The SQL agent's steps (ast_planner, logical_validator, generator, executor) come once per sub-query, and again on a retry. node_finished node, seconds, ok The step ended; ok is false when it raised. result_manifest trace_id, results The aggregator saved the run's results. results is the result_manifest the final response will carry, so a client can start paging the rows (with trace_id as request_id) before the answer is written. answer_delta field, text The next piece of the answer's summary or content, as the answer model writes it. Joined in order, the pieces of a field are that field of final_answer. final the QueryResponse The last event of a run that finished: exactly what /query returns for it. A refusal or a provider failure is a final with status: "error", as /query returns it. error message, error_code The last event of a run that could not finish (an unexpected failure; the traceback is logged on the server).

Every stream ends in exactly one final or one error.

event: node_started
data: {"node": "datasource_resolver"}

event: node_finished
data: {"node": "datasource_resolver", "seconds": 0.41, "ok": true}

...

event: result_manifest
data: {"trace_id": "0f1c...", "results": [{"node_id": "sq_1", "columns": ["customer", "revenue"], "row_count": 5, "truncated": false}]}

event: node_started
data: {"node": "answer_synthesizer"}

event: answer_delta
data: {"field": "summary", "text": "Acme leads "}

event: answer_delta
data: {"field": "summary", "text": "the top 5 customers"}

...

event: final
data: {"sub_queries": [...], "final_answer": {...}, "status": "success", ...}

curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/query/stream \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-NL2SQL-Role: admin" \
  -d '{"natural_language": "Who are the top 5 customers by revenue?"}'

What streams token by token: only the answer. The answer model is asked to stream on this route (and on this route only; /query is unchanged), on both wires: OpenAI's (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) streams the answer's tool call as argument pieces, Anthropic's as input_json_delta pieces, and the engine reads summary and content out of them as they grow. How finely the text arrives is the provider's choice: a provider or a local server that sends the whole answer in one piece gives one answer_delta per field. The other model steps (resolver, decomposer, planner, refiner) return a typed object the next step needs whole, so they are not streamed; their progress is their node_started and node_finished. A streamed answer reports the same token usage as an unstreamed one (stream_options.include_usage is sent on the OpenAI wire).

The route answers Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no, so a proxy passes each event on as it comes. Closing the connection cancels the run before its next step or model call.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/query/{request_id}/results/{result_id}
docs.text:
One page of a run's saved result.

parameter in default meaning request_id path The run's trace_id. result_id path A node_id from the run's result_manifest. offset query 0 First row, from 0. Negative is HTTP 422. limit query 100 Rows per page, at least 1 (else HTTP 422). Above 1,000 it is cut to 1,000; limit in the response says which.

Response model: ResultPage. Delegates to engine.results.page(...), which reads the rows lazily from the result's parquet artifact: only the slice asked for is read. A page past the end has no rows.

curl -H "X-NL2SQL-Role: admin"   "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/query/0f1c.../results/combine_g1?offset=100&limit=100"

{"request_id": "0f1c...", "result_id": "combine_g1", "columns": ["customer", "revenue"],
 "rows": [["acme", 42], ["globex", 40]], "offset": 100, "limit": 100,
 "total_rows": 102, "next_offset": null}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/query/{request_id}/results/{result_id}.csv
docs.text: The whole of a run's saved result as text/csv (UTF-8, header first), sent as an attachment named <request_id>_<result_id>.csv. Delegates to engine.results.csv(...), which reads the parquet artifact a slice at a time and streams each slice out, so the result is never built in memory on the server.

docs.title: Errors and scope of the result routes
docs.text:
• Both need a role, as /query does: no role is HTTP 401.
  • Results are read from the engine's own tenant folder (TENANT_ID, the <tenant_id> of the artifact path) and nowhere else. An unknown request_id, a run of another tenant, a result_id the run's manifest does not list, and an id that is not a plain token (letters, digits, _ and -, so no /, . or ..) are all HTTP 404, so a caller cannot tell one from the other or reach a path outside the run's folder.
  • There is no access control beyond that yet: any caller with a role who knows a run's trace_id can read its result.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
packages/api/tests/test_query_results_routes.py covers the result routes over the real facade and a local artifact store: paging, the cap, HTTP 422 for a bad offset or limit, the complete CSV, HTTP 404 for unknown, foreign and crafted ids, and HTTP 401 without a role.

packages/api/tests/test_query_routes.py and packages/api/tests/test_query_response_shape.py cover this endpoint with FastAPI's TestClient and a stubbed engine (get_engine dependency override) and a stubbed caller (get_user_context override, role admin), so no datasource, LLM or network access is required. packages/api/tests/test_auth.py covers the role sources and the 401.

packages/api/tests/test_query_stream_route.py covers the stream route the same way: the content type, the events in order, a final equal to the /query response, the 401 and the error event. packages/nl2sql/tests/e2e/test_stream_fake_llm.py streams a question on the demo databases through this route with no key.

docs.title: Configuration v2 and the extension registry (Phase 1 design)
docs.text:
Status: built

This page is the design for Phase 1 of the redesign, which ships as release 0.5. Every pull request in the PR plan is built, and each added a "Built" note to the sections it built and updated the reference pages it touched. PR 13 completes Phase 1. The Configuration pages describe the 0.5 config.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
There are no users yet, so nothing we change can break anyone. This design aims to be correct, not compatible:

  • No compatibility code. There are no old names, aliases, shims, deprecation warnings or legacy code paths kept for compatibility. 0.5 reads only the new config. There is no nl2sql config migrate command, only a mapping table in the docs.
  • The right shape, not the smallest diff. Where today's shape is wrong, this page gives the right one and deletes the old. That covers the facade, the settings global, the config models, the CLI flags, the internals the playground and the API reach into, and the names of methods, fields and environment variables.
  • No over-engineering. Ship only what the product needs in 0.5. Anything that can wait for a later phase does.
  • Per-engine config, passed explicitly. The fresh review suggested building today's process-global settings from the new config and leaving the 43 modules that read it alone. That was a compromise to keep the change small. Judged on correctness, the right design is an engine that owns its config and passes it down, with no process-global settings, so two engines in one process never share anything. Phase 1 gets there in staged pull requests, and each one stays green.

docs.title: Owner decisions
docs.text:
The owner answered the six questions this design left open. Each one is written into the section it affects:

# Decision Where 1 nl2sql-api settings go in an api: section of nl2sql.yaml, typed by an Api model. The engine ignores it, and nl2sql-api reads engine.config.api. The NL2SQL_API_* variables are removed. api 2 Only the entry points load .env. The CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo load the .env next to nl2sql.yaml without overriding variables that are already set. The library never reads .env and never writes os.environ. Environment variables 3 The constructor never connects. The entry points call engine.check(), and required: true is enforced there. Lifecycle 4 The S3 and ADLS result backends are deleted now. The Phase 2 results-store interface brings remote stores back. storage 5 nl2sql setup is removed in 0.5. nl2sql init replaces it, and the guided flow comes in Phase 4. CLI 6 The LLM can be replaced at runtime. engine.llm.replace(LLM(...)) and an admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm do it. The swap is atomic and logged, LLM clients are cached per engine, and the plan cache key includes the planner's model. Replacing the LLM at runtime

Two rules from earlier decisions apply throughout:

  • Every component works the same way: a small interface, the built-ins we ship, plugin packages people install, and their own code registered in memory.
  • The engine is the product. The CLI, nl2sql-api and the playground are consumers. Anything one of them needs that another caller could also need becomes an engine method.

docs.title: What ships in 0.5
docs.text: Goal What it means One typed config nl2sql.yaml and its split files build one Config object. Building it in code gives exactly the same object. A short list of environment variables Only NL2SQL_CONFIG, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL and the provider key variables are read directly. Everything else is written in the YAML, as ${env:VAR} where it should come from the environment. A registry, as a value Registry.default() maps names to code for adapters, LLM providers, embeddings providers and secret providers. Plugins add names through entry points, and your own code adds them with add_* or a decorator. A defined loading order Discover names, eagerly load and validate what the config uses, connect lazily, and report readiness with engine.check(). A light import import nl2sql loads no database driver, chromadb, onnxruntime, textual or opentelemetry. A test enforces this. A clean facade run_query and stream_query at the top level, and everything else in noun namespaces. engine.context, the duplicate methods and the sub-API classes are removed. A runtime LLM switch engine.llm.replace() and PUT /api/v1/settings/llm swap the LLM atomically and log who changed what. LLM clients are cached per engine. No process globals Settings, the embeddings cache and the secret manager belong to one engine, and nothing writes os.environ. Two engines can run in one process. The SDK renamed nl2sql-adapter-sdk becomes nl2sql-sdk (nl2sql_sdk). It holds the adapter and secrets interfaces. CLI on one flag A single --config, plus nl2sql init and nl2sql config check.

docs.title: Later phases
docs.text: Later Phase Typed connection models per adapter, IndexScope, test_connection stages, the public SQLAlchemy base, the conformance kit 2 (SDK v2) openai_compatible and azure_openai providers, structured-output fallback, the price table owned by llm/ 2 storage.index, storage.state, storage.traces, storage.results and their store interfaces (nl2sql.stores), pgvector and Postgres state 2 Policies with allow/deny globs, deny_columns, one Scope object, and the PolicyCheck interface (nl2sql.policy_checks) 2 The event bus, hooks and observers (nl2sql.hooks, nl2sql.observers), OpenTelemetry as an optional extra 3 Evals as a product (engine.evals, evals.yaml, scorers via nl2sql.scorers) 3 The guided setup flow (connect, scan, draft, review), Connect a database in both apps, the web app served by nl2sql-api, the replay provider, the Textual app 4 glossary.yaml and knowledge sources (nl2sql.knowledge_sources), routing signals 5

docs.title: 2. The config files
docs.text:
Built: the models and load_config (PR 2)

The models, load_config, ConfigError, load_env_file and the nl2sql.testing.config.make_config test helper are in nl2sql.config. The engine is built from them since PR 7a, and they are exported from nl2sql. Since PR 7b the Configuration pages are the reference. Building them settled these details:

  • In Settings, the schema group is the attribute schema_ in Python, because schema would shadow a pydantic method. The YAML key is schema.
  • Policies.allow_all() (the shorthand) and the allow_all field share a name: the shorthand answers on the class, the field on an instance. default_role must name one of the roles.
  • A secret provider's own keys (everything but id and type) keep their references, like a datasource's connection, until the provider's config_model (PR 4) says which of them are secrets.
  • Outside secret fields and connection, only ${env:...} resolves at load. Another provider's reference there is an error that names the field.
  • datasources is required in code as well as in the file; [] is enough.

docs.title: The table of contents
docs.text:
nl2sql.yaml is short. nl2sql init writes it with each section in its own file:

# nl2sql.yaml
version: 2
datasources: { file: datasources/ }      # a folder, one file per datasource
llm:         { file: llm.yaml }
embeddings:  { file: embeddings.yaml }
policies:    { file: policies.yaml }
storage:     { file: storage.yaml }
curated:     { file: curated.yaml }      # optional
secrets:     { file: secrets.yaml }      # optional
settings:    { file: settings.yaml }     # optional
api:         { file: api.yaml }          # optional, read by nl2sql-api only

A small project can write every section inline instead. This file builds the same Config as the split layout above:

version: 2
datasources:
  - id: shop
    type: sqlite
    connection: { database: shop.db }
llm:        { provider: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
embeddings: { provider: local }
policies:   { allow_all: true }
storage:    { path: .nl2sql }
Section Required Pydantic class Notes version yes Literal[2] Anything else, or a missing version, is an error that links to the mapping table. datasources yes list[Datasource] May be an empty list. The apps add datasources at runtime. llm yes LLM Flat: the keys are the LLM fields. embeddings yes Embeddings {provider: local} is a complete section. policies yes Policies {allow_all: true} is a complete section. storage yes Storage {path: .nl2sql} is a complete section. curated no Curated Absent means curated answers are off. secrets no Secrets The env provider is always available without it. settings no Settings Tuning knobs. Every field has a default. api no Api nl2sql-api's own settings. The engine validates it and never reads it.

The five required sections are explicit choices. There is no hidden default for where data lives, which embedder runs, or who may read what. Each one fits on one line, and nl2sql init writes all five.

glossary and evals are not Phase 1 sections. The root model forbids unknown keys, so writing one in 0.5 is an error.

docs.title: file: includes
docs.text:
Rule Detail Shape A section is either inline, or exactly {file: <path>} with no other keys. Relative paths The path is relative to nl2sql.yaml, not to the working directory. One level Only nl2sql.yaml may include. An included file holds the section's body and cannot include anything itself, so there are no chains and no cycles. No version Only nl2sql.yaml has version:. Datasource folder datasources: {file: datasources/} names a folder. Every *.yaml in it, sorted by name and not recursive, holds one datasource. id may be left out and defaults to the file name without .yaml. If it is given, it must equal the file name, so the owner of sales.yaml owns the sales datasource. Datasource file datasources: {file: datasources.yaml} names a file whose body is the list. No interpolation in paths file: values are literal. ${...} there is an error. Each file once Including the same file twice is an error.

Each team can then own its own database's file:

# datasources/sales.yaml   (id defaults to "sales")
type: postgres
description: Orders, customers and revenue for the EU shop.
connection:
  host: db.internal
  database: sales
  user: nl2sql
  password: "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}"
limits: { row_limit: 1000, timeout_ms: 8000 }
preferred_tables: [public.revenue_daily]
domains: [revenue, customers, orders]
sample_questions:
  - What was revenue by region last quarter?
  - Which customers placed the most orders this year?

docs.title: ${provider:key} interpolation
docs.text:
The grammar is today's: ${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}, ${vault:db/sales#password}. The first part is a secret provider's id. env is built in and always available.

Rule Detail Whole value only A reference is the entire string. "postgres://${env:U}@db" is an error. There is no default syntax (${env:X:-y}). Secrets resolve late Fields of type Secret (every api_key, the secret providers' credentials) and every value under a datasource's connection hold the reference, not the value. They are resolved when the component is built, so engine.config, logs and errors never contain a plaintext secret. A value written literally (or given in code, as the demo gives its key) stays a plain str the engine reads, and repr/str print it as **********: a Secret field always, and under connection or a secret provider's settings, a key whose name contains password, secret, token or api_key. A reference prints as written. A validation error never echoes its input (hide_input_in_errors). Everything else resolves at load Any other field, for example storage.path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}", is resolved by load_config. A missing variable is a load error that names the field. Inside secrets: Only ${env:...} is allowed, because one provider cannot depend on another.

docs.title: Strict keys and "did you mean"
docs.text: Every model sets extra="forbid" and frozen=True. An unknown key is an error, and it suggests the closest known key (difflib.get_close_matches, cutoff 0.6). The same applies to names the registry resolves (type:, provider:), where the suggestion comes from the installed names.

docs.title: Error messages
docs.text:
load_config and NL2SQL(...) collect every problem before raising one ConfigError. They do not stop at the first one.

nl2sql.yaml has 3 problems:

  datasources/sales.yaml → preferd_tables
    Unknown key. Did you mean 'preferred_tables'?

  llm.yaml → provider
    'antropic' is not an installed LLM provider. Did you mean 'anthropic'?
    Installed: anthropic, ollama, openai, openrouter.

  datasources/sales.yaml → type: postgres
    The postgres adapter needs the module 'psycopg2', which is not installed.
    Fix: pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]"

The rules: - Each problem gives the file, then the path inside it (file → a.b[2].c). - What is wrong is said in one sentence, followed by a Fix: line when the fix is known. - A secret is shown as its reference (${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}), never as its value. - A 0.4 file gets one specific message: "configs/datasources.yaml is a 0.4 config file (version: 1). 0.5 reads nl2sql.yaml: see architecture/configuration_v2."

docs.title: The sections
docs.text: All classes live in nl2sql.config and are exported from nl2sql. Field names are the YAML keys.

docs.title: datasources: Datasource
docs.text:
Field Type Default Was (0.4) id str the file name in a folder, otherwise required id type str required, unless adapter is given connection.type description str \| None None description connection dict[str, Any] {} connection without type. It is validated by the adapter. Typed models per adapter arrive in Phase 2. limits Limits Limits() options.row_limit, options.statement_timeout_ms, options.max_bytes and the top-level fold preferred_tables list[str] [] preferred_tables sample_questions list[str] [] sample_questions.yaml, keyed by datasource domains list[str] [] new: a routing hint written by people. The domains generated at indexing are separate and stored with the index. Routing does not read it yet (a later phase). required bool False new: engine.check() fails if this datasource cannot connect adapter adapter object None new: pass a built adapter instead of type (code only)

Limits has row_limit: int | None, timeout_ms: int | None and max_bytes: int | None. The options: bag and the rule that "the lower of the two wins" are removed, so there is one place to set each limit.

docs.title: llm: LLM (flat)
docs.text:
# llm.yaml
provider: anthropic
model: claude-sonnet-5-5
temperature: 0
# api_key is optional: without it the provider's standard variable
# (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) is read. Write it to use another name:
# api_key: "${env:TEAM_ANTHROPIC_KEY}"
agents:
  ast_planner:         { model: claude-opus-5-5 }
  answer_synthesizer:  { provider: openai, model: gpt-5.4 }
  indexing_enrichment: { model: claude-haiku-5 }
prices:
  my-finetune: { input: 0.2, cached_input: 0.1, output: 0.6 }
Field Type Default Was (0.4) provider str \| None required, unless model is an object default.provider model str \| BaseChatModel required default.model temperature float \| None 0.0 default.temperature (null still means "send none") api_key Secret \| None None, which means the preset variable default.api_key base_url str \| None None default.base_url agents dict[AgentName, AgentLLM] {} agents prices dict[str, Price] {} LLM_PRICES (JSON in an env var)

AgentLLM has the same five fields as the top level (provider, model, temperature, api_key, base_url), all optional. An agent takes each field it sets and inherits the rest. Inheritance is decided by which fields were set (model_fields_set), so temperature: null on an agent still means "send none". AgentName is a closed set of the node names: curated_matcher, datasource_resolver, decomposer, ast_planner, refiner, answer_synthesizer and indexing_enrichment. The concatenated 0.4 keys (astplanner, answersynthesizer) and the name: field are gone, along with the LLM_AGENTS mapping between the two spellings. Price has input, output, and optionally cached_input and cache_write, as LLM_PRICES does today.

docs.title: embeddings: Embeddings
docs.text: Field Type Default Was (0.4) provider str \| None required, unless instance is given EMBEDDING_PROVIDER (default was openai) model str \| None the provider's default EMBEDDING_MODEL api_key Secret \| None the provider's standard variable OPENAI_API_KEY via Settings instance LangChain Embeddings object None new (code only)

docs.title: policies: Policies
docs.text:
The semantics are today's, written in YAML instead of JSON. allow_all, default_role and admin_roles are the small additions that the one-line section and the move of NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES need.

# policies.yaml
default_role: viewer
admin_roles: [admin]
refusal_names_tables: false
roles:
  admin:
    description: Every table in every database
    allowed_datasources: ["*"]
    allowed_tables: ["*"]
  analyst:
    description: Sales, except the audit schema
    allowed_datasources: [sales]
    allowed_tables: ["sales.public.*"]
Field Type Default Was (0.4) allow_all bool False new: every caller may read everything (local and dev use). It cannot be combined with default_role or roles. default_role str \| None None new: the role used when the entry point gives none. Without it, no role means a refusal, as today. admin_roles list[str] ["admin"] NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES refusal_names_tables bool False RBAC_REFUSAL_NAMES_TABLES roles dict[str, Role] {} roles in policies.json

Role has description, allowed_datasources and allowed_tables, with today's meaning and pattern rules. The redundant role: field, which repeated the key, is removed. Policies.allow_all() is the code shorthand. The allow/deny globs replace these names in Phase 2, once rather than twice.

docs.title: storage: Storage (path only)
docs.text:
# storage.yaml
path: .nl2sql          # or "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}" in Docker
Field Type Default path Path required. Relative to nl2sql.yaml in a file, and to the working directory in code.

Today's stores move under it:

Store 0.4 location and variable 0.5 location Vector index (chroma) ./chroma_db (VECTOR_STORE), collection nl2sql_store (VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION) <path>/index/. The collection name becomes an internal constant. Schema snapshots, plan cache, feedback data/schema_store.db (SCHEMA_STORE_PATH) <path>/state.db Run traces traces/ (TRACE_DIR) <path>/traces/ Result files ./artifacts (RESULT_ARTIFACT_BASE_URI) <path>/results/

The S3 and ADLS result backends (RESULT_ARTIFACT_BACKEND=s3|adls and their settings) are deleted in 0.5 (owner decision 4). They were untested and unreachable from the new config. The Phase 2 results-store interface brings remote stores back as built-ins or plugins.

In Phase 2, index, state, traces and results become optional sub-blocks, each with a type. A config with only path stays valid.

docs.title: secrets: Secrets
docs.text:
# secrets.yaml
providers:
  - id: vault
    type: hashicorp
    url: https://vault.internal:8200
    token: "${env:VAULT_TOKEN}"

providers: list[SecretProviderConfig]. type is resolved through the registry (env, aws, azure and hashicorp are built in; 0.4's hashi is renamed), and each provider validates its own block with its config_model. The id env is reserved. A provider that fails to configure fails startup and names secrets.providers[i], instead of being logged and swallowed (bug B10). The fallbacks to VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN and AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL are removed: write the field, with ${env:...} if the value comes from the environment.

docs.title: curated: Curated
docs.text: The body is today's curated.yaml without version: datasources: {<id>: {verified_queries: [...], metrics: [...]}}. If the section is present, curated answers are on. If it is absent, they are off. That replaces CURATED_ENABLED, and the eval tier that runs without curated answers builds its engine from cfg.model_copy(update={"curated": None}).

docs.title: settings: Settings
docs.text:
These are the tuning knobs that were environment variables. Every field has a default, so the section is optional.

# settings.yaml (every value shown is the default)
tenant_id: default_tenant
pipeline:
  timeout_s: 60
  plan_cache: true
  strict_columns: true
  today: null                 # pin the run date: 2013-12-31
  retries: { max: 3, base_delay_s: 1.0, max_delay_s: 10.0, jitter_s: 0.5 }
retrieval:
  full_snapshot_max_tables: 15
results:
  row_limit: 100000
  fetch_batch_size: 10000
  preview_rows: 20
traces:
  mode: on_failure            # off | on_failure | always
  sample_rows: 50
  max_field_chars: 20000
schema:
  max_versions: 3
  version_mismatch: warn      # warn | fail | ignore
curated:
  match_top_k: 5
  match_floor: 0.6
feedback:
  enabled: true
observability:
  exporter: none              # none | console | otlp
  otlp_endpoint: null

Each group is its own frozen model (PipelineSettings, RetrySettings, RetrievalSettings, ResultSettings, TraceSettings, SchemaSettings, CuratedSettings, FeedbackSettings, ObservabilitySettings), with today's validation (for example match_floor between 0 and 1).

docs.title: api: Api
docs.text:
These are nl2sql-api's own settings (owner decision 1). The class lives in nl2sql.config, so the file gets the same strict validation, ${env:} rules and nl2sql config check as every other section. The engine never reads it, and nl2sql-api reads engine.config.api. Without the section, nl2sql-api uses the defaults: no role source, so admin routes answer on loopback only, as today.

# api.yaml
role_header: X-NL2SQL-Role      # a header a trusted proxy sets on every request
role: null                      # or one static role for every request
trust_body_role: false          # accept "role" in the request body (dev only)
cors_origins: [https://app.example.com]
Field Type Default Was (0.4) role_header str \| None None NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER role str \| None None NL2SQL_API_ROLE trust_body_role bool False NL2SQL_API_TRUST_BODY_ROLE cors_origins list[str] [] NL2SQL_API_CORS_ORIGINS (comma-separated)

The admin role list is a policy, so it lives in policies.admin_roles, not here.

docs.title: Frozen, except datasources and the LLM
docs.text:
Config and every section are frozen. Code changes a config by copying it:

cfg = load_config("nl2sql.yaml")
cfg = cfg.with_datasource(Datasource(id="shop", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "shop.db"}))
cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"settings": cfg.settings.model_copy(update={"tenant_id": "acme"})})

Once an engine is built, two sections can still change: - datasources, through engine.datasources.add() and remove(); - llm, through engine.llm.replace() (see Replacing the LLM at runtime).

Each call swaps in a new Config atomically, under a lock, so engine.config always matches what the engine runs. Nothing is written to disk. A restart returns to the files, and persisting a change is the calling app's job. Every other section is fixed for the engine's lifetime.

docs.title: The allow-list
docs.text:
Variable Read by Purpose NL2SQL_CONFIG nl2sql.config (load_config with no path) Path to nl2sql.yaml. Without it, ./nl2sql.yaml. NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL configure_logging() The log level when the caller passes none. OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY nl2sql/llm/ only, through PROVIDER_PRESETS Fallback when llm.api_key (or an agent's, or embeddings.api_key) is not set.

Anything else from the environment is written explicitly in the YAML: path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}". There are no generic NL2SQL__SECTION__KEY overrides. Two other kinds of reads stay because they are not configuration: the trace redactor scans os.environ for values to mask, and nl2sql benchmark checks CI. Third-party libraries such as boto3 and the OpenTelemetry SDK still read their own standard variables.

Built: the allow-list (PR 13)

test_environment_reads_only_from_the_allow_list in tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py names each module allowed to read os.environ and why (READS_THE_ENVIRONMENT): nl2sql/config/ (NL2SQL_CONFIG and ${env:...}), nl2sql/llm/ (the provider keys), the env secret provider, common/logger.py (configure_logging reads NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL when the caller passes no level, which the CLI and nl2sql-api no longer do), the trace redactor and nl2sql benchmark (CI). The CLI's demo command and the playground's settings panel ask nl2sql.llm.providers.api_key_from_env for a provider's key. NL2SQL_TODAY, ENV, APP_ENV and ENV_FILE_PATH went with common/settings.py; the first is settings.pipeline.today.

docs.title: .env files
docs.text:
Built (PR 7b, PR 13)

test_only_entry_points_load_dotenv allows load_dotenv only in nl2sql/config/loader.py (load_env_file), and load_env_file only in cli/main.py, cli/commands/demo.py and nl2sql_api/main.py. Every entry point loads the .env before configure_logging(), so a NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL there applies: nl2sql-api in its lifespan, the CLI in its global callback (once --config is known), and nl2sql demo again after it loads the demo project's .env.

Only the entry points load .env (owner decision 2): - The CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo load the .env next to nl2sql.yaml into the process environment at startup. - Variables that are already set win. The file never overrides them. - The library never reads a .env file and never writes os.environ. A Python caller who wants a .env calls python-dotenv before NL2SQL.from_config().

This replaces 0.4's three ways in: pydantic-settings reading .env, the ENV/APP_ENV lookup of .env.<name>, and ENV_FILE_PATH. Loading lives in one helper, nl2sql.config.load_env_file(config_path). Only the entry points call it, and the boundary test allows load_dotenv there and nowhere else.

constant) LLM_CONFIG llm: in nl2sql.yaml DATASOURCE_CONFIG datasources: in nl2sql.yaml SECRETS_CONFIG secrets: in nl2sql.yaml EMBEDDING_MODEL embeddings.model EMBEDDING_PROVIDER embeddings.provider The entry points load the .env next to nl2sql.yaml (.env files). NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES nl2sql_api/auth.py policies.admin_roles NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER, NL2SQL_API_ROLE, NL2SQL_API_TRUST_BODY_ROLE, NL2SQL_API_CORS_ORIGINS nl2sql_api/auth.py, main.py api.role_header, api.role, api.trust_body_role, api.cors_origins NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED cli/demo/playground/hosted.py nl2sql demo --hosted (the flag already exists) NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_PER_MINUTE, NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_PER_SESSION hosted.py nl2sql demo --questions-per-minute N --questions-per-session N VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN secrets/providers/hashi.py secrets.providers[].url / .token AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL secrets/providers/azure.py secrets.providers[].vault_url CURATED_CONFIG (second read) cli/commands/curated.py removed OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY llm/registry.py, indexing/embeddings.py, the demo and doctor commands kept, read in nl2sql/llm/ only. indexing/embeddings.py stops reading the variable itself. CI cli/commands/benchmark.py kept: CI detection, not configuration

docs.title: 4. Creating the engine
docs.text:
Built: the runtime from Config (PR 7a)

NL2SQL(config, *, registry=None), NL2SQL.from_config(), NL2SQL.demo(), check(), close() and the context manager are built. Runtime.from_config(cfg, registry) (nl2sql/runtime.py) replaces NL2SQLContext and nl2sql/context.py; CheckReport, DatasourceStatus and EngineNotReady are in nl2sql/check.py. Config, load_config and the section classes are exported lazily from nl2sql. Building it settled these details:

  • What fails where. Everything that can be known without a connection is one ConfigError from the constructor: an unknown or uninstalled name, a secret provider that cannot start (bug B10), an adapter that rejects its connection settings or a reference that does not resolve, an embeddings provider without its key, and curated answers that do not match the datasources. A datasource that cannot connect is check()'s: failed at stage connect. test_connection() returns a bool, so the reason is generic until the SDK v2 stages (Phase 2). A problem names nl2sql.yaml (or Config when built in code) and the path inside the config (datasources[1].type); which split file a section came from is not tracked yet.
  • Relative files. load_config records the folder of nl2sql.yaml as Config.folder (a private attribute that copies keep and equality ignores). The engine passes it to every adapter as base_dir, and the SQLite and DuckDB adapters read a relative database from there (BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter.local_path). The adapters' connection models no longer have a type field: type is on the Datasource.
  • One secret provider shape. SecretProviderConfig is the one in nl2sql.config (id, type and the provider's own keys, kept as written). The provider's config_model validates the block when the engine builds the provider, after resolving its ${env:...} values. nl2sql/secrets/models.py and the module-level secret_manager are deleted; each engine builds its own SecretManager(registry).
  • Per engine. The embedder is built once from embeddings through the registry, or is the instance given; EmbeddingService is deleted. The LLM is the engine's LLMSet, built from the llm section through its LLMClientCache (PR 9, Replacing the LLM at runtime). Policies.allow_all and default_role are applied by RBAC.
  • Stores. The index is <storage.path>/index/ (collection nl2sql_store, a constant), the schema store <storage.path>/state.db, traces <storage.path>/traces/ and results <storage.path>/results/. The S3 and ADLS result backends and their settings are deleted.
  • Datasources. engine.add_datasource(Datasource) (since 10a engine.datasources.add) builds the adapter (not connected) and swaps in a new engine.config under the engine's lock. Indexing reads a datasource's description and sample questions from its Datasource, so one added in code keeps both (bug B9).
  • The 0.4 entry points (nl2sql._legacy, NL2SQL._legacy()) lived for one PR; PR 7b deleted them with the 0.4 files.
  • Tests. nl2sql.testing.config.make_demo_config(folder) is make_config with the demo's databases and roles; the integration and end-to-end fixtures build their runtime from it.

Every way builds the same Config. Names in it are resolved through a Registry, and the default registry is used when none is passed.

1. From the file. This is the common case.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")   # path=None → NL2SQL_CONFIG → ./nl2sql.yaml

2. From the file, with your own components.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Registry
from nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemyAdapter   # Phase 2; in 0.5, any class implementing the adapter protocol

registry = Registry.default()

@registry.adapter("snowflake")
class SnowflakeAdapter(SQLAlchemyAdapter): ...

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml", registry=registry)   # YAML can now say type: snowflake

3. In code, by name.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Config, Datasource, LLM, Embeddings, Policies, Storage

engine = NL2SQL(Config(
    datasources=[Datasource(id="sales", type="postgres",
                            connection={"host": "db", "database": "sales", "user": "nl2sql",
                                        "password": "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}"})],
    llm=LLM(provider="anthropic", model="claude-sonnet-5-5"),
    embeddings=Embeddings(provider="local"),
    policies=Policies.allow_all(),
    storage=Storage(path=".nl2sql"),
))

4. In code, passing objects. This needs no names and no registry.

engine = NL2SQL(Config(
    datasources=[Datasource(id="dw", adapter=SnowflakeAdapter(...))],
    llm=LLM(model=ChatOpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", model="qwen3")),
    embeddings=Embeddings(instance=MyEmbeddings()),
    policies=Policies.allow_all(),
    storage=Storage(path=".nl2sql"),
))

Policies(check=...) and Storage(index=...) objects arrive with their interfaces in Phase 2.

5. Mixed: load the file, then change it in code.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, load_config, Datasource

cfg = load_config("nl2sql.yaml")
cfg = cfg.with_datasource(Datasource(id="shop", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "shop.db"}))
engine = NL2SQL(cfg)

6. The demo, ready-made.

engine = NL2SQL.demo()                                   # bundled sample databases
engine = NL2SQL.demo(llm=LLM(provider="openai", model="gpt-5.4"), path=".nl2sql-demo")

NL2SQL.demo() builds the demo Config in code. The datasources are the three bundled SQLite files, opened read-only from the installed package, along with the demo policies (admin, analyst, viewer) and the demo curated file. storage.path defaults to ./.nl2sql-demo. Without llm, it uses the first provider whose key variable is set, and raises an error naming the variables when none is. nl2sql demo passes its own LLM (for example one pointed at the local replay server).

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
with NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml") as engine:
    report = engine.check()
    if not report.ok:
        print(report)          # per-datasource stage and fix, LLM keys, index status
    result = engine.run_query("Top 5 customers by revenue")
# close() ran: pools disposed, stores closed
Method What it does NL2SQL(config, *, registry=None) Loads and validates: resolves every name, imports only those components, checks interface versions and driver modules, builds the secret manager, adapters (not connected), LLM clients (no call) and stores. Raises one ConfigError with every problem. It never connects to a datasource or calls a model (owner decision 3). NL2SQL.from_config(path=None, *, registry=None) NL2SQL(load_config(path), registry=registry). engine.check() -> CheckReport Connects to each datasource and records ready or failed(stage, reason, fix). A failed datasource is marked unavailable and left out of routing. It also checks that every agent's API key resolves (no model call) and reports the index status (index.health()). It raises EngineNotReady if a required: true datasource fails, or if datasources are configured and none is ready. It is safe to call again. engine.close() Disposes adapter pools and closes the state store and the vector store client. The engine cannot be used afterwards. Calling it twice is fine. __enter__ / __exit__ with support. __exit__ calls close(). engine.config The current frozen Config. Secrets appear as references only. It changes only through datasources.add/remove and llm.replace.

Startup policy belongs to the entry points. The CLI, nl2sql-api (in its lifespan, before it accepts requests) and the playground call engine.check() straight after construction. They refuse to start on EngineNotReady, and they start degraded, printing the report, when an optional datasource fails. A Python caller decides for itself. Without check(), a broken datasource fails the first query that targets it, with its reason. Building an engine therefore stays cheap and has no side effects for tests, nl2sql config check and notebooks.

docs.title: What can change after creation
docs.text:
Only two things, and each goes through one method:

engine.datasources.add(Datasource(id="hr", type="postgres", connection={...}))   # Connect a database
engine.datasources.remove("hr")
engine.llm.replace(LLM(provider="openai", model="gpt-5.4",
                       agents={"ast_planner": AgentLLM(model="gpt-5.5")}))      # switch models

docs.title: Replacing the LLM at runtime
docs.text:
Built: the LLM client cache and llm.replace (PR 9)

engine.llm.replace(llm, *, by=None, via="python") -> LLMChange is built (Runtime.replace_llm in nl2sql/runtime.py), with LLMSet and LLMChange in nl2sql/llm/llm_set.py and LLMClientCache in nl2sql/llm/client_cache.py. LLMRegistry is now the per-engine holder of the current set and the cache; the nodes still ask it for their client by name. Building it settled these details:

  • The entry point. replace takes via alongside by, so the entry point (python, api, playground) is known when there is no user. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm (PR 10a) replaced POST /llm and configure_llm.
  • Keys. replace fails with ConfigError when an agent's API key does not resolve (llm.api_key, llm.agents.<agent>.api_key). At construction a key that does not resolve is still check()'s to report, and using that agent raises the reason.
  • Clients are built up front, at construction and on replace, so the key is read then: a key set in the environment later is used only once the LLM is set again.
  • Reading the set once. run_with_graph pins the current set to the run (LLMRegistry.begin_run, a context variable read while the graph is built) and releases it when the graph finishes, which a timed-out run has not yet done. The trace records the run's set.
  • Closing. The built-in wires build ChatOpenAI and ChatAnthropic, which share their library's process-wide connection pool, so there is no HTTP client of their own to close: closing calls the client's close() when it has one (a provider registered in code), and is otherwise dropping the reference.
  • The plan cache key carries the planner as provider/model, the effective one for the run (a caller's per-request model included); a model object is Class/model.

Owner decision 6 keeps a runtime model switch. Changing the model by hand is something both the playground and an operator need.

The entry points

Caller How Python engine.llm.replace(llm: LLM, *, by: UserContext \| None = None) -> LLMChange nl2sql-api PUT /api/v1/settings/llm, admin only (require_admin). The body is the llm section as JSON, the same shape as llm.yaml. It replaces POST /llm. It returns the LLMChange with no keys. Playground The settings panel calls engine.llm.replace(...).

Validation. The new section is validated exactly like llm.yaml. The same LLM model runs with extra="forbid" and "did you mean", the provider names are resolved through the engine's registry (checking interface version and find_spec), and every agent's key reference is resolved. A request that fails changes nothing and returns the same ConfigError text, as HTTP 422 from the API. No model is called during validation.

The swap is atomic. - The runtime holds one immutable LLMSet, which maps each agent to its client and resolved settings. - replace builds the new LLMSet completely, then swaps one reference under the engine's lock, along with engine.config (llm is replaced, and nothing else changes). - A run reads the reference once, when it starts. In-flight runs finish on the old set, and every run that starts after the swap uses the new one. No run ever mixes the two.

It is not persisted. The file on disk is not rewritten, so a restart returns to llm.yaml. Saving the change explicitly is out of scope for 0.5. The playground already writes its own llm.yaml for the next start, and keeps doing so as a separate step after replace succeeds.

Every swap is logged. One INFO log line, and one audit record through the engine's event_logger. That stub becomes the audit observer, and the record becomes the llm.changed event, when the Phase 3 event bus lands. The record holds: - who: by.user_id and by.roles when known, otherwise the entry point (api, playground, python); - each agent whose effective provider or model changed, as old and new; - never a key, a key reference or a header value.

INFO nl2sql.llm: LLM replaced by user=u42 roles=[admin] via api:
  default: openai/gpt-5.4 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5;
  ast_planner: openai/gpt-5.4 -> anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

Clients are cached per engine. LLMClientCache is owned by the runtime and is not a global. It also serves initial construction. - The key is the agent's resolved client settings: provider, model, base_url, temperature, and every other client field the agent model has (Phase 2 adds max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries, seed and headers, and the key covers them automatically because it is built from the model's fields). - Secrets are resolved but never stored in the key. The resolved API key (and any secret header) enters the key only as a SHA-256 digest, and the key's string form, used in logs and debugging, prints the digest prefix only. - Sharing. Agents whose settings are equal share one client, so seven agents on one model build one client. Swapping back to an earlier LLM reuses the cached clients instead of building new ones. - Bounded. An LRU of 16 entries. A client evicted from the cache is closed (its HTTP client's close()) once no LLMSet refers to it any more, so an in-flight run on the old set is never cut off. engine.close() closes them all.

The plan cache key includes the planner's model. Today the key is the normalised intent and run date, the datasource and the schema version (pipeline/plan_cache.py). It gains the ast_planner agent's effective provider and model, so after a swap a plan written by another model is never served. Entries from the old model stay in the cache, and swapping back hits them again.

docs.title: 5. The registry
docs.text:
Built: the registry (PR 5)

nl2sql/registry.py holds Registry with default(), empty(), the add_* methods and decorators for the four Phase 1 kinds, names(), and load(kind, name), which imports a name and runs the load-time checks (interface version with the package name, find_spec with the install hint, duplicate entry points naming both packages, "did you mean"). It raises RegistryError; collecting those into a ConfigError is NL2SQL(cfg, registry)'s job, in PR 7a. The built-ins are declared in the four entry point groups. LLMProvider and ResolvedAgent live in nl2sql.llm.providers, EmbeddingsProvider in nl2sql.embeddings. discover_adapters() and nl2sql/secrets/factory.py are deleted: the DatasourceRegistry, the secret manager and nl2sql list-adapters use the registry. Since PR 7a the runtime resolves its LLM providers and builds its embedder through the registry it is given.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
A YAML file holds only text. When it says type: postgres or provider: anthropic, something has to turn that name into code. The Registry is that lookup table. It is a value that you pass to the engine, not a global, so two engines (or two tests) never see each other's registrations.

class Registry:
    @classmethod
    def default(cls) -> "Registry": ...   # built-ins + installed plugins: entry point names only, no imports
    @classmethod
    def empty(cls) -> "Registry": ...     # nothing; for tests and allow-lists

    # chosen kinds in Phase 1: one name per slot
    def add_adapter(self, name: str, cls: type, *, replace: bool = False) -> None: ...
    def add_llm(self, name: str, provider: LLMProvider, *, replace: bool = False) -> None: ...
    def add_embeddings(self, name: str, provider: EmbeddingsProvider, *, replace: bool = False) -> None: ...
    def add_secrets(self, name: str, cls: type, *, replace: bool = False) -> None: ...

    # the same, as decorators
    def adapter(self, name: str): ...
    def llm(self, name: str): ...
    def embeddings(self, name: str): ...
    def secrets(self, name: str): ...

    def names(self, kind: Kind) -> list[str]: ...   # for errors, `nl2sql list-adapters`, the apps
Rule Detail Names only default() lists entry points and imports none of them. A name is imported when an engine's config uses it. No hidden global default() builds a new value each call. Only the scan of installed entry points, which is plain data, may be cached. Clashes add_* with a name already present raises, unless replace=True. Two installed packages declaring the same name raise when that name is used, naming both packages. Objects skip the registry A Datasource(adapter=...), LLM(model=<object>) or Embeddings(instance=...) is used as given. Validation order load_config checks only shape: type is a string. Names are resolved by NL2SQL(...) and by nl2sql config check, against the registry passed in. That is why registering on your own registry before building the engine is enough.

docs.title: Interfaces and versions
docs.text:
Built: the two SDK interfaces

PR 4 built the adapter and secret provider rows below: the attributes on DatasourceAdapterProtocol and the five built-in adapters, and nl2sql_sdk.secrets.SecretProvider with the four built-in providers. A provider's config_model covers its block apart from id and type. PR 5 replaced the temporary nl2sql/secrets/factory.py table with the nl2sql.secrets entry point group.

Each Phase 1 interface carries interface_version: ClassVar[int]. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for, and anything else is a load error: "nl2sql-snowflake implements adapter interface 0; this engine needs 1". There are no minor versions and no window for old ones. Optional capabilities stay separate runtime_checkable protocols, as StreamingAdapterProtocol is today.

Interface Phase 1 shape Adapter (nl2sql_sdk) Today's DatasourceAdapterProtocol, plus interface_version = 1, driver_modules: tuple[str, ...] (checked with importlib.util.find_spec before construction) and install_hint: str. SDK v2 (Phase 2) raises it to 2. Secret provider (nl2sql_sdk) interface_version = 1, config_model: type[BaseModel] (its secrets.providers[] block, extra="forbid"), from_config(cfg) -> Self, get_secret(key) -> str \| None. It moves from nl2sql/secrets/interfaces.py. LLM provider (nl2sql.llm) interface_version = 1, label, api_key_env: str \| None, requires: tuple[str, ...], install_hint, and create(agent: ResolvedAgent) -> BaseChatModel. The four built-ins are made from PROVIDER_PRESETS, which stays the one table of key variables. Embeddings provider (nl2sql.embeddings) interface_version = 1, default_model, requires, install_hint, and create(cfg: Embeddings) -> Embeddings (LangChain).

docs.title: 6. Loading
docs.text:
Built: nl2sql config check (PR 8)

nl2sql.config.check.check_config(path, registry=, connect=) runs steps 1, 2a and 2b, and with connect step 3, and returns every problem, every secret as present or missing, and the datasource statuses; nl2sql config check [--connect] prints them by file. Building it settled these details:

  • Runtime.components(cfg, registry) is step 2b without the stores and without the process-global copy; Runtime.from_config is it plus the stores. So the check writes nothing under storage.path.
  • Config.locate(path) maps a path in the whole config (datasources[0].type) to the file it was read from (datasources/sales.yaml → type). The runtime's problems use it, so NL2SQL(...)'s ConfigError names included files as well.
  • Where llm names no api_key, the provider's standard variable is listed with the secrets. A missing LLM key is reported, not a problem, as in the constructor: check() reports it at startup.
  • With --connect, any datasource that fails is a problem, required or not. Exit codes: 0, 1 on a problem or a missing config, and 2 for a usage error (Typer's).
  • CI's integration job runs it with --connect on the init --demo config before indexing.
flowchart LR
  D["1. Discover<br/>Registry.default()<br/>entry point names only"] --> L["2. Load and validate<br/>load_config + NL2SQL(cfg)<br/>imports only what the config names"]
  L --> C["3. Connect lazily<br/>engine.check() at startup"]
  L -.-> K["CI: nl2sql config check<br/>steps 1 and 2, no engine"]
Step When What happens Fails with 1. Discover Registry.default() Lists entry point names in the four Phase 1 groups. Imports nothing and takes milliseconds. nothing 2a. Load load_config(path) Reads YAML, applies includes, resolves non-secret references, validates the models (extra="forbid", "did you mean"). Pure: no network, no database, no files written. ConfigError listing every problem 2b. Validate components NL2SQL(cfg, registry) For each name the config uses: imports it, checks interface_version, checks driver_modules/requires with find_spec (reporting install_hint if one is missing), and validates its own block (config_model). Builds the secret manager, adapters (not connected), LLM clients (no call), the embedder and the local stores under storage.path. ConfigError listing every problem, before any question is asked 3. Connect first use, and engine.check() Opens database connections. A datasource that fails is marked unavailable and the engine runs degraded, unless the datasource is required: true or none are ready. EngineNotReady from check(), or the datasource's reason on a query that targets it CI nl2sql config check Steps 1, 2a and 2b without creating any store files. --connect also runs step 3. Exit code 0 or 1. the same errors, printed by file

The CLI, nl2sql-api (in its lifespan) and the playground call engine.check() straight after building the engine, and enforce required there. The constructor never connects (owner decision 3).

docs.title: The import-time rule
docs.text:
import nl2sql must not import chromadb, onnxruntime, any database driver (sqlalchemy, psycopg2, psycopg, pymysql, pyodbc, pymssql, duckdb, duckdb_engine), textual or opentelemetry. load_config and Registry.default() must not either. Today import nl2sql loads chromadb, duckdb, opentelemetry, langgraph, langchain_openai and polars, and takes about 2 seconds warm.

How Phase 1 gets there: - nl2sql/__init__.py imports only nl2sql.config (pydantic models), nl2sql.registry and the NL2SQL class. Everything else that it exports (result types, QueryEvent, CancellationToken) goes through the module's __getattr__, which is the pattern it already uses for BenchmarkAPI. - The facade module imports the runtime inside NL2SQL.__init__, not at the top of the module. - The runtime modules import their heavy libraries where they are used, as the adapters already do.

How tests enforce it, in tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py, using the existing _run subprocess helper:

FORBIDDEN_AT_IMPORT = ("chromadb", "onnxruntime", "sqlalchemy", "psycopg2", "psycopg", "pymysql",
                       "pyodbc", "pymssql", "duckdb", "duckdb_engine", "textual", "opentelemetry")

@pytest.mark.parametrize("statement", ["import nl2sql",
                                       "from nl2sql import load_config, Registry; Registry.default()"])
def test_importing_nl2sql_loads_no_heavy_library(statement):
    loaded = _run(f"import sys; {statement}; "
                  f"print(sorted({{m.split('.')[0] for m in sys.modules}} & set({FORBIDDEN_AT_IMPORT!r})))")
    assert loaded == "[]", f"{statement} loaded {loaded}. The rule is in {RULES}."

def test_import_nl2sql_stays_within_its_time_budget():
    # cumulative microseconds for the top-level package, from -X importtime, best of 3
    assert best_of_three_import_us("nl2sql") < 500_000

The budget test reads the cumulative figure that python -X importtime reports for nl2sql. That figure measures imports only, so it is far less noisy than wall-clock time. The rule is added to invariants.md.

docs.title: 7. The facade
docs.text:
Built: the namespaces (PR 10a)

engine.datasources, engine.index, engine.llm (list, get, replace), engine.policies, engine.curated, engine.results and engine.traces (replay) are built, as internal classes in nl2sql/api/ that the facade builds on first use. run_query and stream_query take question and keyword-only options. The flat methods, engine.query, context, get_adapter, SettingsAPI, the sub-API exports, configure_llm, configure_llm_from_config and reload_llm_config are deleted, and test_nl2sql_exports_exactly_the_public_surface fixes the exports. POST /llm is the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm. Building it settled these details:

  • The split. PR 10 was split to stay reviewable. 10a is the namespaces, the REST API and the CLI on them, and the call sites in the playground. 10b moves the playground off the engine's internals: engine.feedback, traces.get, about() and llm.providers(), and the stricter import boundary test for the playground, nl2sql_api and cli/commands/demo.py.
  • Public API only, for the CLI too (owner decision). The CLI, the playground and nl2sql-api use nothing but the facade, never the runtime behind it. nl2sql run shows its live progress from stream_query's events (the PipelineRunner and the monitor callback are deleted; --show-perf is each step's time from its node_finished event, and the CLI records nl2sql.node.duration from them). index.build gains on_datasource, called with an IndexProgress (datasource_id, state: started, done with counts, or failed with reason) that a console line and a Phase 4 index job can both use; nl2sql index prints from it. nl2sql trace replay runs on engine.traces.replay, which 10a builds because the replay needs the runtime. test_the_cli_the_playground_and_the_api_use_only_the_public_api holds all three to it. The CLI's llm_interaction audit event went with the monitor callback; llm.changed is the audit log's one event.
  • llm.replace takes the section as written. Besides an LLM, it takes a mapping, checked by the loader's rules (parse_section in config/loader.py): strict keys with "did you mean", references kept in secret fields. A reference anywhere else is an error rather than read, so a request body never reads the server's environment. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm passes its body straight through and answers a ConfigError with 422 and its text.
  • llm.list() names agents as the llm section does (default, ast_planner, ...), each with provider, model, temperature and inherited.
  • datasources. DatasourceInfo.status is ready (connected by check() or test()), failed (with reason) or unchecked, since building never connects. remove(id) takes the datasource out of routing and engine.config and closes its pool; its index entries stay until the next full build. The REST datasource routes now return DatasourceInfo and DELETE removes.

Built: the playground off the engine's internals (PR 10b)

engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about(), engine.llm.providers() and engine.index.inspect_defaults() are built, and the playground, nl2sql demo and nl2sql feedback use them. Building it settled these details:

  • feedback.record(result, *, question, role, rating, note=None) takes the run's QueryResult (or its JSON) and builds the stored row from it and from the run's trace, so run_record moved behind the facade too: the playground remembers the part of each answered result a rating reads (no rows) and hands it over when the page rates the run. list(limit=None), stats(*, traces=None), export(path) (refuses the gold set's path with ValueError, returns {"written", "skipped"}) and clear() complete it. nl2sql feedback builds the engine without check(); the state store the engine opens holds the table, so the commands no longer avoid creating state.db.
  • traces.get(trace_id) returns the document or None, and raises ValueError for an id that is not a plain token; the playground's build_app lost its trace_dir argument.
  • about() is engine_info() (version, git_sha, python) plus steps, describe_pipeline over llm.list(). llm.providers() lists what the engine's registry can load: name, label, key_variable, key_present. index.inspect_defaults() is k, lambda_mult, fetch_multiplier and the entry types: the "retrieval inspector's defaults" the playground read from VectorStore.
  • Every new method returns plain dicts, so the export list is unchanged.
  • The stricter boundary test is test_the_playground_the_demo_command_and_the_api_import_only_the_public_nl2sql: nl2sql_api imports the top-level nl2sql only; the playground and cli/commands/demo.py import the top-level nl2sql, their own CLI package, and STILL_IMPORTED_FROM_INSIDE, a named list that only shrinks: nl2sql.common.settings (until PR 13), nl2sql.llm.providers (the provider catalogue the CLI reads, per CLAUDE.md), nl2sql.llm.request_key (use_request_llms, until Phase 4), and nl2sql demo's replay machinery, questions and init_project (nl2sql.llm.replay, nl2sql.testing.fake_llm, nl2sql.datasets.demo, nl2sql.config). nl2sql.feedback, nl2sql.tracing, nl2sql.pipeline, nl2sql.indexing and PROVIDER_PRESETS are out.
  • Left for PR 13: the playground still reads settings.feedback_enabled from the global, and the settings panel and nl2sql demo still write a key into os.environ.

The namespaces that are new (feedback, traces, results) exist because their data now lives under storage.path in the engine's config. A caller that built FeedbackStore(settings.schema_store_path) or read settings.trace_dir has no global to read any more, so the engine has to expose them.

docs.title: Impact on the consumers
docs.text:
Consumer Today What Phase 1 changes nl2sql-api NL2SQL() in the lifespan; engine.get_setting("observability_exporter"); flat methods; POST /llm calls configure_llm; role and CORS settings from NL2SQL_API_* NL2SQL.from_config() (reads NL2SQL_CONFIG), then engine.check(). Uses engine.config.settings.observability.exporter and the namespaces. POST /llm becomes PUT /api/v1/settings/llm (admin only), calling engine.llm.replace(). Admin roles come from engine.config.policies.admin_roles. The role header, static role, body-role trust and CORS origins come from engine.config.api. The lifespan loads the .env next to nl2sql.yaml before building the engine. The nl2sql-engine pin becomes ~=0.5.0 (bug B17). The CLI Builds NL2SQLContext directly in run, index, trace replay, setup, cli/common/indexing.py; reads settings.* paths Every command builds NL2SQL.from_config(ctx.config_path) and uses the facade. run_pipeline and run_indexing take the engine. NL2SQLContext is no longer importable from the CLI. The playground (cli/demo/) NL2SQL(), engine.context.policies_cfg, reload_llm_config, FeedbackStore(settings.schema_store_path), settings.trace_dir, settings.feedback_enabled, describe_pipeline, engine_info, PROVIDER_PRESETS; writes keys into os.environ Builds from the demo folder's nl2sql.yaml. It still writes llm.yaml for the next start, and a key typed in the panel goes into the new LLM as a value and into the demo folder's .env, never into os.environ. use_request_llms (hosted per-request keys) and run_record stay internal imports until Phase 4, when the web app moves onto nl2sql-api.

The boundary test test_the_playground_never_touches_the_engine_context (since 10a test_the_cli_the_playground_and_the_api_use_only_the_public_api) becomes stricter: the playground and nl2sql_api may not import nl2sql.common.settings (which is deleted anyway), nl2sql.context, nl2sql.configs, nl2sql.feedback, nl2sql.pipeline or nl2sql.tracing.

docs.title: What is global today
docs.text:
Global Where Why it breaks two engines settings singleton common/settings.py:355, imported by 43 modules One set of values per process. reload_settings() mutates it in place. In-place settings edits around a run evaluation/tier1.py:133, tier2.py:494, retrieval_recall.py:154, tracing/replay.py:297 They save, change and restore the global, which races with any other thread running a query. EmbeddingService._instance indexing/embeddings.py:116 One embedder per process, keyed only by the provider name. secret_manager secrets/__init__.py:12, used by api/policy_api.py One set of resolved secrets per process. os.environ writes context.py:50-52, cli/main.py:91-93, cli/commands/demo.py (keys, ENV, PLAN_CACHE_ENABLED), cli/commands/setup.py, cli/demo/manager.py, cli/demo/playground/settings.py Config travels through the environment, so it is shared by every engine in the process and leaks into child processes.

Logging handlers and the OpenTelemetry provider are global by nature. Only the application entry point configures them, and that does not change in Phase 1. OpenTelemetry moves in Phase 3.

docs.title: The target
docs.text:
• The runtime owns its settings. The engine builds one internal Runtime, which replaces NL2SQLContext, from its Config. Every node, store and service already receives that context object, so ctx.settings (the Settings model) is the carrier. A module that has no context takes the value it needs as a parameter: run_date(today) instead of reading settings.today.
  • The embedder belongs to the runtime. It is built once from cfg.embeddings by the registry. EmbeddingService and its class cache are deleted.
  • The secret manager belongs to the runtime. It is built from cfg.secrets, and the module-level secret_manager is deleted.
  • No os.environ writes. Keys and options travel in the Config.
  • Runs that need different settings build a derived config. Evaluation and trace replay build an engine (or runtime) from cfg.model_copy(update=...) instead of editing a global and restoring it.

docs.title: Staging it
docs.text:
Built: step 1 (PR 7a)

_copy_into_global_settings in nl2sql/runtime.py copies the settings section, policies.refusal_names_tables, llm.prices, whether curated is present, and the store locations under storage.path into the global. READS_THE_SETTINGS_GLOBAL in tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py is the ratchet list, and tests/e2e/test_two_engines_fake_llm.py is the strict expected failure. The repository's root conftest.py puts the global back after every test, because building an engine changes it.

Built: step 2, the pipeline (PR 11)

The pipeline nodes, the SQL agent subgraph, pipeline/runtime.py, the plan cache, execution and aggregation read ctx.settings, ctx.config.policies and ctx.artifact_store; build_artifact_store() is gone. run_date(today) is in nl2sql/common/dates.py, and PlanCache(store, enabled=..., today=...) takes its settings as parameters. Evaluation (tiers 1 and 2, retrieval recall) and trace replay pinned pipeline settings by editing the global, which the pipeline no longer reads, so until PR 12 gives them derived configs they pin them on the runtime with pinned_config(ctx, {"settings.pipeline.plan_cache": False}) in nl2sql/runtime.py. That swaps ctx.config for the run and puts it back, with the same one-engine-at-a-time caveat the global had. Node tests build their context with nl2sql.testing.runtime.fake_runtime. With the pipeline on the runtime, tests/e2e/test_two_engines_fake_llm.py passes, so it is a normal test from this PR on rather than from PR 13.

Built: step 2, indexing and the rest (PR 12)

indexing, services, tracing and evaluation no longer read the global; secrets and feedback already did not, and the embedder and the secret manager have been per runtime since PR 7a. The trace writer takes its sizes and folder from ctx.settings.traces and ctx.traces_dir, and its settings snapshot is the run's settings section. tracing.replay caps the replayed result with the run's settings.traces. The curated search takes k from the caller's settings.curated.match_top_k, index health reads state.db directly, and PipelineMonitorCallback takes settings.observability as a parameter. pinned_config and the Runtime.config setter are deleted: evaluation (tiers 1 and 2, retrieval recall) and trace replay call ctx.derive({"settings.pipeline.plan_cache": False, ...}), which returns a run-scoped runtime built from derived_config (dotted paths over model_copy). It shares the adapters, embedder, stores and the engine's LLMClientCache, and has its own config, curated answers and LLMSet, built through that cache from the derived llm section (LLMRegistry.derive). An llm.replace on the engine is therefore what the next run starts from, equal agent settings share one client, and a run that replaces its LLMs (tier 1's gold-plan fake, tier 2's configs, replay's playback clients) never changes the engine's. nl2sql.runtime stays on the ratchet list for the copy step, which PR 13 deletes.

Built: step 3, the apps, and the global deleted (PR 13)

The playground reads settings.feedback.enabled from engine.config. common/settings.py, common/env_hint.py and _copy_into_global_settings are deleted, with the repository's root conftest.py (it restored the global, and pointed its trace and artifact folders at a temporary directory, which storage.path now does), the READS_THE_SETTINGS_GLOBAL ratchet and the nl2sql.common.settings entry in STILL_IMPORTED_FROM_INSIDE. pydantic-settings is no longer a dependency. test_no_module_writes_the_environment and test_environment_reads_only_from_the_allow_list are the two permanent tests, and test_only_entry_points_load_dotenv a third. tests/e2e/test_two_engines_fake_llm.py has passed as a normal test since PR 11. Every os.environ write is gone; the demo's are described in Demo and playground.

Each step is one green PR, and no release happens in between:

  1. The switch PR (7a in the plan) introduces Runtime.from_config(cfg). For the length of the migration only, it also copies cfg.settings into the old settings object, so modules not yet moved still read correct values. A ratchet test in test_boundaries.py lists the modules still allowed to import nl2sql.common.settings, and that list may only shrink.
  2. Three migration PRs move folders onto ctx.settings and remove them from the ratchet list:
  3. the pipeline nodes, execution and aggregation;
  4. indexing (with the embedder), secrets, services, tracing, evaluation and feedback;
  5. the CLI, the playground and nl2sql-api.
  6. The last migration PR deletes common/settings.py, env_hint.py, the copy step and the ratchet list. It then adds two permanent tests:
  7. No environment writes or stray reads. No module under nl2sql/ or nl2sql_api/ assigns to os.environ, calls os.putenv or load_dotenv. os.environ and os.getenv reads are allowed only in nl2sql/config/ (for NL2SQL_CONFIG), nl2sql/llm/ (provider keys), the env secret provider, configure_logging (for NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL), the trace redactor and nl2sql benchmark (for CI).
  8. Two engines in one process. This test is written in the switch PR, marked xfail(strict=True), and flipped to a normal test here:
def test_two_engines_in_one_process_keep_their_own_config(tmp_path, fake_llm):
    env_before = dict(os.environ)
    a = NL2SQL(demo_config(tmp_path / "a", row_limit=5, plan_cache=False, llm=fake_llm.config("a")))
    b = NL2SQL(demo_config(tmp_path / "b", row_limit=50, plan_cache=True, llm=fake_llm.config("b")))
    with a, b:
        a.index.build(); b.index.build()
        ra = a.run_query("List every track", user_context=ADMIN)
        rb = b.run_query("List every track", user_context=ADMIN)
    assert ra.rows_returned == 5 and rb.rows_returned == 50          # each engine's own settings
    assert (tmp_path / "a" / "index").exists() and (tmp_path / "b" / "index").exists()
    assert fake_llm.requests_for("a") and fake_llm.requests_for("b")  # each engine's own LLM
    assert a._runtime.embedder is not b._runtime.embedder
    assert dict(os.environ) == env_before                            # nothing written

docs.text:
Built

The rename is built (PR 1), and so is the secrets module (PR 4).

What 0.4 0.5 Distribution nl2sql-adapter-sdk nl2sql-sdk (free on PyPI on 2026-10-13) Import package nl2sql_adapter_sdk nl2sql_sdk Folder packages/adapter-sdk/ packages/sdk/ Modules capabilities, contracts, protocols, schema the same four, plus secrets (the SecretProvider protocol). The stores and policy modules come in Phase 2. Everything is re-exported from nl2sql_sdk. Dependencies pydantic>=2.0 unchanged: pydantic and the standard library only Engine dependency nl2sql-adapter-sdk~=0.1 nl2sql-sdk~=0.5.0: the engine's own version as a compatible release, on a line release-please bumps Entry points nl2sql.adapters unchanged.
