docs.title: Overview
docs.text: GraphState is the shared, typed state container for the NL2SQL pipeline's LangGraph execution. It exists to provide a single, structured place where node outputs, errors, reasoning, and subgraph artifacts accumulate as the graph runs. Its scope is the main pipeline graph built in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/graph.py, and it is the input/output contract for graph nodes declared in that graph.

docs.title: Primary class
docs.text:
• GraphState in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/state.py

Fields (exact names and types from code): - trace_id: str - user_query: str - user_context: UserContext - datasource_id: Optional[str] - verified_match: Optional[VerifiedMatch] - datasource_resolver_response: Optional[DatasourceResolverResponse] - decomposer_response: Optional[DecomposerResponse] - execution_dag: Optional[ExecutionDAG] - aggregator_response: Optional[AggregatorResponse] - answer_synthesizer_response: Optional[AnswerSynthesizerResponse] - artifact_refs: Annotated[Dict[str, ArtifactRef], update_results] - subgraph_outputs: Annotated[Dict[str, SubgraphOutput], update_results] - errors: Annotated[List[PipelineError], operator.add] - reasoning: Annotated[List[Dict[str, Any]], operator.add] - warnings: Annotated[List[Dict[str, Any]], operator.add] - subgraph_id: Optional[str] - subgraph_name: Optional[str]

Reducer behavior in GraphState: - update_results(current, new) merges dicts as {**current, **new}. - operator.add concatenates lists for errors, reasoning, and warnings.

docs.text:
• SubgraphExecutionState in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/state.py is the per-subgraph state used by the SQL agent subgraph.

docs.title: Field Lifecycle
docs.text: The lifecycle below lists creation, mutation, reads, and resets based strictly on code.

docs.title: trace_id
docs.text:
• Creation: default factory in GraphState (uuid4) if not provided; always set in run_with_graph when GraphState is instantiated.
  • Mutation: not mutated after creation in this repository.
  • Read points: build_scan_payload and wrap_subgraph use it; ExecutorRequest uses it in ExecutorNode.
  • Reset: none.

docs.text:
• Creation: passed into GraphState in run_with_graph.
  • Mutation: none in code.
  • Read points: DatasourceResolverNode, DecomposerNode, AnswerSynthesizerNode.
  • Reset: none.

docs.text:
• Creation: passed into GraphState in run_with_graph; a caller that passes none (or None) gets an empty UserContext, the field's default.
  • Mutation: none in code.
  • Read points: DatasourceResolverNode (RBAC), ExecutorNode, and subgraph state in wrap_subgraph.
  • Reset: none.

docs.text:
• Creation: passed into GraphState in run_with_graph.
  • Mutation: none in code.
  • Read points: DatasourceResolverNode (explicit override).

docs.text:

  • Read points: resolver_route, DecomposerNode, and build_scan_payload.

docs.text:

docs.text:

  • Read points: wrap_subgraph uses it to determine sub_query id and build SubgraphOutput.

docs.text:

  • Read points: wrap_subgraph and ExecutorRequest via ExecutorNode.

docs.title: Ownership Model
docs.text:
Ownership is defined by which node returns updates for a field: - verified_match: CuratedMatcherNode, on a verified answer only. On that path the matcher also writes decomposer_response, execution_dag, artifact_refs and subgraph_outputs (one sub-query, plan_source="verified"), and no resolver, decomposer or SQL agent runs. - datasource_resolver_response: DatasourceResolverNode - decomposer_response: DecomposerNode - execution_dag: DecomposerNode - aggregator_response: EngineAggregatorNode - answer_synthesizer_response: AnswerSynthesizerNode - artifact_refs: wrap_subgraph (subgraph wrapper in graph_utils.py) - subgraph_outputs: wrap_subgraph - errors, reasoning: emitted by many nodes and merged by list reducers - warnings: emitted by nodes that return warnings in the main graph (currently DatasourceResolverNode) - subgraph_id, subgraph_name: created in build_scan_payload, used only for subgraph execution context - trace_id, user_query, user_context, datasource_id: owned by the pipeline entrypoint (run_with_graph)

Shared vs private: - Shared: errors, reasoning, warnings, artifact_refs, subgraph_outputs are aggregate fields merged across branches. - Private/branch-scoped: subgraph_id, subgraph_name are injected into subgraph payloads for a single subgraph execution.

docs.title: State Flow Across DAG
docs.text:
Step-by-step execution flow as defined in build_graph and routing: 1. run_with_graph constructs GraphState with user_query, user_context, and optional datasource_id, then calls graph.invoke(initial_state.model_dump()). 2. DatasourceResolverNode runs first (after CuratedMatcherNode falls back, when curated answers are configured) and populates datasource_resolver_response, reasoning, and errors. 3. resolver_route decides whether to continue based on datasource_resolver_response. 4. DecomposerNode produces decomposer_response, the execution_dag built from it, and reasoning. 5. build_scan_layer_router emits Send branches using build_scan_payload for each pending scan node. The payload contains subgraph_id, subgraph_name, trace_id, user_context, decomposer_response, and datasource_resolver_response. 6. Each subgraph is wrapped by wrap_subgraph, which: - Builds a SubgraphExecutionState using the payload and a sub_query resolved from decomposer_response. - Invokes the subgraph and validates the result into SubgraphExecutionState. - Returns updates for artifact_refs, subgraph_outputs, errors, and reasoning. 7. The router checks artifact_refs to decide which scan nodes are still pending. When none remain, it routes to aggregator. 8. EngineAggregatorNode consumes execution_dag and artifact_refs to produce aggregator_response. 9. AnswerSynthesizerNode consumes aggregator_response and decomposer_response to produce answer_synthesizer_response.

Subgraph internal flow uses SubgraphExecutionState and is defined in build_sql_agent_graph: schema_retriever -> ast_planner -> logical_validator -> generator -> executor, with a retry loop via retry_handler and refiner.

docs.title: Mutability Rules
docs.text:
From code: - GraphState and SubgraphExecutionState are Pydantic BaseModel classes with extra="ignore" and arbitrary_types_allowed=True. No immutability or frozen settings are defined. - List fields (errors, reasoning, warnings) are merged using operator.add. - Dict fields (artifact_refs, subgraph_outputs) are merged using update_results ({**current, **new}). - Subgraph boundary is a serialization boundary: wrap_subgraph uses SubgraphExecutionState(...).model_dump() to pass data into the subgraph and SubgraphExecutionState.model_validate(...) to rehydrate the result.

No explicit copy-on-write mechanisms are defined beyond Pydantic serialization at subgraph boundaries.

docs.title: Merge Semantics
docs.text:
Defined reducers in GraphState: - update_results merges dicts with {**current, **new}. Keys in new overwrite keys in current. - operator.add concatenates list fields (errors, reasoning, warnings).

No explicit reducer is defined in this repository for scalar fields; any conflict resolution beyond these reducers is not specified in code here.

docs.title: Replayability
docs.text: GraphState carries identifiers and artifact references that could support replay, but no replay or rehydration mechanism is implemented. See failure_recovery.md for replay support details and limitations.

docs.title: Determinism Impact
docs.text: Determinism guarantees and non-determinism sources are documented in determinism.md. GraphState only carries the artifacts produced by those nodes (IDs, errors, and diagnostics).

docs.title: Serialization + Persistence
docs.text:
Serialization: - GraphState and SubgraphExecutionState are Pydantic models. run_with_graph calls initial_state.model_dump() before invoking the graph. - wrap_subgraph uses model_dump() and model_validate() for subgraph boundaries.

Persistence: - GraphState itself is not persisted in this repository. - artifact_refs contain ArtifactRef entries with uri, backend, format, and content_hash, which reference artifacts stored elsewhere by executor components.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Based on code only: - No explicit ordering guarantee is defined for merging parallel branch dict updates beyond {**current, **new}. - No built-in persistence or snapshotting for GraphState is implemented. - No explicit reset or cleanup semantics for accumulated fields (errors, reasoning, warnings, artifact_refs, subgraph_outputs).

docs.title: Indexing, Chunking, and Retrieval Architecture
docs.text: This document describes current indexing behavior as implemented in code. Indexing transforms schema snapshots into typed chunks that are embedded and stored in a Chroma vector store. Retrieval uses these chunks as candidates and then resolves authoritative schema details from SchemaStore (see ../schema/store.md for schema contracts and store behavior).

docs.title: Indexing flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Adapter[Datasource Adapter] --> Snapshot[Schema Snapshot]
    Snapshot --> Enrich[LLM Enrichment - optional]
    Enrich --> Register[SchemaStore.register_snapshot]
    Register --> Chunker[SchemaChunkBuilder]
    Curated[curated.yaml] --> CChunker[CuratedChunkBuilder]
    Chunker --> Refresh[VectorStore.refresh_schema_chunks]
    CChunker --> Refresh
    Refresh --> Store[Chroma Vector Store]

The snapshot profiles each column on its own: a column, row count or table the database cannot profile is indexed without statistics and logged, rather than failing the datasource's index (see Column statistics).

docs.title: What is indexed today
docs.text: Schema-derived chunks, and the verified queries of curated.yaml when the file exists. There is no symbolic index, behavioral index, or other catalog in the current implementation.

docs.title: Chunk types and contracts
docs.text:
Chunk types are defined in nl2sql.indexing.models:

  • DatasourceChunk (schema.datasource): datasource description, domains, and example questions. The description is the one the datasource was registered with (description: in the datasources config, or the description of a Datasource passed to engine.datasources.add); the orchestrator reads it from the datasource registry, falling back to the datasources file only when the registry has none. It lives in the config rather than the database, so the orchestrator writes it into the snapshot's metadata, where it takes precedence over any description the adapter or enrichment produced. Example questions come from the SAMPLE_QUESTIONS file.
  • TableChunk (schema.table): table name, PKs, column list, FK summaries, row counts.
  • ColumnChunk (schema.column): column type, stats, synonyms, PII flags.
  • RelationshipChunk (schema.relationship): FK relationships, columns, cardinality.
  • MetricChunk (schema.metric): defined but not emitted by SchemaChunkBuilder.
  • VerifiedQueryChunk (curated.verified_query): one phrasing of a verified query, or its description, built by CuratedChunkBuilder (nl2sql.indexing.curated). Each {placeholder} is filled with the param's example, else its default, else its own name, because a raw {n} embeds poorly: "Best {n} customers in {year}" is embedded as "Best 10 customers in 2012". Metadata: id, type, datasource_id, query_id, schema_version. Ids: curated.verified_query:<datasource_id>:<query_id>:<n>, the phrasings in order, then the description. The SQL is never indexed.

Chunk models live in nl2sql.indexing.models and are Pydantic models. IDs are deterministic and include schema_version.

docs.title: Verified queries
docs.text:
Verified query entries are written in the same build as the datasource's schema entries: IndexingOrchestrator.index_datasource() appends them to the schema chunks before refresh_schema_chunks(). A build replaces every entry of its datasource, so curated entries written on their own would be deleted by the next schema re-index.

At the switch the collection metadata also records curated_hash:<datasource_id>, a SHA-256 of that datasource's verified queries as canonical JSON (metrics are left out; nothing indexes them yet). Index health compares it with the file as it is now (see Index health).

Changing curated.yaml does not re-read the schema. nl2sql index --curated-only (engine.index.build(curated_only=True), IndexingOrchestrator.refresh_curated(), VectorStore.refresh_curated_chunks()) writes a new build for each datasource the usual way, except that the active build's schema entries are copied into it with their stored vectors: no schema read, no snapshot registered, no enrichment model call, and only the verified queries are embedded. The switch and the deletion of the old build are the ones described below, so the refresh is just as safe. It needs the datasource to have been indexed once; otherwise that datasource fails with a message saying to run nl2sql index. --curated-only cannot be combined with --full or --enrich.

VectorStore.retrieve_verified_query_candidates(question, datasource_ids, k) returns the verified queries a question most resembles. It is a plain similarity search, not MMR, because several phrasings of one query are exactly what should match: it reads the active builds of the given datasources only, fetches k × 10 entries, keeps each query's best phrasing (by cosine similarity), and returns the best k (CURATED_MATCH_TOP_K, 5), each with its score and the phrasing that won. With no verified query entry among those datasources it returns nothing without embedding the question. Given an explain list, it appends a record shaped like the MMR one below. Nothing in the pipeline calls it yet; the matcher that will is described in Curated Answers (design).

docs.title: Chunk → index mapping (actual)
docs.text:
All chunk types are embedded as langchain_core.documents.Document and stored in Chroma:

  • Document.page_content = chunk.get_page_content()
  • Document.metadata = chunk.get_metadata()

There is one index (Chroma collection) per VectorStore configuration, shared by every datasource. Each entry also carries a build_id (see below); it is stripped from retrieved documents, because the resolver prints a datasource entry's metadata into the decomposer prompt.

docs.title: Rebuilding without an empty index
docs.text:
Re-indexing never deletes the collection first. Each datasource is rebuilt on its own, inside the one collection (VectorStore.refresh_schema_chunks):

flowchart TD
    A[Read schema, register snapshot] --> B[Write every entry under a new build_id]
    B --> C{All entries written?}
    C -->|no| D[Delete the partial new build; previous entries stay active]
    C -->|yes| E[Switch: collection metadata build:DS = new build_id]
    E --> F[Delete the datasource's other builds]
  • The collection's metadata names each datasource's active build (build:<datasource_id>) and when it was switched in (built_at:<datasource_id>). Every retrieval filters on the active builds, so while the old and new builds coexist a reader sees exactly one of them, never both and never a mix of schema versions. Entries written before builds existed have no build_id and are read as they are until their datasource is next re-indexed.
  • Other datasources are never read, deleted or rewritten by a datasource's rebuild. nl2sql index --datasource X rebuilds only X; nl2sql index rebuilds each configured datasource in turn, and a failure keeps that datasource's previous entries active and exits 1.
  • Callers that serve questions can hold them back around the switch: engine.index.build(..., switch_guard=...). The playground passes its RunGate, so questions in flight finish first.
  • nl2sql.indexing.rebuild.rebuild_index, behind engine.index.build, is the one entry point for nl2sql index, the demo's startup repair, the playground's Rebuild and the REST index routes. Its on_datasource callback gets an IndexProgress per datasource (started, then done with the entry counts or failed with the reason): nl2sql index prints a line from it.

docs.title: One embedding model per collection
docs.text: A query is embedded once, in one space, so every datasource in a collection must use the same embedding model. The collection records it (embedding_model, e.g. local/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) on its first write. If the configured model differs, retrieval and per-datasource re-indexing raise EmbeddingModelMismatchError, which also catches two different models of the same dimension that the dimension check cannot. A model change is the one case that needs every datasource rebuilt at once: nl2sql index --full builds all of them into a staging collection (<name>__staging) and swaps it in by renaming only when all succeed; a failure discards the staging collection and leaves the live one untouched. A collection written before models were recorded adopts the configured model on its next write (the dimension check still applies).

docs.title: Index health
docs.text: nl2sql.indexing.health judges an index by its contents, never by whether its folder exists (the demo once had a data/vector_store_demo folder holding 0 entries). Only active builds are counted. Status, worst first: missing (no folder or collection), empty (0 entries), stale (a configured datasource has no entries, its entries were built from an older schema version than the latest snapshot, or the configured embedding model differs), ok. It reports entry counts by type, the schema version per datasource, when each was built and the recorded embedding model. warnings never change the status: a datasource whose curated.yaml section has changed since it was indexed (its recorded curated_hash differs from the file's) gets "curated.yaml changed for 'chinook' since it was indexed; run nl2sql index --curated-only --datasource chinook". Questions keep working meanwhile; the stale entries still name queries that exist. A preferred_tables entry missing from the datasource's latest snapshot is a warning too. nl2sql doctor prints it under Index, nl2sql demo rebuilds at startup when it is not ok, and the playground and GET /api/v1/index/status show it (through engine.index.health()), the playground with a Rebuild button.

docs.title: Chunking strategy (as implemented)
docs.text:
Chunking is aligned to planning intent:

  • Routing uses datasource-level chunks.
  • Schema context uses table/metric chunks.
  • Planning context uses columns and relationships for specific tables.

If retrieval returns no candidates, the retriever falls back to full schema enumeration.

docs.title: Retrieval pipeline (staged, code-accurate)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    SubQuery --> SemQuery[_build_semantic_query]
    SemQuery --> L1[retrieve_schema_context (tables/metrics)]
    L1 -->|no tables| L2[retrieve_column_candidates]
    L2 --> L3[retrieve_planning_context (columns/relationships)]
    L3 --> Snapshot[SchemaStore.get_snapshot]
    Snapshot --> Tables[relevant_tables for planner]

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
1. Schema context: retrieves table/metric chunks.
  2. Column candidates: fallback to column chunks when no table matches.
  3. Planning context: retrieves columns/relationships for the selected tables.
  4. Authoritative resolution: resolves tables/columns from SchemaStore snapshot.

docs.title: Authoritative vs semantic sources
docs.text:
• Semantic candidates come from Chroma (vector search over chunks).
  • Authoritative schema is resolved from SchemaStore snapshots.
  • Vector store content is never treated as authoritative.

docs.title: Metadata propagation
docs.text:
• datasource_id and schema_version are included in all chunk metadata.
  • TableChunk includes primary_key, columns, row_count, and FK summaries.
  • ColumnChunk includes dtype, pii, description, and stats when available.
  • RelationshipChunk includes join column pairs and cardinality.

Metadata is consumed by SchemaRetrieverNode to construct Table objects for planning and by LogicalValidatorNode to validate joins and filters.

docs.title: Versioning and determinism
docs.text:
• Schema snapshots are fingerprinted and versioned (YYYYMMDDhhmmss_<fp8>).
  • Chunk IDs embed schema_version for deterministic indexing.
  • Retrieval uses the SubQuery.schema_version when available; otherwise latest snapshot.
  • MMR ranking may introduce non-determinism in ordering for similar scores.

docs.title: Retrieval: MMR, not a re-ranking model
docs.text:
Every vector search in the engine is one maximal marginal relevance (MMR) search over the one Chroma collection, nl2sql_store, which holds every datasource (the demo's three databases: 3 datasource, 20 table, 121 column and 18 relationship entries, 162 in all, of which Chinook is 87). There is no re-ranking model. What is sometimes called re-ranking is this:

  1. Embed the query text with the collection's embedder (the local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 costs nothing per query).
  2. Fetch the pool: the fetch_k = 4 * k entries nearest to it, filtered by entry type, datasource and active build.
  3. Pick k of them one at a time. The first pick is the entry most similar to the query (cosine similarity). Every later pick is the pool entry with the highest 0.7 * similarity(entry, query) - 0.3 * max similarity(entry, earlier picks), so an entry that nearly repeats an earlier pick loses to a less similar one that adds something. lambda_mult = 0.7 is the weight on similarity.

The documents come back in pool order (nearest first), not pick order, exactly as Chroma.max_marginal_relevance_search returns them.

Caller Search Entry types k Pool DatasourceResolverNode datasources datasource 5 20 SchemaRetrieverNode tables table, metric 8 32 SchemaRetrieverNode, when tables finds nothing columns column 8 32 SchemaRetrieverNode, over the tables found planning column, relationship 12 48

The schema retriever runs none of these when the schema has SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FULL_SNAPSHOT_MAX_TABLES tables or fewer (15 by default, so each of the demo's three schemas, at 11, 4 and 5 tables, is always sent whole); the resolver runs none when the request names a datasource_id or only one datasource is registered. The demo is no longer such a case: with three datasources registered, the resolver searches on every question.

A datasource's preferred_tables change the order but not the searches: on either path they come first, and on the retrieval path a preferred table the tables search scored within 0.05 of its least similar pick is added (see SchemaRetrieverNode).

nl2sql.indexing.retrieval_trace.mmr_search is the one implementation: it makes the Chroma query and calls the same maximal_marginal_relevance function Chroma's method does, and returns the documents with a record of the search (the query, the pool with similarity, Chroma distance and type, the picks in order with the score each won with, and what was dropped). The record comes from numbers MMR computes anyway, so it costs no second search. Nodes put it in their run trace (see Debugging a run), and the playground's Retrieval inspector (engine.index.inspect) runs the same search for any text, with k, lambda, entry types and datasource exposed. That inspector is the tool for chunking experiments: change the chunks, rebuild, search the same text, and diff the Copy as text output.

The resolver's datasources search is exact: instead of Chroma's nearest-neighbour query it scores every active schema.datasource entry by cosine similarity and takes the nearest. There is one such entry per datasource among hundreds of others, and Chroma's approximate (HNSW) search under a filter that selective can return fewer entries than exist, which dropped a datasource from a question's candidates now and then. The other searches stay approximate.

docs.title: Tenant isolation (current state)
docs.text:
Tenant scoping is not implemented in indexing:

  • No tenant_id field exists in chunk metadata.
  • Vector store queries do not filter by tenant.
  • Schema store is global.

docs.title: Failure modes and fallbacks
docs.text:
Current failure behaviors:

  • Vector store retrieval wrapped by VECTOR_BREAKER; failures fast‑fail.
  • Vector retrieval errors in SchemaRetrieverNode return empty results with warnings.
  • If no candidates are found, the retriever falls back to full schema snapshot.
  • Enrichment is opt-in: engine.index.build, rebuild_index, IndexingOrchestrator and nl2sql index all default to enrich=False; pass enrich=True (or nl2sql index --enrich) to spend tokens on it. It only fills blanks: a table or column comment read from the database is never overwritten.
  • Enrichment failures return the original snapshot without enrichment, and never fail indexing. enrich_schema_snapshot resolves its own LLM inside the guard, so a missing API key, an unreachable endpoint and a failed call all degrade the same way. A missing/unusable LLM logs at INFO; any other failure (a 401, a timeout) logs one WARNING line with the reason and no stack trace (the trace is logged at DEBUG).
  • Retrieving from a vector store whose persisted vectors do not match the configured embedding provider raises EmbeddingDimensionMismatchError; a recorded embedding model that differs from the configured one raises EmbeddingModelMismatchError. Either is fixed with nl2sql index --full.
  • When the resolver finds no datasource and the index is empty, its SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FAILED error says so and names nl2sql index, instead of "No datasource candidates resolved."
  • A failed rebuild leaves the previous entries active (see above).

docs.title: Performance characteristics (current)
docs.text:
• Embedding uses the engine's own embedder, built from its embeddings section: OpenAI embeddings, or the local ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model with provider: local.
  • Vector search is MMR (lambda_mult=0.7, fetch_k = 4*k); see Retrieval.
  • No caching or sharding layers are implemented.
  • Index refresh re-embeds every entry of the datasource being re-indexed; other datasources are untouched. nl2sql index --curated-only embeds only the verified queries and copies the schema entries' stored vectors.

docs.title: Observability hooks
docs.text:
• VECTOR_BREAKER logs breaker state changes.
  • Indexing and retrieval log errors; no metrics are emitted in indexing code.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Chunk models: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/models.py
  • Chunk builder: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/chunk_builder.py
  • Verified query entries and their hash: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/curated.py
  • Vector store: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/vector_store.py
  • Schema retriever: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py
  • Indexing orchestrator: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/orchestrator.py
  • Embeddings: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/embeddings.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: These invariants capture rules that are enforced by the code paths responsible for planning, validation, and execution. They exist to keep the system deterministic, secure, and stable under malformed input or misconfiguration.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Sub-query intents and post-combine operations must not contain SQL. Each text field (intent, metric names, filter, group-by and order-by attributes, expected-schema names) is checked on its own and rejected if it opens with a SELECT ... FROM statement, or contains a statement terminator (;) or a comment marker (--, /*, */). English words that happen to be SQL keywords are allowed: "customers from Brazil" and "tracks where the genre is Rock" are valid intents.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• SubQuery.validate_semantic_only() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas
  • PostCombineOp.validate_semantic_only() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError ("contains SQL syntax") when a field matches; the decomposer response fails validation.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents physical SQL leakage into semantic planning stages and keeps decomposer output safe to interpret downstream.

docs.title: Combine Groups Require Roles and Join Keys
Definition
docs.text: Combine groups with compare or join operations must include a role for every input and at least one join key pair.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • CombineGroup.validate_roles() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError when roles or join keys are missing.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures combine operations are well-defined and deterministic for aggregation.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Combine-group inputs must reference existing subqueries, and post-combine ops must reference existing combine groups.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • DecomposerResponse.validate_references() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError for unknown subquery or group references.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents invalid execution graphs and dangling references.

docs.title: Expression AST Must Match Its Kind
Definition
docs.text: Expression nodes must satisfy kind-specific required fields (e.g., binary ops require left/right and an operator).

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • Expr.model_post_init() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError when required fields are missing or operators are invalid.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Guarantees the AST is structurally complete before SQL generation.

docs.title: Plan Model Is Strict and Read-Only
Definition
docs.text: Plan fields are schema-validated with no unknown fields, and query type must be READ.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• ConfigDict(extra="forbid") on plan models in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.schemas
  • PlanModel.query_type: Literal["READ"] in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.schemas, which pydantic enforces before any node sees the plan (the plan cache re-validates on read, so a cached plan is covered too)

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Pydantic validation errors for extra/invalid fields and for any query_type other than READ; the plan never reaches the validator. LogicalValidatorNode no longer re-checks it — the branch was unreachable.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents mutation or unknown plan constructs from entering execution.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Each table alias in the plan must be unique.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • LogicalValidatorNode._alias_collision() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with INVALID_PLAN_STRUCTURE.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents ambiguous column resolution.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Every func expression names a function from ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.functions, written as a plain identifier (any case).

The only date functions on the list are the ones the planner prompt offers: DATE_PART and DATE_TRUNC, plus YEAR, QUARTER, MONTH, DAY and EXTRACT, which are read as DATE_PART. STRFTIME is still accepted as a legacy name (LEGACY_FUNCTIONS): a recorded demo answer and three hand-written tier 1 gold plans call it. Nothing offers it to the model, and the validator's rejection message leaves it out of the functions it lists.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• LogicalValidatorNode._unsupported_functions() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_date_functions_agree_with_prompt.py reads the allow-list and the planner prompt together, so a date function cannot be allowed by one and forbidden by the other

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION (severity ERROR, so the refiner can retry).

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: func_name is model text that becomes the function's name in the SQL. Without the check, any text, including a second statement, reached the query.

docs.title: Expected Schema Must Match Select List
Definition
docs.text: When expected_schema is provided, the plan’s select_items count and aliases must match it.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with INVALID_PLAN_STRUCTURE.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Keeps multi-stage subqueries contractually aligned.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: All column references must map to declared table aliases and be unambiguous.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• LogicalValidatorNode._validate_columns() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node, which resolves the plan with sqlglot.optimizer.qualify.qualify() against the schema retrieved for the query
  • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() converts resolution failures to PipelineError

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with COLUMN_NOT_FOUND: a retryable ERROR by default, a WARNING that does not block when logical_validator_strict_columns is turned off.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents queries from referencing non-existent or ambiguous columns.

docs.title: Joins Must Be Valid and Schema-Backed
Definition
docs.text: Join aliases must exist, join conditions must reference both sides, must include an equality pair, and must match allowed schema relationships.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() join checks in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with INVALID_PLAN_STRUCTURE or JOIN_TABLE_NOT_IN_PLAN.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents invalid joins and enforces schema-authorized relationships.

docs.title: Policy Enforcement Is Namespaced and Fail-Closed
Definition
docs.text: Allowed tables must be namespaced as datasource.*, datasource.schema.*, datasource.schema.table or datasource.table, and policy checks fail if datasource ID is missing. Access is decided on datasource, schema and table: a two-part datasource.table means that table in the datasource's default schema only, and a table the plan names without a schema is in the default schema. One function, table_allowed() in nl2sql.auth.rbac, decides for every node.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• RolePolicy.validate_namespace() in nl2sql.auth.models
  • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_policy() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node
  • table_allowed() and default_schema() in nl2sql.auth.rbac, called with the same datasource, schema and table by the validator, the schema retriever, the executor's value check and the curated matcher

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: ValueError for invalid policy format; PipelineError with SECURITY_VIOLATION if datasource ID is missing or a table is not allowed. An unknown role, or no role, allows nothing and is refused the same way, never with VALIDATOR_CRASH. The user-facing refusal names no table unless RBAC_REFUSAL_NAMES_TABLES is set; the table and roles are in the error's details.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures access control boundaries are explicit and enforced.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Only datasources permitted by RBAC may be selected or resolved.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• DatasourceResolverNode._get_allowed_datasource_ids() and __call__() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.datasource_resolver.node
  • CuratedMatcherNode._searchable() and _check_access() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.curated_matcher.node: the verified-query search covers only datasources the role may read, and every table a verified query's SQL reads must pass table_allowed()

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with SECURITY_VIOLATION if no allowed datasource is available. The check runs before the resolver's answerability LLM call, so a denied caller triggers no model call and the model only ever sees datasources the role may read. It runs on every path, including the single-datasource shortcut that skips the vector search. The curated matcher refuses nothing itself: a verified query on a datasource or table the role may not read is never offered or never run, and the run falls back (policy_denied) to the resolver, which refuses as above.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents execution against unauthorized datasources.

docs.title: SQL Execution Requires SQL, Datasource, and Capability
Definition
docs.text: Execution only proceeds when SQL text exists, a datasource ID is present, and the datasource supports SQL.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• ExecutorNode.__call__() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.executor.node
  • SqlExecutorService.validate_request() in nl2sql.execution.executor.sql_executor

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with MISSING_SQL, MISSING_DATASOURCE_ID, or INVALID_STATE.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents invalid execution requests and ensures capability compatibility.

docs.title: Execution DAG Must Be Valid and Acyclic
Definition
docs.text: Post-combine ops must target known combine groups, all edges must reference existing nodes, and the DAG must be acyclic.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• build_execution_dag() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.dag, called by DecomposerNode.__call__()
  • ExecutionDAG._layered_toposort() in nl2sql.execution.dag

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError, leading to PipelineError with PLANNER_FAILED.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures deterministic and well-ordered aggregation execution.

docs.title: Aggregation Requires Scan Artifacts and Single-Input Post Nodes
Definition
docs.text: Scan nodes must have corresponding artifacts, and post-combine nodes must have exactly one input.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • AggregationService.execute() in nl2sql.aggregation.aggregator

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError when artifacts are missing or post nodes have invalid inputs.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Guarantees aggregation operates on complete, correctly wired inputs.

docs.title: An Engine Keeps Its Data Under storage.path
Definition
docs.text: storage is a required section of the config. An engine keeps its vector index in <storage.path>/index/, its schema snapshots, plan cache and feedback in <storage.path>/state.db, its traces in <storage.path>/traces/ and its result files in <storage.path>/results/. The index collection name is an internal constant.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• Config in nl2sql.config (the section is required)
  • Runtime.from_config() in nl2sql.runtime (StorePaths.under)

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A config without storage is a ConfigError from load_config, or a validation error building Config in code.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: There is no hidden default for where data lives, and two engines with different storage.path values never share a store.

docs.title: SQL Generation Enforces a Row Limit Cap
Definition
docs.text: Generated SQL must not exceed the row limit: the datasource adapter’s row_limit, bounded by the RESULT_ROW_LIMIT ceiling (100,000), which is also the limit when the datasource sets none. A result that reaches the limit is flagged as truncated. Verified SQL is held to the same limit, but a person's SQL is never rewritten: the executor stops reading its result at the limit (ExecutorRequest.max_rows).

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• GeneratorNode.__call__() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.generator.node
  • wrap_subgraph() in nl2sql.pipeline.graph_utils sets SubgraphOutput.truncated, which QueryResult and the answer carry
  • CuratedMatcherNode._run() sets max_rows and truncated for a verified query; _Stream in nl2sql.execution.executor.sql_executor stops at max_rows and closes the adapter's stream

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: No error; the limit is clamped to the smaller of the two. A cut result is flagged (truncated), and the answer says it was cut at N rows.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Protects execution resources and prevents runaway result sizes, without passing off a cut result as complete.

docs.title: The Answer Model Sees a Preview, Never the Whole Result
Definition
docs.text: The answer synthesizer's prompt carries at most ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS (20) rows of each result, with its total row count, its column names and a partial flag. The model is told to state only numbers from the preview or the count, and not to reproduce the result.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • result_preview() and AnswerSynthesizerNode._serialize_result() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.answer_synthesizer.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: None; rows past the preview are left out of the prompt.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: The prompt's size must not grow with the result: that is what kept the row limit at 1,000. The user sees the full result as a table, so the model has no need to copy it.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Pipeline execution must complete within settings.global_timeout_sec.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • run_with_graph() in nl2sql.pipeline.runtime

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with PIPELINE_TIMEOUT and a timeout response message.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures latency bounds and prevents hung requests.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Dependencies point in one direction: nl2sql-sdk → nothing, nl2sql.adapters.* → the SDK, nl2sql (the engine) → the SDK, and every caller — the REST API, the CLI, the playground — → the top-level nl2sql facade.

Concretely:

  • The SDK imports only pydantic and the standard library.
  • An adapter imports only the SDK, its driver, SQLAlchemy, sqlglot, pydantic and the standard library. SQLAlchemy and sqlglot are adapter-layer libraries: the shared connection layer, and the expression vocabulary the engine hands over to be rendered.
  • Nothing outside nl2sql/adapters/ imports an adapter, SQLAlchemy or a database driver. The engine reaches an adapter through the nl2sql.adapters entry points and DatasourceAdapterProtocol.
  • Nothing outside nl2sql/cli/ imports the CLI, and nl2sql.cli.demo never imports nl2sql.cli.commands.
  • nl2sql_api imports only the top-level nl2sql namespace, and so do the playground and nl2sql demo, apart from a named list of exceptions (STILL_IMPORTED_FROM_INSIDE: the provider catalogue in llm/providers.py, the hosted demo's per-request keys, and the demo's replay machinery and questions). In particular they never import nl2sql.feedback, nl2sql.tracing, nl2sql.pipeline, nl2sql.indexing or PROVIDER_PRESETS: engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about(), engine.index.inspect_defaults() and engine.llm.providers() serve them. The CLI, the playground and nl2sql_api reach the engine only through NL2SQL's public methods and namespaces, never the runtime behind them (engine._runtime, a namespace's _ctx).
  • The runtime (pipeline, execution, indexing, datasources, llm, auth, aggregation, schema, services, context, public_api) never imports nl2sql.evaluation or nl2sql.feedback at module scope. A deferred import inside a function is fine.
  • A provider's API-key environment variable is read in nl2sql/llm/ only. PROVIDER_PRESETS (llm/registry.py) is the one table; everything the CLI, the playground, evaluation and the REST API know about providers derives from it through llm/providers.py.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py — an AST import scan of packages/*/src, one test per rule
  • packages/api/tests/test_architecture.py — the REST API's own imports, and that its response model is nl2sql.QueryResult

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the rule and the file, line and import that broke it. Each documented exception is a named constant in the test module with the reason beside it.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Each rule keeps one thing replaceable. The SDK is what a third-party adapter compiles against, so a dependency there is a dependency every adapter author inherits; an adapter that imported the engine would close the circle and make the split meaningless. Engine code that imports an adapter, or SQLAlchemy, is a second way to reach a database that no new adapter can plug into. And import nl2sql loading nl2sql.evaluation cost every SDK user the YAML loaders, the gold dataset and the fake LLM before anyone asked a question.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The playground once read engine.context.ds_registry, engine.context.schema_store and engine.context.vector_store through getattr, so the schema view, the retrieval inspector and index health existed only in the playground; nl2sql-api had a placeholder where index status should be. The fix was facade methods that both callers use. Later the CLI's run, index and trace replay built on the runtime too; they now use stream_query's events, engine.index.build's IndexProgress callback and engine.traces.replay. The playground then still imported the feedback store, the trace reader, the pipeline's step list and the provider presets; those are engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about() and engine.llm.providers() now, which nl2sql feedback uses too. The rule stops the shortcut being taken again, which is what keeps a second client cheap.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
import nl2sql loads none of chromadb, onnxruntime, sqlalchemy, psycopg2, psycopg, pymysql, pyodbc, pymssql, duckdb, duckdb_engine, textual or opentelemetry, and its imports stay under 500 ms.

Concretely:

  • nl2sql/__init__.py imports only the NL2SQL class. Every other public name (QueryResult, QueryEvent, CancellationToken, the API classes, the benchmark) is imported the first time it is asked for, through the module's __getattr__. from nl2sql import QueryResult works as it always did.
  • nl2sql/public_api.py imports the runtime (Runtime and the API classes) inside NL2SQL.__init__, not at the top of the module.
  • Runtime modules import their heavy libraries where they are used, as the adapters already do.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• test_importing_nl2sql_loads_no_heavy_library in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py — imports nl2sql in a fresh interpreter and checks sys.modules
  • test_import_nl2sql_stays_within_its_time_budget in the same module — the cumulative figure python -X importtime reports for nl2sql, best of five, under 500 ms. It measures imports only, not wall-clock time, so a busy runner does not fail it.

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the heavy libraries that were loaded, or the import time against the budget.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Code that only needs a name — a type hint, nl2sql --help, a config check in CI, a REST client building a request — should not pay for a vector store, a database driver and a tracing stack. import nl2sql used to load chromadb, duckdb, opentelemetry, langgraph, langchain_openai and polars and took about 2.2 seconds; it now takes about 15 ms. The cost moves to NL2SQL(...), which needs the runtime anyway.

docs.title: An Engine Owns Its Config: No Process Globals
Definition
docs.text:
Everything an engine reads comes from its own Config, handed down through the runtime (ctx.settings, ctx.config) or passed as a parameter. Nothing is process-global, so two engines in one process share nothing.

Concretely:

  • There is no settings singleton. A module with no runtime takes the value it needs as a parameter (run_date(today), PlanCache(store, enabled=..., today=...)).
  • No module writes the process environment: no os.environ assignment, pop or update, no os.putenv. Keys and options travel in the Config. nl2sql demo --api-key and a key saved in the playground's settings panel are written to the demo's .env and given to the engine as a value in its LLM config, never put in os.environ; nl2sql demo --hosted refuses to start when a provider key variable is set rather than drop it.
  • The environment is read from an allow-list only: NL2SQL_CONFIG (nl2sql/config/), NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL (configure_logging), the provider key variables (nl2sql/llm/, through PROVIDER_PRESETS), ${env:VAR} references (nl2sql/config/ and the env secret provider), the trace redactor, which masks every value the environment holds, and CI in nl2sql benchmark. Anything else is configuration and is written in nl2sql.yaml, as ${env:VAR} where it should come from the environment.
  • Only the entry points load a .env file: the CLI, nl2sql demo and nl2sql-api call nl2sql.config.load_env_file(), which loads the .env next to nl2sql.yaml and never overrides a variable already set. It is the one place that calls load_dotenv. The library never reads a .env; a Python caller who wants one loads it before NL2SQL.from_config().
  • Runs that need different settings (evaluation, trace replay) take a run-scoped runtime with a derived config (ctx.derive(...)) instead of editing shared state.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• test_no_module_writes_the_environment, test_environment_reads_only_from_the_allow_list and test_only_entry_points_load_dotenv in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py, an AST scan of packages/*/src (READS_THE_ENVIRONMENT names each allowed reader and why); the first also scans scripts/, so a maintenance script passes keys as arguments instead of writing the environment
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/e2e/test_two_engines_fake_llm.py — two engines in one process, each with its own row limit, plan cache, LLM, embedder and storage, and os.environ unchanged afterwards

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the file, line and the write or read that broke the rule.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: 0.4 kept its settings in a process-global object that every module imported, and carried keys and options through os.environ. Two engines in one process (a test, a server with two configs, an evaluation run beside live traffic) then read each other's values, an evaluation that pinned a setting raced every other query, and a key set for one engine leaked into every other engine and child process.

docs.title: Dialect Knowledge Lives in the Adapter
Definition
docs.text: No engine module names a database dialect or writes one database's SQL. The plan says what; the adapter says how. An adapter declares its dialect with get_dialect(), which must return a name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts, and may override render_sql() for what sqlglot cannot express.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• test_no_dialect_name_outside_the_adapters and test_no_dialect_specific_sql_outside_the_adapters in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py — a scan of every non-docstring string literal, f-string chunks included
  • test_get_dialect_is_a_sqlglot_dialect, over every nl2sql.adapters entry point
  • The plan's one function vocabulary: ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.functions (see Plan Functions Are Known Functions)

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the literal and where it was written. The documented exceptions are the engine's own SQLite metadata store (schema/store.py, schema/sqlite_store.py), the in-process polars/DuckDB compute engine (aggregation/engines/polars_duckdb.py), and the plan's function allow-list.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: SQL that only one database understands, written in the engine, is wrong for every other database — and it is wrong silently, because it parses. A dialect name in engine code is worse: it is a switch statement that every future adapter has to be added to, in a repo whose point is that adapters are pluggable.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The planner prompt asked for STRFTIME('%Y', o.order_date) to get a year. On SQLite that works; on Postgres and SQL Server it is a call to a function that does not exist, and on MySQL it means something else. The fix was not to teach the prompt about dialects but to move the decision: the plan asks for DATE_PART('year', x), the generator builds a typed sqlglot node, and SQLiteAdapter.render_sql() rewrites it to STRFTIME for SQLite only. Related: get_dialect() returned SQLAlchemy's postgresql and mssql, which sqlglot rejects, so no SQL could be generated for either datasource — a one-word bug that the entry-point contract test now catches.

docs.title: The Validator Rejects Everything the Generator Can
Definition
docs.text: Anything the generator can refuse, the logical validator must refuse first. The validator is the last node with a retry edge back to the planner; the generator runs after it.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_logical_validator_generator_parity.py — each case asserts both halves: the generator rejects the plan, and so does the validator, with a retryable code
  • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A structural mistake is returned as a retryable PipelineError from the validator, so check_logical_validation sends the plan back to the refiner and the planner sees the message. The same mistake reaching the generator is a terminal SQL_GEN_FAILED.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: A check that lives only in the generator is a dead end rather than a retry. The model produced a fixable plan and got a hard failure, one node past the only gate that could have asked it to try again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The validator resolves columns against a throw-away query in which every table is CROSS JOINed — correct for column resolution, and deliberately blind to join topology. So a plan declaring three tables and joining only two validated CLEAN, then failed in the generator with "Table alias(es) t3 are declared in the plan but never joined to the FROM table." Three more join-shape mistakes behaved the same way. Every one is a pure function of plan.tables and plan.joins — no schema, no dialect — so each belongs in the validator, where the message reaches the planner.

docs.title: Verified SQL Is Human-Authored, Read-Only and Parameter-Bound
Definition
docs.text: A verified query's SQL is written, reviewed and committed by a person in curated.yaml. The model picks a verified query by id and supplies parameter values; it never writes or edits the SQL. The SQL must be exactly one read-only query whose :name placeholders are exactly its declared params. Values are typed and checked by code (type, min/max, choices, required) and bound by the adapter's driver, never interpolated into the SQL text. A query with params runs only on an adapter that declares SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• VerifiedQuery and ParamSpec in nl2sql.config.curated, and inspect_verified_sql() and check_curated_queries() in nl2sql.configs.curated, at startup, in nl2sql curated validate, and in nl2sql curated test (CuratedAPI.test()), which runs only queries that pass them, with their values bound
  • resolve_params() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.curated_matcher.params
  • CuratedMatcherNode._match() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.curated_matcher.node: parses the SQL read-only again before running, and checks the capability
  • BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter._run() in nl2sql.adapters.sqlalchemy_base.adapter: conn.execute(text(sql), parameters); without parameters the call is exactly conn.execute(text(sql))
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/sqlalchemy_base/test_bound_parameters.py: a value 1; DROP TABLE x is compared as a value and the table survives

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A broken file fails startup. At question time a bad value, a denied table, a missing capability or a failed run falls back to the generated pipeline with a reason code in the matcher's trace record; it is never an error of the run.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: The model emits a typed plan, never SQL holds on this path too: no model wrote the SQL, and a value cannot change what the query does.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
• State: Plan Model Is Strict and Read-Only; Context Requires Vector Store and Schema Store Configuration
  • Execution: SQL Execution Requires SQL, Datasource, and Capability; Execution DAG Must Be Valid and Acyclic; Aggregation Requires Scan Artifacts and Single-Input Post Nodes; Pipeline Execution Is Time-Bounded
  • Security: Policy Enforcement Is Namespaced and Fail-Closed; Datasource Access Is RBAC-Gated; Plan Model Is Strict and Read-Only; Verified SQL Is Human-Authored, Read-Only and Parameter-Bound
  • Determinism: Expected Schema Must Match Select List; Joins Must Be Valid and Schema-Backed
  • Resource bounds: SQL Generation Enforces a Row Limit Cap; The Answer Model Sees a Preview, Never the Whole Result; Context Requires Vector Store and Schema Store Configuration
  • Boundaries: Package Boundaries Are One-Way; Importing nl2sql Is Light; An Engine Owns Its Config: No Process Globals; Dialect Knowledge Lives in the Adapter
  • Retryability: The Validator Rejects Everything the Generator Can; Plan Functions Are Known Functions

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Column existence enforcement degrades to warnings when settings.pipeline.strict_columns is turned off (it is on by default), so missing columns then do not always block execution.
  • Schema version mismatch handling is policy-driven and may only emit warnings (e.g., settings.schema.version_mismatch: warn), so mismatch is not always enforced as a hard failure.
  • Semantic-only checks are pattern based: they block a field that opens with SELECT ... FROM, a statement terminator and comment markers, rather than parsing for every possible SQL construct. An intent that literally reads "select ... from ..." is rejected as SQL.
  • If the vector store is unavailable, datasource resolution can return a response without errors, relying on downstream stages to detect missing candidates.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: NL2SQL is a multi-stage orchestration pipeline built on LangGraph. A single request flows through control-plane nodes (resolution, decomposition, planning), capability-driven subgraphs (SQL agents), and an aggregation layer. The system is wired by Runtime, which instantiates registries, stores, and policy enforcement.

docs.title: Key runtime components
docs.text:
• Runtime initializes registries, stores, and policy enforcement.
  • build_graph() compiles the LangGraph control-plane pipeline.
  • run_with_graph() executes the pipeline with cancellation and timeout.
  • GraphState is the shared mutable state across pipeline nodes (see graph_state.md).

docs.title: System topology
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    UserQuery[User Query] --> Runtime[run_with_graph()]
    Runtime --> Graph[build_graph()]
    Graph --> Resolver[DatasourceResolverNode]
    Resolver --> Decomposer[DecomposerNode]
    Decomposer --> Router[Scan Layer Router]
    Router --> Subgraph[SQL Agent Subgraph]
    Subgraph --> Router
    Router --> Aggregator[EngineAggregatorNode]
    Aggregator --> Synthesizer[AnswerSynthesizerNode]

    subgraph Context[Runtime]
        DS[DatasourceRegistry]
        LLM[LLMRegistry]
        VS[VectorStore]
        SS[SchemaStore]
        RBAC[RBAC]
        AS[ArtifactStore]
    end

docs.title: Subsystem architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    User[User Query]
    Planner[Planner/Decomposer]
    Schema[Schema Store]
    Retrieval[Chunking + Retrieval]
    Validator[Validation Layer]
    Execution[Execution Layer]
    Adapter[Adapter/Plugin Backend]
    Artifacts[Artifact Store]
    Obs[Observability]

    User --> Planner
    Planner --> Retrieval
    Retrieval --> Schema
    Planner --> Validator
    Validator --> Execution
    Execution --> Adapter
    Execution --> Artifacts
    Planner --> Obs
    Execution --> Obs

docs.title: Major subsystems (and responsibilities)
docs.text:
• Planner / Decomposer: DecomposerNode produces stable, semantically-scoped sub-queries and, from them, a deterministic ExecutionDAG.
  • Schema Store: SchemaStore persists versioned schema snapshots with fingerprints.
  • Chunking + Retrieval: SchemaChunkBuilder produces typed chunks; VectorStore provides staged retrieval for routing and planning context.
  • Validation layer: LogicalValidatorNode enforces schema correctness and RBAC.
  • Execution layer: ExecutorNode routes to capability-driven executor services (e.g., SQL executor).
  • Adapter / Plugin backend: adapters implement DatasourceAdapterProtocol and are discovered via entry points.
  • Artifact store: executor results are persisted as Parquet artifacts and referenced by ArtifactRef.
  • Observability: structured logs, OpenTelemetry metrics, and audit events.

docs.title: End-to-end flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User
    participant Runtime as run_with_graph
    participant Resolver as DatasourceResolverNode
    participant Decomposer as DecomposerNode
    participant Router as Scan Layer Router
    participant Subgraph as SQL Agent Subgraph
    participant Agg as EngineAggregatorNode
    participant Synth as AnswerSynthesizerNode

    User->>Runtime: user_query
    Runtime->>Resolver: GraphState
    Resolver->>Decomposer: resolved datasources
    Decomposer->>Router: ExecutionDAG over the sub-queries
    Router->>Subgraph: Send(sub_query)
    Subgraph-->>Router: ArtifactRef + diagnostics
    Router->>Agg: all scan artifacts
    Agg->>Synth: aggregated rows
    Synth-->>Runtime: final_answer + errors
