docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Retrieves schema context for a sub‑query using staged vector search and authoritative snapshots.
  • Exists to constrain planning to relevant tables/columns while remaining schema‑grounded.
  • Sits at the entry of the SQL agent subgraph.
  • Class: SchemaRetrieverNode
  • Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Build a semantic query from sub‑query intent, filters, group_by, expected_schema, metrics.
  • Retrieve candidate tables/columns/relationships from VectorStore.
  • Resolve authoritative tables from SchemaStore.
  • Fall back to full schema snapshot when retrieval returns no candidates.
  • Rank the datasource's preferred_tables first and set preferred=True on them, on the full-snapshot path and the retrieval path; see Preferred tables.
  • Strip column statistics (sample_values, min_value, max_value, distinct_count, null_percentage) from every table the caller's role cannot read, on every path, while keeping its name, columns, types, keys and relationships ("structure yes, data no"). The rule is RBAC's table_allowed, the one the logical validator refuses with; with no RBAC in the context, every table is stripped. See Security Model.
  • The tables it returns keep every statistic, but the planner and refiner prompts render them with render_schema_for_prompt (schema.py), which sends only sample_values and, for date, time and numeric columns other than keys, a range of [min_value, max_value]. See AST Planner: prompt layout.

docs.title: Internal Flow (Step-by-Step)
docs.text:
1. Build semantic query with _build_semantic_query().
  2. Retrieve table/metric chunks via retrieve_schema_context().
  3. If no table chunks, retrieve columns via retrieve_column_candidates().
  4. If tables are identified, retrieve columns/relationships via retrieve_planning_context().
  5. Resolve schema snapshot via _resolve_snapshot().
  6. Build Table objects with _build_tables_from_snapshot().
  7. If no tables were found, return full snapshot with warning.
  8. On exception, log error and return empty relevant_tables.

docs.title: Preferred tables
docs.text:
A datasource's preferred_tables (in datasources.yaml, see Datasources) are matched against snapshot tables by bare name or schema.table, case ignored.

  • Full snapshot: every preferred table is in the list, first.
  • Retrieval: preferred tables the tables search picked come first. A preferred table the search scored but did not pick is added (before the planning search, so its columns and relationships are fetched too) when its similarity is at least the least similar pick's minus PREFERRED_MARGIN (0.05).
  • Each preferred Table has preferred=True. render_schema_for_prompt sorts preferred tables first, then by name, and prints "preferred":true on them only; with no preferred tables the block is byte-identical to before. Planner instruction 14 tells the model to plan against a preferred table when it answers the question.
  • RBAC is unchanged: a preferred table the role cannot read is ranked and marked, and loses its statistics like any other unreadable table.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Purpose: orchestrates the end-to-end NL2SQL pipeline as a LangGraph state machine.
  • Why it exists architecturally: central control plane that wires global nodes, subgraphs, and aggregation into a single execution DAG.
  • When it is invoked: via run_with_graph() runtime entry point.

Defining function: build_graph() Source file path: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/graph.py

docs.title: Boundary Definition
docs.text: This graph is the top-level orchestrator. It encapsulates datasource resolution, decomposition (which builds the execution DAG), routing to subgraphs, aggregation, and answer synthesis. It does NOT implement subgraph internals (SQL planning/execution), per-node business logic, or adapter-specific execution; those are delegated to nodes and registered subgraphs.

docs.title: Entry Conditions
docs.text:
Required state: - GraphState.user_query must be provided. - GraphState.trace_id is auto-generated if not provided.

Preconditions: - Runtime must be initialized with registries/services used by nodes (vector store, LLM registry, datasource registry, schema store, RBAC).

Triggering parent graph: - None. This is the root graph invoked by run_with_graph() in pipeline/runtime.py.

docs.title: Exit Conditions
docs.text:
Successful completion criteria: - Reaches END after answer_synthesizer when aggregation and synthesis finish without fatal interruptions.

Failure exits: - datasource_resolver can short-circuit to END via resolver_route when no datasource is resolved/allowed, or when its answerability check refuses the question (QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE); no other LLM call runs. - layer_router can return END if no execution_dag or layers are present. - layer_router returns END once every scan has run if none produced an artifact (every sub-query was denied or failed), and whenever the graph was built with execute=False. The aggregator and answer synthesizer are skipped, so the run's errors are the sub-queries' own -- for a policy denial, SECURITY_VIOLATION first -- and no LLM call is spent explaining an empty result. - layer_router raises PipelineExecutionError (an NL2SQLError carrying the PipelineError payload on .error) when no compatible subgraph exists for a datasource; this propagates as an exception from the router function. A conditional-edge router may only return routing decisions, so it cannot report the failure as a PipelineError value in state the way a node does.

Partial completion behavior: - If routing cannot schedule any scan-layer work but execution_dag exists and at least one scan produced an artifact, it routes to aggregator directly. If some scans produced artifacts and others did not, the aggregator still runs and reports the missing ones as AGGREGATOR_FAILED. - Errors added to GraphState.errors do not automatically stop the graph; the graph relies on routing logic and node behavior for termination. - aggregator_route ends the run when the aggregator failed (AggregatorResponse.errors is not empty), so the answer synthesizer never spends a model call on an empty result and AGGREGATOR_FAILED is the run's outcome.

docs.title: Internal Node Composition
docs.text:
Execution order (nominal path): - curated_matcher — CuratedMatcherNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/curated_matcher/node.py — only when curated answers are configured and the run executes: answer with a verified query (curated_route → verified → layer_router), or fall back (generated → datasource_resolver). Without curated answers the node is not in the graph and datasource_resolver is the entry point. - datasource_resolver — DatasourceResolverNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/datasource_resolver/node.py — resolve candidate datasources, RBAC, and the answerability check (an LLM call). - decomposer — DecomposerNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/decomposer/node.py — decompose query into sub-queries, and build the ExecutionDAG from them (decomposer/dag.py). - layer_router — inline lambda + routes.build_scan_layer_router — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/routes.py — route each scan layer to a subgraph or aggregator. - <subgraph nodes> — via wrap_subgraph() — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/graph_utils.py — invoke registered subgraphs per scan node. - aggregator — EngineAggregatorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/aggregator/node.py — execute aggregation DAG. - answer_synthesizer — AnswerSynthesizerNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/answer_synthesizer/node.py — produce final answer.

Mermaid diagram (main pipeline only): 

flowchart TD
    curated_matcher -.->|verified| layer_router
    curated_matcher -.->|generated| datasource_resolver
    datasource_resolver -->|continue| decomposer
    datasource_resolver -->|end| END
    decomposer --> layer_router
    layer_router -->|subgraph| subgraph_exec
    subgraph_exec --> layer_router
    layer_router -->|aggregator| aggregator
    layer_router -->|end| END
    aggregator -->|ok| answer_synthesizer --> END
    aggregator -->|failed| END

The dotted edges exist only when curated answers are configured.

docs.title: State Contract
docs.text:
State model: GraphState (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/state.py).

Field ownership, reducers, and lifecycle are defined in ../graph_state.md.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Execution Flow
docs.text:
1. With curated answers configured, curated_matcher runs first. On a verified hit it has already run the query and filled decomposer_response, execution_dag, artifact_refs and subgraph_outputs as for one sub-query, so layer_router finds the scan done and goes straight to step 7. Any fallback continues at step 1 with nothing in the state changed.
  2. datasource_resolver resolves candidate datasources (vector search only when more than one datasource is registered), filters them by RBAC, then asks the LLM whether any allowed datasource can answer the question.
  3. resolver_route decides:
  4. continue if allowed datasources exist and the question was judged answerable.
  5. end if none exist, the question is not answerable, or the response is missing.
  6. decomposer uses the LLM to produce SubQuery objects and combine groups, then builds a deterministic ExecutionDAG from them in code. The DAG is a pure function of that output, so it is not a node of its own; a DAG that cannot be built is reported as PLANNER_FAILED and the run ends at the router.
  7. layer_router inspects the DAG and current artifact_refs:
  8. If no DAG or layers, returns END.
  9. If next scan layer is empty, routes to aggregator -- or to END when no scan produced an artifact or execute is False.
  10. For each scan node, resolves a compatible subgraph and sends build_scan_payload.
  11. Each subgraph execution returns artifact_refs, subgraph_outputs, and errors to GraphState.
  12. layer_router is re-entered until all scan-layer nodes produce artifacts.
  13. aggregator executes the DAG using the stored artifact_refs.
  14. aggregator_route ends the run if aggregation failed; otherwise answer_synthesizer summarizes aggregated results into a final answer.
  15. Graph reaches END.

docs.title: Determinism Guarantees
docs.text: Determinism guarantees and non-determinism sources are documented in ../determinism.md.

docs.title: Error Propagation
docs.text: Failure domains, retry scope, and recovery limitations are centralized in ../failure_recovery.md.

docs.title: Retry + Recovery
docs.text: See ../failure_recovery.md for retry scope and recovery behavior.

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
• Blocking calls include LLM requests in datasource_resolver, decomposer and answer_synthesizer.
  • The decomposer's DAG construction and the aggregator are CPU-bound.
  • Subgraph executions are dispatched per scan layer and can run in parallel via LangGraph routing.
  • Overall pipeline is executed on a single-worker thread pool created per run and guarded by settings.pipeline.timeout_s.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
• Each node uses nl2sql.common.logger.get_logger() with node-specific names.
  • GraphState.trace_id is propagated into subgraph IDs and executor requests, but no code binds it into logging context (trace_context is defined but not used).
  • run_with_graph() accepts LangGraph callbacks via config={"callbacks": callbacks}.
  • No explicit metrics or tracing spans are emitted in the graph code.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• settings.pipeline.timeout_s (default 60) controls total pipeline timeout. It is read from the runtime (ctx.settings), as is every setting the nodes use.
  • Subgraph selection is governed by datasource capabilities in the subgraph registry.

docs.title: Extension Points
docs.text:
• Add new subgraphs by constructing them in build_graph() and extending resolve_subgraph() with their required capabilities.
  • Insert additional nodes in build_graph() by adding nodes/edges to the StateGraph.
  • Customize routing by replacing build_scan_layer_router() or resolver_route().

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• execute=False in build_graph() makes layer_router return END instead of dispatching the aggregator, and is passed to the SQL agent subgraph.
  • Errors accumulated in GraphState.errors do not alter routing unless explicit routes inspect them.
  • No trace/span propagation into logging context, despite trace context helpers existing.
  • Merge reducers for artifact_refs/subgraph_outputs overwrite on key conflicts without ordering guarantees.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Purpose: plan, validate, generate, and execute SQL for a single sub-query.
  • Why it exists architecturally: isolates SQL-capable execution into a reusable subgraph that can be scheduled per scan node in the global execution DAG.
  • When it is invoked: when layer_router resolves a datasource with SUPPORTS_SQL capability and sends a scan-layer payload.

Defining function: build_sql_agent_graph() Source file path: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/sql_agent.py

docs.title: Boundary Definition
docs.text: This subgraph encapsulates the SQL planning and execution loop for a single SubQuery. It does NOT perform cross-subquery aggregation, answer synthesis, or datasource resolution; those responsibilities are owned by the main pipeline graph and upstream nodes.

docs.title: Entry Conditions
docs.text:
Required state: - SubgraphExecutionState.trace_id - SubgraphExecutionState.sub_query (must include id, datasource_id, and intent)

Preconditions: - sub_query.datasource_id must map to a registered adapter/executor. - Schema store and vector store may be used if configured; otherwise schema retrieval falls back to full schema snapshot.

Triggering parent graph: - layer_router in the main pipeline graph sends build_scan_payload() to the subgraph via wrap_subgraph().

docs.title: Exit Conditions
docs.text:
Successful completion criteria: - Reaches END after executor and produces executor_response.

Failure exits: - check_planner returns end when planner output is missing and retries are exhausted or errors are non-retryable. - check_logical_validation returns end when validation errors are non-retryable or retries are exhausted. - check_execution returns end after executor unless the database rejected the query as wrong (EXECUTION_FAILED) and retries remain: a success, a refusal (DB_EXECUTION_ERROR: permission, timeout, connection) and any other executor error all end the subgraph. - Cancellation forces end in router checks and in the retry handler. The run's CancellationToken is read from the RunnableConfig (configurable.cancellation_token); when no token is present the subgraph behaves as not cancelled.

Partial completion behavior: - If planner or logical validation errors are retryable and retry budget remains, execution loops via retry_handler → refiner → ast_planner. - So does a query the database rejected as wrong (an unknown column or table, a type mismatch, bad syntax): the adapter marks the error retryable and the executor reports it as EXECUTION_FAILED, with the database's own first line as the message.

docs.title: Internal Node Composition
docs.text:
Execution order (nominal path): - schema_retriever — SchemaRetrieverNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py — retrieve relevant schema tables/columns. - ast_planner — ASTPlannerNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/ast_planner/node.py — create SQL AST plan. - logical_validator — LogicalValidatorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/validator/node.py — validate plan correctness and policy constraints. - generator — GeneratorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/generator/node.py — generate SQL text from AST. - executor — ExecutorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/executor/node.py — execute SQL and produce artifacts. - retry_handler — retry_node() — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/sql_agent.py — apply exponential backoff and increment retry count. - refiner — RefinerNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/refiner/node.py — generate feedback for the planner.

Mermaid diagram (sql_agent only): 

flowchart TD
    schema_retriever --> ast_planner
    ast_planner -->|ok| logical_validator
    ast_planner -->|retry| retry_handler
    ast_planner -->|end| END
    logical_validator -->|ok| generator
    logical_validator -->|retry| retry_handler
    logical_validator -->|end| END
    retry_handler --> refiner --> ast_planner
    generator --> executor
    executor -->|retry| retry_handler
    executor -->|end| END

docs.title: State Contract
docs.text:
State model: SubgraphExecutionState (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/state.py).

Field ownership, reducers, and lifecycle are defined in ../graph_state.md.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Execution Flow
docs.text:
1. schema_retriever builds a semantic query from sub_query and retrieves relevant schema context; if none found, it falls back to full schema snapshot.
  2. ast_planner runs an LLM planning chain to produce PlanModel.
  3. check_planner routes:
  4. ok if a plan exists.
  5. retry if errors are retryable and retry budget remains.
  6. end if errors are non-retryable or retries exhausted.
  7. logical_validator validates the plan for structural and policy compliance.
  8. check_logical_validation routes:
  9. ok when no blocking errors exist.
  10. retry when retryable errors exist and retry budget remains.
  11. end when errors are non-retryable or retries exhausted.
  12. generator converts the plan to SQL for the target datasource dialect.
  13. executor runs SQL via the datasource adapter and returns artifacts/errors. check_execution routes retry when every executor error is a retryable EXECUTION_FAILED and retry budget remains, otherwise end. It also routes retry when the query returned no rows on a filter value the column does not have but a close one exists (VALUE_NOT_FOUND ERROR, raised once per sub-query; see ExecutorNode).
  14. If routed to retry: retry_handler waits with exponential backoff and jitter, then increments retry_count.
  15. refiner uses LLM feedback to enrich error context, then loops back to ast_planner. Both are told about the latest attempt only, as {node, error_code, message} (nl2sql.pipeline.retry_feedback): never an earlier attempt's errors again, never a stack trace or details.
  16. Subgraph terminates at END.

docs.title: Determinism Guarantees
docs.text: Determinism guarantees and non-determinism sources are documented in ../determinism.md.

docs.title: Error Propagation
docs.text: Failure domains, retry scope, and recovery limitations are centralized in ../failure_recovery.md.

docs.title: Retry + Recovery
docs.text: See ../failure_recovery.md for retry scope and recovery behavior.

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
• Blocking LLM calls: ASTPlannerNode and RefinerNode.
  • External I/O: vector store retrieval and schema store access in SchemaRetrieverNode; datasource execution in ExecutorNode.
  • CPU-bound steps: SQL generation via sqlglot in GeneratorNode.
  • Retry loop introduces sleep-based delays on failures.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
• Node-specific loggers are used (schema_retriever, planner, logical_validator, generator, executor, refiner).
  • trace_id is stored in state and forwarded to executor requests; logging context is not explicitly set.
  • No explicit metrics or tracing spans are emitted by the subgraph code.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Read from the runtime's settings.pipeline.retries when the subgraph is built:

  • max (default 3)
  • base_delay_s (default 1.0)
  • max_delay_s (default 10.0)
  • jitter_s (default 0.5)

docs.title: Extension Points
docs.text:
• Modify build_sql_agent_graph() to insert, remove, or rewire nodes and edges.
  • Add new subgraphs by constructing them in build_graph() and extending resolve_subgraph() with their required capabilities.
  • Replace node implementations via dependency injection in Runtime.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Generator errors are not routed into the retry loop; a failure proceeds to executor, which reports MISSING_SQL, and terminates at END.
  • No subgraph-specific metrics or trace spans are emitted.
  • The executor retries only what the adapter marks retryable. An adapter that raises instead of returning a failed ResultFrame ends the sub-query with EXECUTOR_CRASH.

Because the generator has no retry edge, the invariant the loop depends on is that logical_validator rejects every plan generator would refuse to build. LogicalValidatorNode._validate_buildable() enforces it by running the generator's own _build_query() — see Buildability. Without it, a plan whose tables are not joined reached generator and ended the sub-query with a terminal SQL_GEN_FAILED.

docs.title: REST API (api)
docs.text:
The api section of nl2sql.yaml holds nl2sql-api's own settings. It is optional. The engine validates it like every other section (strict keys, ${env:...} references) and never reads it; nl2sql-api reads engine.config.api.

# nl2sql.yaml
api: { file: api.yaml }

# api.yaml
role_header: X-NL2SQL-Role      # a header a trusted proxy sets on every request
role: null                      # or one static role for every request
trust_body_role: false          # accept "role" in the request body (dev only)
cors_origins: [https://app.example.com]
Field Default Meaning role_header none The header a trusted, authenticating proxy sets with the caller's roles (comma-separated). Only configure it when the proxy overwrites that header on every request, or any client can pick its own role. role none One static role for every request, used when no header carries one. trust_body_role false Dev only: take user_context from the request body. Any client can then choose any role; the API logs a warning at startup. cors_origins [] Browser origins allowed to call the API. Empty, no cross-origin request is allowed.

The role sources are tried in that order: the header, then the static role, then the body (only with trust_body_role). A request with no role is a 401. See Caller role.

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text:
The routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index need one of the roles in policies.admin_roles (default [admin]), which is a policy, so it lives in the policies section, not here. A request with another role is a 403.

Without any role source (role_header, role and trust_body_role all unset), admin routes answer loopback clients only, so a fresh local install still works and a published port does not hand out admin. See Admin routes.

docs.title: Starting nl2sql-api
docs.text:
nl2sql-api builds its engine from NL2SQL_CONFIG (else ./nl2sql.yaml), after loading the .env next to that file without overriding a variable already set. It calls engine.check() before it accepts requests: a required datasource that fails, or datasources configured and none ready, stops it with EngineNotReady; an optional one that fails leaves it serving the others. See Startup.

NL2SQL_CONFIG=/etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml uvicorn nl2sql_api.main:app

The NL2SQL_API_* variables of 0.4 are not read; see From 0.4.

docs.title: Curated Answers (curated.yaml)
docs.text:
The curated section of nl2sql.yaml, usually its own curated.yaml, is where a data team writes verified queries: SQL they have already written and reviewed, with typed parameters, and the questions each query answers.

What works today

The section is loaded and checked (at startup and with nl2sql curated validate), every query can be run once with nl2sql curated test, its questions are indexed with nl2sql index, a question is matched to a verified query and answered by it (see What happens at question time), and the playground badges such an answer Verified. The demo ships six verified queries (In the demo). Preferred tables (below) and proposals from thumbs-up feedback (From feedback to verified queries) are built too. Business metrics are parsed but not used yet.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
curated: { file: curated.yaml }

The section is optional. Present, curated answers are on; absent, they are off, and nothing else changes. To turn them off, remove the line from nl2sql.yaml (the file can stay). A file: that does not exist is an error, and so is a section that is broken: building the engine (NL2SQL(config), nl2sql run, the REST API, the playground) fails with a ConfigError that names every problem, as a broken datasource does.

The matching knobs are in the settings section:

Setting Default Meaning settings.curated.match_top_k 5 Verified query candidates a question's search returns and the model is shown, one per query. settings.curated.match_floor 0.6 Cosine similarity the best candidate must reach before the model is asked to choose one. Below it the question is answered as if there were no curated section, with no model call. Calibrated on the local embedding model; see the design.

docs.title: Writing the file
docs.text:
One section covers every datasource, keyed by the datasource id. This is one of the demo's verified queries (nl2sql init --demo writes all six):

# curated.yaml
datasources:
  chinook:
    verified_queries:
      - id: top_customers_by_revenue
        description: "Customers ranked by invoiced revenue in a calendar year"
        questions:
          - "Who are our top {n} customers by revenue in {year}?"
          - "Best {n} customers in {year}"
        params:
          n:    { type: int, default: 10, min: 1, max: 100 }
          year: { type: int, min: 2000, max: 2100, example: 2012 }
        sql: |
          SELECT c.CustomerId,
                 c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS customer,
                 c.Country,
                 ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS revenue
          FROM Customer c
          JOIN Invoice i      ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
          JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
          WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) = :year
          GROUP BY c.CustomerId, customer, c.Country
          ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.CustomerId
          LIMIT :n
    metrics: []

docs.title: A verified query
docs.text: Key Required Meaning id yes A slug: lower-case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. Unique within its datasource. description yes What the query returns, in a sentence. questions yes, at least one Phrasings the query answers. {name} marks where a parameter goes. params no The parameters, by name. sql yes The query, in the datasource's own SQL dialect.

docs.title: A parameter
docs.text: Key Meaning type int, float, string or date (YYYY-MM-DD). default The value used when the question gives none. A param with no default is required. min, max Bounds, for int, float and date. choices The allowed values, for string. example A typical value, used where a value is needed and there is no default.

docs.title: The SQL
docs.text:
• Write it in the dialect of the datasource it belongs to: the SQLite example above uses strftime, a Postgres datasource would use EXTRACT. It is parsed with the dialect the datasource's adapter declares.
  • Exactly one statement, and a query: a SELECT, a set operation such as UNION, or a WITH around one. No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, CREATE, DROP, ALTER, SELECT ... INTO or statements the parser cannot type (VACUUM, PRAGMA), anywhere in the tree, a CTE included.
  • Parameters are :name placeholders, and they are exactly the declared params: no placeholder without a param, no param the SQL does not use. Positional ? placeholders are refused. Values are always bound, never pasted into the text, so a value cannot change the shape of the query.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
metrics: (a list of name, description, expression, table) is accepted and checked for shape so the format is fixed, but nothing uses it yet.

Every key is checked: a misspelt one (descripton:) is an error, not ignored.

docs.title: Checking the file
docs.text:
nl2sql curated validate                              # ./nl2sql.yaml, or NL2SQL_CONFIG
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml curated validate

Building the engine runs every startup check; a section that fails one exits 1 with the ConfigError. The command then adds the one that needs the index: every table a query reads (CTE names aside) is in its datasource's latest indexed schema, compared case-insensitively. A datasource that has not been indexed yet is skipped for that check, with a note. The command prints a table, one row per query, and exits 1 on any error, so it can run in CI:

                         Verified Queries
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Datasource ┃ Query                    ┃ Status ┃ Details                            ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ chinook    │ top_customers_by_revenue │ OK     │ Verified against the indexed schema │
└────────────┴──────────────────────────┴────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
Check At startup curated validate YAML parses and every key is known yes yes Every datasource key is a configured datasource yes yes Query ids unique within a datasource yes yes Every {placeholder} in a question is a param, every param is in a question yes yes Defaults, examples, bounds and choices agree with the type yes yes SQL is one read-only query in the datasource's dialect yes yes SQL :name placeholders are exactly the params yes yes Tables the SQL reads are in the indexed schema no yes, when indexed

From Python, the same check is engine.curated, on the engine's own config:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
report = engine.curated.validate()
if not report.ok:
    for error in report.errors:
        print(error)
    for entry in report.entries:
        print(entry.datasource_id, entry.query_id, entry.status, entry.details)

docs.title: Testing the queries
docs.text:
validate reads the SQL; it does not run it, so a column renamed under a query passes it. nl2sql curated test runs every verified query once against its database:

nl2sql curated test
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml curated test

It reads the same config as validate. Each param is bound to its default, else its example; a param with neither fails its query without running it, so give every required param an example. A query that fails the static checks (not read-only, placeholders that do not match the params) is never run. The rest run read-only through their datasource's adapter, the same path a matched question takes, with the values bound and only the first batch of rows fetched. It prints one row per query and exits 1 if any fails, so it can run in CI after a schema change:

                                     Verified Queries
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Datasource ┃ Query                    ┃ Status ┃ Params          ┃ Details                                      ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ chinook    │ top_customers_by_revenue │ PASS   │ n=10, year=2012 │ 10 rows in 0.00 s                            │
│ chinook    │ revenue_by_year          │ FAIL   │                 │ The database rejected the query: no such     │
│            │                          │        │                 │ column: Total                                │
└────────────┴──────────────────────────┴────────┴─────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

From Python it is engine.curated.test(), which returns a report like validate()'s: ok, errors, and one entry per query with its status (PASS or FAIL), params, row_count and details.

docs.title: Indexing the questions
docs.text:
nl2sql index embeds every phrasing of every verified query, and its description, beside the datasource's schema entries. Placeholders are filled first with the param's example, else its default: "Best {n} customers in {year}" is indexed as "Best 10 customers in 2012". The SQL is never indexed.

After editing the curated section, re-index its questions:

nl2sql index --curated-only                       # every datasource
nl2sql index --curated-only --datasource chinook  # one

--curated-only keeps each datasource's schema entries exactly as they are and embeds only the verified queries: it reads no schema and makes no enrichment model call, so it takes seconds. The datasource must have been indexed once with plain nl2sql index. A plain nl2sql index also picks up the file, and a schema re-index always keeps the verified queries.

Until you re-index, nl2sql doctor and the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index/status) warn:

Warning: curated.yaml changed for 'chinook' since it was indexed; run `nl2sql index --curated-only --datasource chinook`.

It is a warning, not a failure: the index stays ok, because the stale entries still name queries that exist.

docs.title: What happens at question time
docs.text:
With the file loaded and at least one verified query in it, every question that executes starts at the curated matcher (node reference):

  1. It searches the indexed phrasings of the verified queries of the datasources the caller's role may read (only the pinned datasource when a request names one), and keeps the best settings.curated.match_top_k queries.
  2. If the best one's similarity is below settings.curated.match_floor, the question goes to the normal pipeline. No model call is made.
  3. Otherwise one model call sees those candidates: each one's datasource.id, description and params (type, bounds, choices, default). Never the SQL. The model picks the one that answers the whole question and gives its parameter values, or answers none_of_these.
  4. Code checks the values against the param specs. A param the question does not give takes its default; a required one missing, or a value out of bounds, sends the question to the normal pipeline.
  5. Every table the SQL reads must be allowed for the role by the policies section. If one is not, the question goes to the normal pipeline, which refuses it the way it always does. The user is never told a verified query exists.
  6. The SQL runs with the values bound by the driver, through the same executor as generated SQL. The row limit is the datasource's row_limit (capped by settings.results.row_limit): the executor stops reading there and marks the result cut, rather than adding a LIMIT to your SQL. The result is saved, paged and exported like any other, and the answer is written from it, told what the numbers mean by the query's description.

A verified answer costs two model calls (the choice and the answer). When anything above does not hold, the run continues as if there were no curated section, and the answer is generated.

Every answer says where it came from, in QueryResult.source (and the REST response):

{"type": "verified", "id": "top_customers_by_revenue", "datasource_id": "chinook", "params": {"n": 5, "year": 2012}}

or {"type": "generated", ...} with the other fields null. The sub-query of a verified answer has plan_source: "verified", its sql is your SQL with its :name placeholders, and its plan is null.

In the playground a verified answer carries a green Verified · top_customers_by_revenue label beside the question, with the bound values in its tooltip. The Plan station says no plan was written and lists the query and its values, the Checks station shows the matcher's three checks (read-only, params, role), and the SQL station shows your SQL as Verified SQL, with its placeholders. A generated answer looks as it always has.

Why a question was not matched is in the run trace: the curated_matcher node's curated_match record lists the candidates and their similarities, the floor, the model's choice and reason, the checked values, and one reason code: not_configured, no_candidates, below_floor, none_of_these, model_failed, unknown_query, param_invalid, param_missing, policy_denied, capability_missing or execution_failed. A verified query that fails to run also adds a warning to the result.

The model for the choice is the curated_matcher agent in the llm section, falling back to the top level.

Parameters are bound by the datasource's adapter. Every built-in adapter binds them; a third-party adapter has to declare SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS (SDK), and a verified query with params on one that does not is never run (capability_missing).

docs.title: In the demo
docs.text:
nl2sql init --demo (which nl2sql demo runs the first time) writes curated.yaml with six verified queries on Chinook and includes it from nl2sql.yaml; nl2sql demo indexes their questions with the schema:

Query One of its phrasings Params top_customers_by_revenue "Who are our top {n} customers by revenue in {year}?" n (default 10), year (example 2012) revenue_by_year "What is the total revenue per year?" none monthly_revenue "What was the monthly revenue in {year}?" year (example 2013) sales_by_country "What are total sales by country?" none best_selling_genres "Which genre sells the most tracks?" n (default 5) top_artists_by_tracks_sold "Who are the top {n} artists by tracks sold?" n (default 10)

Two of the guided questions, "What is the total revenue per year?" and "Which genre sells the most tracks?", are phrasings of these, so with a key they come back verified. Check and run them with nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml curated validate and nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml curated test.

The keyless demo (a hosted Space with no key, or nl2sql demo replaying recordings) answers from recorded model answers, and those include the matcher's VerifiedQueryChoice for every guided question. So without a key, "What is the total revenue per year?", "Which genre sells the most tracks?", "How many customers do we have, by country?" and "How many purchases were there per month in 2013?" come back verified, and the rest generated.

docs.title: Preferred tables
docs.text: Preferred tables are not in the curated section: they are a preferred_tables list on a datasource, naming views or tables (built by the data team, never by the package) the planner should reach for first. See Datasources: preferred tables.

docs.title: From feedback to verified queries
docs.text:
A thumbs-up on a generated answer in the playground is a candidate verified query: a real question, and SQL a person said was right. Export them as proposals and review them like any other change to the curated section:

nl2sql curated proposals export                                   # print to stdout
nl2sql curated proposals export --out curated.proposals.yaml

Each proposal is an entry in the curated section's shape, under the datasource the run used:

datasources:
  chinook:
    verified_queries:
    - id: how_many_customers_are_in_brazil
      description: 'TODO: say what this query returns.'
      questions:
      - How many customers are in Brazil?
      sql: |
        SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM Customer WHERE Country = 'Brazil'
  • id comes from the question: lower case, words joined by _, at most 60 characters, q_ in front when it would start with a digit, and _2, _3 after it when two questions give the same id.
  • questions holds the question as it was asked, as the one phrasing.
  • sql is the run's generated SQL, exactly as it ran. Every value in it is literal ('Brazil' above): the proposal has no params.
  • description is a placeholder.

The same question (ignoring case and spacing) on the same datasource is proposed once, from its newest thumbs-up. These are skipped, and counted by reason in the command's summary: thumbs-down ratings, answers that came from a verified query already, runs that did not succeed, runs with no SQL or more than one statement, runs on more than one datasource, and ratings recorded before the feedback table kept the datasource (see Feedback and Signals).

Reviewing is the approval. There is no approved state and no queue: a person reads each entry, checks the SQL answers the question, writes the description, turns the values a reader would change into {params} in the question and :params in the SQL with a params: entry, drops the row-cap LIMIT the generator added unless the question asks for it, adds other phrasings, moves the entry into the curated section, runs nl2sql curated validate, and commits it. The same steps head the exported file as comments.

export never writes the config's own files: it refuses an --out that is nl2sql.yaml or any file it includes, and exits 2. Neither the REST API nor the playground writes it either.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Models and SQL checks: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/curated.py
  • The section in the config: Curated in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/models.py
  • Index entries and the change hash: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/curated.py
  • Startup check: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py
  • Facade: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/curated_api.py
  • Command: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/cli/commands/curated.py
  • The demo's verified queries: CHINOOK_VERIFIED_QUERIES in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/datasets/chinook.py
  • The playground badge: verifiedSource() in web/playground/src/results.js
  • Matching and running: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/curated_matcher/
  • Proposals from feedback: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/feedback/proposals.py

docs.title: Datasource Configuration
docs.text:
The datasources section of nl2sql.yaml lists the databases the engine can query. nl2sql init writes it as a folder, one file per datasource, so each team can own its own database's file:

# nl2sql.yaml
datasources: { file: datasources/ }

# datasources/sales.yaml   (the id defaults to the file name: "sales")
type: postgres
description: Orders, customers and revenue for the EU shop.
connection:
  host: db.internal
  port: 5432
  database: sales
  user: nl2sql
  password: "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}"
limits: { row_limit: 1000, timeout_ms: 8000, max_bytes: 10485760 }
preferred_tables: [public.revenue_daily, v_monthly_sales]
domains: [revenue, customers, orders]
sample_questions:
  - What was revenue by region last quarter?
  - Which customers placed the most orders this year?
required: true

The section can also be a file holding the list (datasources: {file: datasources.yaml}), or the list written inline in nl2sql.yaml. An empty list is valid: the apps add datasources at runtime.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning id the file name in a folder, otherwise required The datasource's id. In a folder, if it is given it must equal the file name. type required The adapter: sqlite, duckdb, postgres, mysql, mssql, or an adapter a plugin registers. A misspelt or uninstalled one is a ConfigError with "did you mean" and the install hint. description none What is in the database. The resolver's answerability check reads it, so write one. connection {} The adapter's own connection settings (host, port, database, driver, options, ...), validated by the adapter. Every value may be a ${provider:key} reference and keeps it until the adapter is built. A relative SQLite or DuckDB database is relative to nl2sql.yaml. limits none row_limit, timeout_ms, max_bytes; see Limits. preferred_tables [] Tables or views the planner should reach for first. See Preferred tables. sample_questions [] Questions the datasource answers. They are indexed into its schema.datasource entry, which routing reads. domains [] A routing hint written by people. Routing does not read it yet. required false engine.check() fails (EngineNotReady) when this datasource cannot connect, and the CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo refuse to start. See Startup.

In Python, Datasource(id=..., adapter=MyAdapter(...)) passes a built adapter object instead of type.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
limits:
  row_limit: 1000       # the most rows one sub-query returns
  timeout_ms: 8000      # the longest one statement may run
  max_bytes: 10485760
  • timeout_ms: Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB enforce it (SQL Server rounds up to whole seconds); SQLite does not, and uses it only as its lock-wait timeout. See each adapter page for how.
  • row_limit: unset, it is settings.results.row_limit (100,000); set higher, settings.results.row_limit still bounds it. A result that reaches it is flagged as truncated and the answer says so. It is applied before results are combined, so a join input that reaches it is refused (RESULT_TRUNCATED) and a union input that reaches it is flagged with a warning; see row cap before a combine.
  • max_bytes: passed to the adapter.

There is one place for each limit: the 0.4 options: bag and the top-level spellings are gone.

docs.title: Preferred tables
docs.text:
The package never creates a view. The data team creates it in the database, lists it under preferred_tables, and runs nl2sql index; every built-in adapter snapshots views as well as tables (PostgreSQL materialized views are not read). At question time the schema retriever lists preferred tables first and marks them "preferred": true in the schema the planner sees, and the planner is told to plan against a preferred table when it answers the question:

  • When the whole schema is sent (settings.retrieval.full_snapshot_max_tables tables or fewer), every preferred table is in it, first.
  • Otherwise the retrieved tables are re-ordered so preferred ones come first, and a preferred table the search scored but did not pick is added when its similarity is within 0.05 of the least similar pick.

RBAC is unchanged: a preferred table the role may not read loses its data like any other table, and the validator refuses a plan that reads it.

A name that is not in the indexed schema is a warning, not an error: nl2sql doctor and the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index/status) print "Preferred table 'v_x' of 'chinook' is not in the indexed schema". The usual cause is a view created after the last index; re-index the datasource.

docs.title: When a datasource fails to start
docs.text:
A datasource the engine cannot build (an unknown type, a missing driver, an invalid connection config, a ${...} reference that does not resolve) stops it: building the engine raises one ConfigError that names every such datasource and the reason. Building never connects, so this needs no database.

A datasource that cannot connect is found by engine.check() (see Public Facade → Lifecycle), and does not stop the engine unless it is required. The others stay routed, and the broken one is marked unavailable:

  • the log has an error: Datasource 'sales' is unavailable: <reason>;
  • check() reports it failed at stage connect, with a fix;
  • engine.datasources.list() (and GET /api/v1/datasource) shows it with status: "failed" and the reason, and nothing is routed to it;
  • the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index/status) carries the same sentence as a warning;
  • a query with datasource_id set to it, and nl2sql index or engine.index.build([...]) naming it, fail with that reason.

check() raises EngineNotReady when a required: true datasource fails, or when datasources are configured and none is ready. A later check(), or engine.datasources.test(id), that connects routes the datasource again.

nl2sql doctor prints the same check() report. After check(), engine.policies.validate() reports a role that names an unavailable datasource as UNAVAILABLE.

A secret provider that cannot start is different: it fails startup. See Secrets → When a provider fails to start.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use ${env:VAR} for environment variables, or ${provider:key} for a secret from a provider in the secrets section.
  • Adapter-specific fields under connection are passed through to the adapter.
  • From Python, engine.datasources.add(Datasource(...)) adds one to a running engine (built, not connected), and engine.datasources.remove(id) takes one out; nl2sql-api's POST /api/v1/datasource takes the same shape as JSON.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
The embeddings section of nl2sql.yaml chooses how schema entries are embedded during nl2sql index, and how questions are embedded during retrieval. nl2sql init writes the key-free local provider:

# embeddings.yaml
provider: local
Field Default Meaning provider required local, openai, or a provider a plugin registers. model the provider's default The embedding model. api_key the provider's standard variable A ${env:VAR} or ${provider:key} reference, resolved when the embedder is built.

In Python, Embeddings(instance=MyEmbeddings()) passes a LangChain embeddings object instead of a provider name. Each engine builds its own embedder once.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
provider Model Dimensions API key local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (ONNX, bundled with chromadb); the only model 384 none openai model, default text-embedding-3-small 1536 api_key, else OPENAI_API_KEY

An openai section with no key resolving is a ConfigError when the engine is built, naming the variable.

Notes on the local provider:

  • No extra dependency. The model ships with chromadb, which is already a transitive dependency through langchain-chroma.
  • One-time download. The first indexing run downloads roughly 79 MB of ONNX model files into a local cache directory. Expect a pause of up to a few minutes; a log line is emitted before the download starts.
  • Embeddings only. This removes the API key requirement from the embedding step. It does not make querying key-free: answering a question still needs a chat model (see LLMs).

docs.title: Switching providers
docs.text: Switching providers requires a re-index. The two providers produce vectors of different dimensionality, so an existing index cannot be read with the other provider. Retrieving from an index whose vectors disagree with the configured provider raises EmbeddingDimensionMismatchError naming both providers. The check runs on the read path only, so the fix is to re-run nl2sql index --full; alternatively, point storage.path at a separate folder per provider.

docs.title: LLM Configuration
docs.text:
The llm section of nl2sql.yaml names the model every agent uses, and optional per-agent overrides. nl2sql init writes it to llm.yaml with the provider's default model and no key.

# llm.yaml
provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0
# api_key is optional: without it the provider's standard variable
# (OPENAI_API_KEY) is read. Write it to read another one:
# api_key: "${env:TEAM_OPENAI_KEY}"
agents:
  ast_planner:         { provider: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5, temperature: null }
  indexing_enrichment: { model: gpt-5.4-mini }
prices:
  gpt-4o: { input: 2.5, cached_input: 1.25, output: 10 }

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The section is flat: its keys are the top-level agent's.

Field Default Meaning provider required openai, anthropic, openrouter, ollama, or a provider a plugin registers. A misspelt or uninstalled one is a ConfigError with "did you mean". model required The model identifier. In Python it may be a LangChain chat model object instead (LLM(model=ChatOpenAI(...))), with no provider. temperature 0.0 A float, or null to send no temperature at all; see Temperature. api_key none Without it, the provider's standard variable (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) is read. With it, a ${env:VAR} or ${provider:key} reference (or a literal, which is not recommended). The reference is resolved when the client is built, never at load. base_url the provider's An endpoint override; see Other OpenAI-compatible endpoints. agents {} Per-node overrides, keyed by node name; see Per-node models. prices {} Per-model prices per million tokens; see Prices.

engine.check() reports every agent whose key does not resolve, without calling a model.

docs.title: Providers and wire types
docs.text:
The engine is model-agnostic. A provider is a preset: an endpoint, the environment variable its key comes from, and the wire type it speaks, which is the HTTP protocol on the wire. Everything that differs between wire types lives in one adapter per wire type, in nl2sql/llm/wires/:

wire type adapter client providers openai wires/openai.py ChatOpenAI openai, openrouter, ollama, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint anthropic wires/anthropic.py ChatAnthropic (the anthropic extra) anthropic

Each adapter owns four things, so neither the registry nor the nodes know which wire they are on:

openai wire anthropic wire Client ConfiguredChatOpenAI, seed=42 CachingChatAnthropic, max_tokens=16000 Structured output tool call (function_calling) forced tool call (function_calling) Prompt caching nothing to mark: OpenAI caches long prefixes by itself cache_control on the last system block Usage prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens → cached; no cache writes reported cache reads and writes, see Query API → usage

Both adapters also turn a model's HTTP 400 on temperature into the same "set temperature: null" error (see Temperature).

The providers:

provider wire type default endpoint API key openai openai OpenAI's own API required (OPENAI_API_KEY) anthropic anthropic Anthropic's own API required (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) openrouter openai https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 required (OPENROUTER_API_KEY) ollama openai http://localhost:11434/v1 not required

Any other value raises ValueError: Unsupported LLM provider, naming the valid providers. Every agent picks its own provider, so one question can use several; see Per-node models.

docs.title: Adding a provider
docs.text:
• A provider that speaks an existing wire type (a gateway, a hosted OpenAI-compatible service) is one entry in PROVIDER_PRESETS in nl2sql/llm/registry.py: its endpoint, key variable and wire. Nothing else changes. For a one-off endpoint you don't even need that: set base_url on an openai agent (see Other OpenAI-compatible endpoints).
  • A new wire type (Gemini, Bedrock) is one new adapter module in nl2sql/llm/wires/ implementing the Wire protocol in wires/base.py (build_client, structured_output_method, mark_cache, read_usage), one entry in WIRES in wires/__init__.py, and presets that name it. Add a case to CASES in tests/unit/test_llm_wire_contract.py. The contract suite then runs every structured-output call, usage, cache and key test against it.

docs.title: OpenAI
docs.text:
nl2sql init and nl2sql demo write gpt-5.4 as the OpenAI default. On the owner's account (probed 2026-09-20) it accepted temperature: 0 with a limit of 500,000 tokens per minute, against 30,000 for the previous default gpt-4o - less than one question with a single retry needs (about 33,500 tokens).

Every node asks for structured output as a tool call. The planner used to use langchain-openai's default, a json_schema response format; it now uses a tool call like the other nodes, because that is what the openai wire's adapter uses for every node, and what OpenRouter's and Ollama's models support most widely.

provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0

docs.title: Anthropic (Claude)
docs.text:
Claude runs on Anthropic's own API through ChatAnthropic, not through an OpenAI-compatibility shim: prompt caching and reliable structured output need Anthropic's native API. langchain-anthropic is an optional extra:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[anthropic]"

Selecting provider: anthropic without it fails on the first LLM call with ValueError: ... Install the anthropic extra: pip install "nl2sql-engine[anthropic]", and nl2sql doctor reports the missing extra.

provider: anthropic
model: claude-opus-5
temperature: null          # Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 reject any temperature

nl2sql init --provider anthropic and nl2sql demo write claude-opus-5 as the Claude default, with temperature: null. Current models:

model temperature minimum cacheable prefix claude-opus-5 rejected (HTTP 400): use null 512 tokens claude-sonnet-5 rejected (HTTP 400): use null 1,024 tokens claude-haiku-4-5 accepted, e.g. 0.0 4,096 tokens

These come from Anthropic's documented model rules, not from a probe on a real account. A rejected temperature fails with the same "set temperature: null" error as OpenAI (see Temperature).

How the engine uses it:

  • Structured output is a forced tool call (with_structured_output's function_calling method), for every node. Anthropic's native JSON outputs (output_config.format) do not accept recursive schemas, and the planner's PlanModel is recursive; neither does strict tool use (strict: true). Claude now and then nests a tool call's arguments one level down under a key of its own choosing ({"input": {...}}, {"query": {...}}, {"dtype": {...}}). Recording runs on claude-opus-5 failed the decomposer this way on up to 9 of 20 questions, and no other node. The root cause was the decomposer's tool: it went out with an empty description and no field descriptions, while its prompt asked for "JSON only" rather than a tool call. DecomposerResponse now describes itself and each top-level field ("call this tool with the decomposition itself as the arguments ... do not wrap them"), and the prompt asks for the tool call. As a safety net the wire also unwraps that shape before any node parses it: a dict with exactly one key the schema does not declare, holding an object with every required field and at least one declared one. Any other malformed answer still fails validation as before. A new node's response model should carry a docstring and field descriptions for the same reason.
  • Prompt caching. The resolver, decomposer, planner and refiner send a stable system message and a variable human message. On the anthropic wire only, the last system block carries cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"} (a 5-minute cache). Anthropic renders tools, then system, then messages, so the breakpoint caches the tool schema and the system prompt; the question follows it. The answer synthesizer sends no system message, so nothing is marked. Other providers send no cache_control.
  • Whether a prefix clears the minimum. On Chinook the planner's cached prefix is its system prompt (about 3.5k tokens, most of it the retrieved schema) plus the PlanModel tool schema (about 2k): above every model's minimum. The decomposer's (about 0.7k of system prompt plus a 1.4k tool schema) and the refiner's (about 2.7k, no tool) clear Opus 5's 512 and Sonnet 5's 1,024 but not Haiku 4.5's 4,096, so on Haiku they are silently not cached. The resolver's answerability check (datasourceresolver) is marked the same way, but its prefix (about 260 tokens of system prompt plus a small tool schema) is below every Claude model's minimum, so it is never cached. The decomposer's prefix is the same for every question; the planner's and refiner's include the retrieved tables, so they hit when a sub-query retrieves the same tables again (a retry, or a similar question).
  • max_tokens is 16,000 per call: every node call is non-streaming, and the SDK refuses a non-streaming call whose max_tokens could outlast its timeout.
  • Usage. Cache reads and writes are reported as cached_input_tokens and cache_write_input_tokens, with each input token counted once (see Query API → usage). With a price in llm.prices, a cache write costs 1.25x the model's input rate (Anthropic's price for a 5-minute write, the only kind the engine asks for) unless the price gives its own cache_write.

nl2sql demo --record records Claude too: with an Anthropic key the recording proxy speaks Anthropic's Messages API to https://api.anthropic.com, and stores each answer under the same name and question an OpenAI one would get, so replay (which answers on the OpenAI wire) serves it unchanged. The hosted demo's shipped recordings are made this way; see Hosted demo.

docs.title: OpenRouter
docs.text:
OpenRouter is an OpenAI-compatible gateway: a single API key reaches Anthropic, Google, Meta and hundreds of other models. Models are named <vendor>/<model>, for example anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 or google/gemini-2.5-pro.

provider: openrouter
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
temperature: 0.0

docs.title: Ollama
docs.text:
Ollama exposes an OpenAI-compatible API on http://localhost:11434/v1, so it needs no api_key and no base_url: start the daemon, pull a model, and point llm.yaml at it.

provider: ollama
model: llama3.1
temperature: 0.0

Set base_url if the daemon is not on localhost:11434 (a remote box, or a different port).

Ollama is supported at the transport level, not guaranteed end to end

The pipeline drives every model through with_structured_output, and the AST planner's target is PlanModel — a recursive Pydantic schema whose Expr references itself. That is a demanding structured-output target, and small local models often handle it poorly: expect malformed plans, empty fields or repeated refiner loops depending on the model you choose. Whether a given local model works is a property of that model, not of the transport. Prefer the largest instruct model with reliable JSON-schema/tool-calling support that your hardware allows, and validate against your own questions before relying on it.

Ollama also does not make the demo run fully offline: embeddings are a separate path (see below), and the demo's other steps are unchanged.

docs.title: Temperature
docs.text:
Each agent sends exactly the temperature its config names, and seed=42:

  • Omitted, it is 0.0, sent with every call. This reduces variance; it does not make output reproducible (see Determinism).
  • temperature: null sends no temperature parameter at all, so the model uses its own default.

Use null for models that accept only their default. Probed on 2026-09-20 with the engine's parameters of the time (temperature=0, seed=42, strict json_schema; the planner now sends a tool call instead):

model temperature: 0 gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4o accepted gpt-5.5, gpt-5-mini rejected: HTTP 400 "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.0 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported."

The rejected models accepted the same call without temperature (still with seed=42), so only the temperature needs to go. When a model rejects it, the first LLM call fails with an error that names the model and the agent and says what to set, instead of the provider's raw response:

ValueError: Model 'gpt-5.5' (LLM agent 'default') rejected the temperature
parameter (HTTP 400: Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.0 with
this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.) Set 'temperature: null'
for agent 'default' in the LLM config file so no temperature is sent to this
model.

Nothing is retried without the parameter: what the config says is what is sent.

langchain-openai would drop it silently

langchain-openai removes any temperature other than 1 from a model whose name starts with gpt-5 before the request is built, so gpt-5.4 would never receive the 0.0 it accepts. The registry sets the configured value after the client is constructed, so the config - not the model name - decides what is sent.

docs.title: Per-node models
docs.text:
The six pipeline nodes that call a model, and indexing enrichment, each have an agent. An agent not under agents runs on the top level:

agents key node curated_matcher picks the verified query that answers the question, if any (one short call; only when curated answers are configured and a candidate clears the floor) datasource_resolver checks that the connected data can answer the question at all (one short call; refuses with QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE) decomposer splits the question into sub-queries ast_planner writes the query plan (the largest prompt: it carries the schema) refiner explains a failed plan so the planner can retry answer_synthesizer writes the final answer from the rows indexing_enrichment writes missing schema descriptions during nl2sql index --enrich (optional, off by default)

Any other key is an error with "did you mean". An agent takes every field it sets (provider, model, temperature, api_key, base_url) and inherits the rest from the top level. Inheritance follows which fields were written, so temperature: null on an agent still means "send none". Each node can be on a different provider, and so a different wire type. For example, plan on Claude and run everything else on OpenAI, with one cheaper node that only accepts its default temperature:

provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0
agents:
  ast_planner:
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-opus-5
    temperature: null        # Claude Opus 5 rejects a temperature
  answer_synthesizer:
    model: gpt-5-mini        # on OpenAI, inherited
    temperature: null        # gpt-5-mini rejects temperature=0

Here curated_matcher, datasource_resolver, decomposer and refiner run on the top level. With no api_key, the planner reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the others OPENAI_API_KEY. Each node keeps its own key, endpoint and cache behaviour: the planner's system prompt is cache-marked for Anthropic, the others are sent unmarked to OpenAI. The model each call actually used is recorded per node in QueryResult.usage.calls and in a run trace's llm.by_node (see Debugging).

In the demo, the playground's Settings page writes exactly these entries into the demo folder's llm.yaml. Choosing a provider and a model for a step adds an agents: entry with provider, model and the temperature that model takes: 0.0, or null for gpt-5.5, gpt-5-mini, claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5. A step on the default's provider takes the default's base_url and api_key; a step on another provider names no key (its standard variable is read) and no base_url. A key saved on the page goes to the demo's .env. Choosing "Default" removes the entry. The running engine reloads its llm section from nl2sql.yaml, so the change applies to the next question. The page offers the providers and models in VERIFIED_MODELS (nl2sql/llm/providers.py), OpenAI and Anthropic for now, and a provider only once its key is saved. See the Settings page.

The playground's Pipeline page reads the same configuration back: it lists every step of a run and, for each of the six a model decides, the provider and model it is set to use, then what it actually spent once a question has been asked. It is served by GET /api/pipeline from engine.about(), whose steps (nl2sql.pipeline.steps) take their six model steps from LLM_AGENTS rather than repeating the table above. See the Pipeline page.

On the hosted demo (nl2sql demo --hosted) the same choice is offered and nothing is written at all. The visitor keeps one key per provider and a model per step in their own browser tab, and both travel with each question: a key per provider in a header of its own, and the choices in one compact X-NL2SQL-Models header, {"astplanner": "anthropic:claude-opus-5"} (the header names a step by its registry agent name, LLM_AGENTS in nl2sql/llm/providers.py). The server validates every name against LLM_AGENTS and VERIFIED_MODELS, builds each step's client for that one request from the key for the provider it names, caches none of them, and refuses with 400 -- naming the step and the provider -- when a step is on a provider the request brought no key for. See Hosted demo.

When nl2sql demo picks replay or live mode at start-up it points the top level of llm.yaml at the chosen provider. In replay and record mode every agents: entry follows, with the local replay server or recording proxy as base_url and the placeholder api_key (replay, proxy) it accepts, because one fake or proxy serves every call; no key goes into the environment. In live mode a step keeps the provider it was given; only an entry with no provider, or one left on the replay endpoint, follows the top level, and no api_key is written. Moving an entry between OpenAI and Anthropic replaces a model the new provider does not serve (a gpt- model on Anthropic, a claude- one on OpenAI) with that provider's default and its temperature. Every provider key saved in the demo's .env is loaded at start-up, so each step finds its own.

docs.title: Other OpenAI-compatible endpoints
docs.text:
A config-supplied base_url always overrides the provider preset. That is what lets the same code path serve any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint — vLLM, LiteLLM, a local proxy — without a new provider:

provider: openai
model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
api_key: "${env:LOCAL_LLM_KEY}"
base_url: http://localhost:8000/v1

Pick the provider whose credential behaviour matches the endpoint: openai or openrouter if the endpoint expects a key, ollama if it accepts any key.

docs.title: Clients are built when the LLM is set
docs.text:
The engine builds every agent's client when it is created, and again when the LLM is replaced, without calling a model. Each engine keeps its clients in its own cache (an LRU of 16), keyed on the agent's resolved settings: provider, model, base_url, temperature and the API key. The key enters the cache key only as a SHA-256 digest, so a cache key can be logged and never holds a secret. Agents with equal settings share one client: seven agents on one model build one client.

A missing key does not stop the engine from starting:

  • Building the engine (which nl2sql index, the API and the demo all do) does not require a chat provider key. A machine with no key can still run key-free work such as indexing with embeddings: {provider: local}. That holds for indexing because the indexing_enrichment pass is genuinely optional: it is skipped, not merely deferred to a later failure.
  • engine.check() reports every agent whose key does not resolve, without calling a model. Using that agent raises the same error, naming the agent, the provider and the environment variable to set:
ValueError: LLM agent 'default' uses provider 'openai', which requires an API
key, but none could be resolved. Set OPENAI_API_KEY ... or in the environment,
or give the agent an 'api_key' in the LLM config file.

The key is read when the clients are built. A key set in the environment after the engine started is used only once the LLM is set again.

Genuine misconfiguration fails immediately: an unknown provider, or an agent with no model.

docs.title: Replacing the LLM at runtime
docs.text:
engine.llm.replace swaps the whole llm section at once, while the engine runs:

from nl2sql import LLM, AgentLLM

change = engine.llm.replace(
    LLM(provider="anthropic", model="claude-sonnet-5-5",
        agents={"ast_planner": AgentLLM(model="claude-opus-5-5")}),
    by=user,          # optional: the UserContext making the change
)
print(change.changes)  # {"default": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"}, ...}
  • Validated like the file. The new section is checked as the llm section of nl2sql.yaml is: every provider must be registered and installed, and every agent's API key must resolve. If anything is wrong it raises ConfigError and nothing changes. No model is called.
  • Atomic. The new clients are built first, then the engine's LLM and engine.config.llm are swapped together. A query reads the engine's LLM once, when it starts: queries already running finish on the old LLM, and every query that starts afterwards uses the new one. No query mixes the two.
  • Logged and audited. One INFO line on the nl2sql.llm logger and one llm.changed audit record name who made the change (by's user and roles when given, otherwise the entry point, python by default) and, for each agent whose provider or model changed, the old and the new one. They never hold a key, a key reference or a header.
INFO nl2sql.llm: LLM replaced by user=u42 roles=[admin] via api: default: openai/gpt-5.4 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; ast_planner: openai/gpt-5.4 -> anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
  • Not saved. Nothing is written to disk, so a restart goes back to the config file.
  • Cached clients. Swapping back to an earlier LLM reuses the clients built for it. A client that falls out of the cache is closed (its close(), when it has one) once no running query uses it.
  • Plans follow the model. The plan cache key includes the planner's provider and model, so after a swap a plan written by another model is never served. Swapping back hits the old plans again. See Determinism → The plan cache.

replace also takes the section as written in nl2sql.yaml, as a mapping, checked by the same rules as the file. A ${...} reference is kept in a secret field (api_key) and is an error anywhere else, so data that did not come from your files never reads the environment. nl2sql-api serves it as the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm: the body is the section as JSON, and a bad one is HTTP 422 with the ConfigError text. The playground's model switch calls replace too. engine.llm.list() shows the model each agent runs on.

docs.title: Embeddings are a separate path
docs.text: None of Anthropic, OpenRouter or Ollama covers embeddings — they are not routed through LLMRegistry at all. Each engine builds its own embedder from its embeddings section: {provider: local} embeds with the key-free ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model bundled with chromadb, and {provider: openai} reads OPENAI_API_KEY (or embeddings.api_key). Switching embedding providers requires a re-index.

docs.title: Prices
docs.text:
prices gives per-model prices per million tokens, so QueryResult.usage reports a cost:

prices:
  gpt-4o: { input: 2.5, cached_input: 1.25, output: 10 }

Optional cached_input (cache reads) defaults to input; optional cache_write (cache writes) defaults to input times the wire's write premium: 1.25 for Claude (provider: anthropic, whose 5-minute cache write Anthropic bills at 1.25x input) and 1 for the OpenAI wire. The rest of the prompt is billed at input. With no price for a model, QueryResult.usage reports tokens only and cost is null. No prices are built in.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• agents overrides give individual nodes, or indexing enrichment, their own model and temperature; see Per-node models.
  • indexing_enrichment is optional and runs only when asked for (nl2sql index --enrich, or enrich=True from Python). Omit it, or leave its key unset, and indexing still works - the schema is indexed without LLM-written descriptions. It never replaces a comment read from the database.
  • nl2sql init --provider takes openai, anthropic or openrouter, the providers with a default model, and writes no key. nl2sql demo --api-key picks the provider from the key's shape (sk-ant- is Anthropic, sk-or- is OpenRouter, anything else is OpenAI). To use Ollama, edit llm.yaml as shown above.

docs.title: Policies Configuration
docs.text:
The policies section of nl2sql.yaml decides who may read what. nl2sql init writes it to policies.yaml.

On your own machine, one line is enough: every caller may read everything.

# policies.yaml
allow_all: true

For anything shared, write roles:

# policies.yaml
default_role: viewer
admin_roles: [admin]
refusal_names_tables: false
roles:
  admin:
    description: Every table in every database
    allowed_datasources: ["*"]
    allowed_tables: ["*"]
  analyst:
    description: Sales, except the audit schema
    allowed_datasources: [sales]
    allowed_tables: ["sales.public.*"]

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Default Meaning allow_all false Every caller may read everything. It cannot be combined with default_role or roles. Policies.allow_all() is the Python shorthand. default_role none The role used when the caller gives none. It must name one of roles. Without it, a question with no role is refused. admin_roles [admin] The roles nl2sql-api lets through on the routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index. See REST API. refusal_names_tables false Name the role and the forbidden table in the refusal the user sees. Off, the message is "You do not have permission to see the data this question requires."; the table and role are always in the log and the run trace. The demo (nl2sql init --demo) sets it, since showing a refusal is its point. See Security Model. roles {} Role name to policy: description, allowed_datasources (ids or *) and allowed_tables (entries below).

docs.title: Table entries
docs.text:
Entry Allows * every table in every datasource datasource.* every table in every schema of one datasource datasource.schema.* every table in one schema datasource.schema.table one table in one schema datasource.table that table in the datasource's default schema only

Access is decided on the schema as well as the table. The plan names the schema a table is read from, and the SQL is written with it, so a grant of sales.orders does not let a plan read audit.orders:

allowed_tables: [warehouse.sales.orders, "warehouse.reference.*"]

docs.title: Two-part entries and the default schema
docs.text:
A two-part datasource.table entry predates schemas in policies. It is read as that table in the datasource's default schema, never in any schema:

  • The default schema is the one the adapter reports: the schema an unqualified table name resolves to on that connection (public on PostgreSQL by default, dbo on SQL Server, the connected database on MySQL, main on SQLite and DuckDB).
  • If an adapter cannot report one, main is the default.
  • A table the plan names without a schema is in the default schema.

So on a PostgreSQL datasource warehouse, warehouse.orders allows public.orders and refuses audit.orders. On SQLite and DuckDB, which have the one schema, two-part entries mean what they always did.

The first two-part entry loaded logs a warning, once per process, saying it is read as the default schema. To grant a table outside the default schema, write the three-part form.

An entry has two or three dot-separated parts (or is *), no part is empty, and * may only be the last part: datasource.*.orders is rejected when the config is loaded.

docs.title: One rule everywhere
docs.text: table_allowed() in nl2sql/auth/rbac.py is the only place an entry is matched. The logical validator (which refuses the plan), the schema retriever (which strips the statistics of tables the role cannot read), the executor's value check (which only probes readable tables) and the curated matcher (which only answers with a verified query whose tables are all readable) call it with the same datasource, schema and table, so they cannot disagree.

docs.title: Checking the policies
docs.text:
nl2sql policy validate checks that every datasource and table rule a role names is a configured datasource, against the config --config names:

nl2sql --config nl2sql.yaml policy validate

A role naming a datasource that is not configured is MISSING, and the command exits 1. From Python, engine.policy.validate_policies() returns the same report; after engine.check(), a role naming a datasource that failed to connect is UNAVAILABLE.

docs.title: Secrets Configuration
docs.text:
The secrets section of nl2sql.yaml is optional. It lists secret providers that the rest of the config can reference as ${provider_id:key}. The env provider (${env:VAR}) is always there without it.

# nl2sql.yaml
secrets: { file: secrets.yaml }

# secrets.yaml
providers:
  - id: aws-main
    type: aws
    region_name: "us-east-1"

providers may be omitted or left empty: both mean "no secret providers configured".

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
Each provider has:

  • id: unique provider ID used in secret references (e.g. ${aws-main:db_password})
  • type: aws, azure, hashicorp, or a provider a plugin registers. The id env is reserved for the built-in provider.

Every other key is the provider's own setting:

type Settings Extra to install aws region_name, profile_name, both optional (boto3's own lookup fills them in) nl2sql-engine[aws] azure vault_url (required), client_id, client_secret, tenant_id.
