docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
  -v "$PWD/my-project:/etc/nl2sql:ro" \
  -v nl2sql-data:/data -e NL2SQL_DATA_DIR=/data \
  nl2sql-api

Provider keys come from the environment (-e OPENAI_API_KEY=...) or from the mounted .env. Before it serves, the API calls engine.check(): a datasource with required: true that cannot connect stops the container, and any other that fails is logged and left out. Build the index once with POST /api/v1/index-all, or with nl2sql --config my-project/nl2sql.yaml index against the same storage.

docs.title: API usage
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/query \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"natural_language":"Top 5 customers by revenue last quarter?"}'

docs.title: PyPI (Python API)
docs.text: Use this path when you want to embed NL2SQL directly in a Python application. See the Core API documentation at docs/api/index.md.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# Core only
pip install nl2sql-engine

# install all available adapters. (Never prefer this, until you really need all adapters.)
pip install "nl2sql-engine[all]"

# Core with selected adapters
pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]"
pip install "nl2sql-engine[mysql,mssql]"
pip install "nl2sql-engine[duckdb]"

# The browser playground behind `nl2sql demo` (adds fastapi + uvicorn).
# `[all]` does NOT include it -- `all` covers database drivers only.
pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]"

Running a query needs an LLM key; only indexing is key-free. See Known limitations.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The engine reads one config, nl2sql.yaml, and the files it includes. nl2sql init writes it (in Python, nl2sql.config.init_project("my-project") writes the same files); see Start a config with nl2sql init. Each section has its own page:

  • Datasources
  • LLMs
  • Embeddings
  • Policies
  • Storage
  • Secrets
  • Settings

docs.title: Building the engine in Python
docs.text:
from nl2sql import NL2SQL

with NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml") as engine:   # or $NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml
    report = engine.check()                         # connects, and reports what is ready
    print(report)

Building the engine never connects to a datasource or calls a model. engine.check() does: it raises EngineNotReady when a datasource with required: true fails, and otherwise leaves a failed datasource out of routing. The library never reads a .env file; call python-dotenv yourself before from_config if you keep keys in one. See Public Facade for every way to build it, including a Config built in code and NL2SQL.demo(). Use the config for fixed, app-wide settings. Use runtime registration when you need to add datasources on a long-running process without restart.

docs.title: Datasource configuration
docs.text:
datasources/ holds one file per datasource; the file name is its id:

# datasources/my_postgres.yaml
type: postgres
description: Primary analytics DB.
connection:
  host: localhost
  port: 5432
  user: "${env:POSTGRES_USER}"
  password: "${env:POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
  database: analytics
limits: { row_limit: 100, timeout_ms: 8000, max_bytes: 10485760 }

Install the adapter extras that match type:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]"

See Adapters for the full list of available adapters. See Datasource config for field definitions.

docs.title: LLM configuration
docs.text:
llm.yaml selects the model and any per-agent overrides:

# llm.yaml
provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0
# api_key is optional: without it OPENAI_API_KEY is read.
agents:
  indexing_enrichment: { model: gpt-5.4-mini }

To route chat through OpenRouter instead — one key for Anthropic, Google, Meta and hundreds of other models, with no extra dependency:

provider: openrouter
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
temperature: 0.0

To use Claude on Anthropic's own API, with the system prompts prompt-cached, install the anthropic extra and point the config at it:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[anthropic]"

provider: anthropic
model: claude-opus-5
temperature: null          # Claude Opus 5 rejects a temperature

See LLM configuration → Anthropic.

A local Ollama daemon is configured the same way, with provider: ollama; how well a given local model handles the pipeline's structured output varies by model, so see LLM configuration → Ollama first.

Note that OpenRouter serves chat completions only. Embeddings are their own section: embeddings: { provider: local } (what nl2sql init writes) embeds with a key-free ONNX model, and provider: openai needs OPENAI_API_KEY. See Embeddings.

See LLM config for full schema details.

docs.title: Add a datasource at runtime
docs.text:
You can register a datasource programmatically without editing config files:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Datasource, Limits

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
engine.datasources.add(Datasource(
    id="runtime_pg",
    type="postgres",
    description="Runtime Postgres datasource",
    connection={
        "host": "localhost",
        "port": 5432,
        "user": "postgres",
        "password": "${env:RUNTIME_PG_PASSWORD}",
        "database": "analytics",
    },
    limits=Limits(timeout_ms=8000, row_limit=100, max_bytes=10485760),
))

engine.index.build(["runtime_pg"])

The description is indexed as given, even though no file lists runtime_pg, and the datasource joins engine.config. Indexing makes no LLM call unless you ask for one: engine.index.build(["runtime_pg"], enrich=True) has the indexing_enrichment agent write descriptions for tables and columns the database left without a comment.

You can also add the datasources of another config:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, load_config

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
for datasource in load_config("other/nl2sql.yaml").datasources:
    engine.datasources.add(datasource)

docs.title: Replace the LLM at runtime
docs.text:
engine.llm.replace swaps the whole llm section in the running engine, as one step: it is validated as llm.yaml is, every agent's key must resolve, and questions already running finish on the old LLM.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, LLM, AgentLLM

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
engine.llm.replace(LLM(provider="openai", model="gpt-5.4",
                       agents={"ast_planner": AgentLLM(model="gpt-5.5")}))
engine.llm.list()["ast_planner"]["model"]   # 'gpt-5.5'

The llm section of another config:

from nl2sql import load_config

engine.llm.replace(load_config("other/nl2sql.yaml").llm)

docs.title: Policies configuration (RBAC)
docs.text:
policies.yaml defines which roles can access which datasources and tables:

# policies.yaml
default_role: viewer
admin_roles: [admin]
roles:
  admin:
    description: System Administrator
    allowed_datasources: ["*"]
    allowed_tables: ["*"]
  viewer:
    description: Read-only access to the catalogue
    allowed_datasources: [my_postgres]
    allowed_tables: ["my_postgres.public.products"]

{allow_all: true} (what nl2sql init writes) lets every caller read everything, for local use only. See Policies config for allowed table formats and wildcards.

docs.title: Secrets configuration (optional)
docs.text:
A secrets section is only needed when you want to pull secrets from a provider other than the environment:

# secrets.yaml
providers:
  - id: azure-prod
    type: azure
    vault_url: "https://my-vault.vault.azure.net/"

A datasource then writes password: "${azure-prod:db-password}". See Secrets config for supported providers and fields.

docs.title: Run a query
docs.text:
from nl2sql import NL2SQL
from nl2sql.auth.models import UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
user_ctx = UserContext(user_id="user123", roles=["admin"])

result = engine.run_query(
    "Top 5 customers by revenue last quarter?",
    user_context=user_ctx
)

print(result.final_answer)
for sub_query in result.sub_queries:
    print(sub_query.datasource_id, sub_query.sql)

The QueryResult includes sub_queries (each with its generated sql), final_answer, errors, warnings, artifact_refs, and a trace_id for observability. Each sub-query carries a capped sample of its rows (rows); the full result set lives in artifact storage and is addressed through artifact_refs.

A question repeated on the same day reuses its validated plan from the plan cache (no planner call, same SQL and rows; still validated every time), and sub_query.plan_source says "cache". Turn it off with settings.pipeline.plan_cache: false; empty it with nl2sql cache clear. See Determinism → The plan cache.

docs.title: Lifecycle (configure → check → index → query)
docs.text:
1. Configure datasources, LLMs, and policies (nl2sql init).
  2. Build the engine and call engine.check().
  3. Index schemas at least once (and after schema changes).
  4. Run queries.

docs.title: Index schema (required)
docs.text:
engine.index.build(["my_postgres"])   # one datasource
engine.index.build()                  # every datasource

docs.title: Configure providers
docs.text:
Secrets providers are installed via extras and selected in the secrets section:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[aws]"
pip install "nl2sql-engine[azure]"
pip install "nl2sql-engine[hashicorp]"

See Configuration for the whole config, the environment variables it reads, and where each 0.4 file and variable went.

docs.title: From Source (Development)
docs.text: Use this path when you want to contribute or run the latest changes.

docs.title: Clone and install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/nadeem4/nl2sql.git
cd nl2sql

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

pip install -e packages/sdk -e "packages/nl2sql[postgres,duckdb,demo]" -e packages/api
pip install --group dev

These are the extras the full test suite needs (see CONTRIBUTING.md): postgres and duckdb supply the drivers the adapter tests import, and demo supplies the FastAPI/uvicorn server behind nl2sql demo. Add mysql or mssql for those drivers, or use [all] for every dialect driver (it does not include demo). There is no sqlite extra: that driver is in the standard library. pip install --group dev (pip 25.1 or newer) installs the PEP 735 dev group from the root pyproject.toml: pytest, pytest-randomly, pytest-timeout and httpx.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The engine reads one nl2sql.yaml. nl2sql init writes it, with each section in its own file, and nl2sql init --demo writes the demo's. See Start a config with nl2sql init and Configuration.

nl2sql init my-demo --demo
nl2sql --config my-demo/nl2sql.yaml index

docs.title: Run locally
docs.text:
CLI:

nl2sql --config my-demo/nl2sql.yaml run "How many customers are there?"

Python API:

python -c "from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext; print(NL2SQL.from_config('my-demo/nl2sql.yaml').run_query('How many customers are there?', user_context=UserContext(roles=['admin'])))"

API service:

NL2SQL_CONFIG=my-demo/nl2sql.yaml nl2sql-api --port 8000

or in Docker:

docker build -f packages/api/Dockerfile -t nl2sql-api .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 -v "$PWD/my-demo:/etc/nl2sql" nl2sql-api

See Docker (REST API) for adapter extras, the role settings and the data volume.

docs.title: Debugging a Run with Traces
docs.text:
A run trace is one JSON file that records everything a single question did inside the engine: every node execution in order (retries and parallel sub-queries included), the state each node read and the update it returned, its errors and warnings, and for every LLM call the exact messages sent, the raw response, the parsed result and the token usage. The final QueryResult is in it too.

The point is to run a failing question once, then debug it from the file: read it, print its timeline, or replay it through the pipeline without calling the model again.

docs.title: When a trace is written
docs.text:
Each engine reads these from the settings.traces section of its config, so two engines in one process trace by their own settings. The 0.4 variable each one is still set from by the CLI and the playground is in brackets.

Setting Default Meaning settings.traces.mode on_failure off, on_failure or always. settings.traces.sample_rows 50 Result rows kept in the trace. settings.traces.max_field_chars 20000 Longest string kept in a node's recorded inputs and outputs.

Traces are written to <storage.path>/traces/ (see Storage); nl2sql init puts storage.path in .gitignore.

on_failure writes a trace when the run returned errors, needed a retry in any sub-query, had a node fail, or did not complete (timeout, cancellation, crash). A run that recovered on retry therefore still leaves a trace.

The demo's config (nl2sql init --demo) sets settings.traces.mode: always in its settings.yaml, so every playground question is traced.

The trace is recorded by a callback that run_with_graph attaches to every run, so the CLI, the Python API, the REST API and the playground all produce it. Writing a trace never fails a run; a write error is logged as a warning.

Where the file went is reported back:

  • QueryResult.trace_path (Python API) and trace_path in the REST /query response: the path, or null when no trace was written. trace_id is in the file name.
  • nl2sql run prints Trace written to <path>.
  • The playground shows a Download trace link under Cost & time when Debug is on.

File names are <UTC timestamp>_<trace_id>.json, so a directory listing sorts by time.

docs.title: What is in the file
docs.text:
{
  "trace_format_version": 1,
  "trace_id": "159afe1f-3305-4907-903a-55495d040665",
  "started_at": "2026-09-21T16:48:37.324431+00:00",
  "finished_at": "2026-09-21T16:48:37.712202+00:00",
  "duration_s": 0.3878,
  "outcome": "completed",
  "failed": true,
  "error": null,
  "request": {"question": "How many customers are there?", "roles": ["admin"],
              "tenant_id": "default_tenant", "datasource_id": null, "execute": true},
  "engine": {"version": "0.1.2", "git_sha": "2cfe121", "python": "3.13.14"},
  "llm": {"configured": {"default": {"provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5.4", "temperature": 0.0}},
          "by_node": {"decomposer": "gpt-5.4", "ast_planner": "gpt-5.4", "refiner": "gpt-5.4",
                      "answer_synthesizer": "gpt-5.4"}},
  "settings": {"...": "the run's settings section: pipeline, retrieval, results, traces, schema, ..."},
  "limits": {"sample_rows": 50, "max_field_chars": 20000, "max_list_items": 200, "note": "..."},
  "nodes": ["... one entry per node execution, below ..."],
  "result": {"...": "the QueryResult, rows capped"}
}

One entry of nodes (the planner's second attempt, from a run whose first plan named a column that does not exist; long values shortened here):

{
  "seq": 20, "end_seq": 21,
  "node": "ast_planner", "sub_query_id": "sq_9579d7d41aee", "attempt": 2, "parent": "sql_agent",
  "status": "ok",
  "started_at": "2026-09-21T16:48:37.683402+00:00", "duration_s": 0.0071,
  "inputs": {"sub_query": "...", "relevant_tables": "...", "errors": "...", "retry_count": 1},
  "outputs": {"ast_planner_response": "...", "reasoning": "...", "errors": []},
  "errors": [], "warnings": [], "exception": null,
  "llm_calls": [{
    "key": {"node": "ast_planner", "sub_query_id": "sq_9579d7d41aee", "attempt": 2, "call_index": 1},
    "model": "gpt-5.4",
    "params": {"model": "gpt-5.4", "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 42},
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "[ROLE]\nYou are a SQL Planner. ..."}],
    "prompt_sha256": "63ccb543...",
    "response": {"content": "{\"query_type\": \"READ\", ... \"column_name\": \"CustomerId\" ...}",
                 "tool_calls": [], "finish_reason": "stop", "model_name": "gpt-5.4"},
    "parsed": {"query_type": "READ", "...": "..."},
    "usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2, "...": "..."}
  }]
}
  • seq / attempt / sub_query_id: seq orders executions by start. The attempt counts per node and sub-query, so a retried planner is attempt: 2. Nodes inside the SQL agent carry parent: "sql_agent".
  • status: ok, warning (the node returned warnings, such as COLUMN_NOT_FOUND when strict columns are off), error (it returned an ERROR or CRITICAL error, raised, or an LLM call failed) or unfinished (it never ended: the run timed out or was cancelled first).
  • inputs are the state fields that node reads, not the whole graph state; outputs is the update it returned.

  • llm_calls: the messages exactly as sent, the model's raw answer (text content, or tool calls with their arguments), what the node parsed it into, and the usage record from TokenUsageCallback (the same record QueryResult.usage.calls reports). params holds what was sent: an agent configured with temperature: null has no temperature there, and llm.configured shows it as null. model is the model the provider says answered, per call, so per-node models show up per node in llm.by_node.

  • Plan cache hits. When a sub-query's plan came from the plan cache, its ast_planner entry has outputs.ast_planner_response.plan_source: "cache" and llm_calls: [] (zero planner tokens), and the validator, generator and executor entries follow as usual. The result shows the same thing as result.sub_queries[].plan_source and result.usage.plan_cache_hits. See Determinism → The plan cache.

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text:
The datasource_resolver and schema_retriever entries carry a retrieval object in outputs: what the vector search retrieved and how MMR chose among it (the engine has no re-ranking model; see Indexing).

"retrieval": {
  "skipped": false,
  "query": "Tracks sold per genre, highest first\ngroup_by: genre name ...",
  "searches": [{
    "search": "tables",
    "filter": {"datasource_id": "chinook", "types": ["schema.table", "schema.metric"]},
    "k": 8, "fetch_k": 32, "lambda_mult": 0.7,
    "pool": [
      {"rank": 1, "id": "schema.table:[main].[Track]:<version>", "label": "[main].[Track]",
       "type": "schema.table", "datasource_id": "chinook", "table": "[main].[Track]", "column": null,
       "similarity": 0.5651, "distance": 0.8698,
       "picked": true, "pick_order": 1, "mmr_score": 0.5651, "redundancy": 0.0}
    ],
    "picks": ["<ids in the order MMR picked them>"],
    "dropped": ["<ids of the pool entries not picked>"]
  }],
  "tables": [{"table": "Track", "columns": ["Name", "GenreId"]}]
}
  • query is the text actually embedded: the question for the resolver, and for the schema retriever the sub-query's intent, filters, group-by, expected columns and metrics, one per line.
  • pool is every candidate, nearest first. similarity is the cosine similarity MMR uses; distance is Chroma's (squared L2), and null for the resolver's datasources search, which scores every datasource entry itself rather than asking Chroma's approximate search. pick_order is the order MMR picked in, mmr_score the score the pick won with, and redundancy its similarity to the closest earlier pick.
  • searches lists each search in order; the schema retriever runs tables (or columns when that finds nothing), then planning over the tables found.
  • tables (schema retriever) is what survived: the tables and columns sent to the planner.
  • skipped: true with a reason means no search ran: the schema is small enough to send whole (each of the demo's three schemas, at 11, 4 and 5 tables, always is), only one datasource is registered ("single datasource: vector search skipped", which the demo is not: it registers three, so the resolver searches on every question), the request named a datasource_id, or there is no vector store. The resolver's answerability check is an LLM call, so it is in that entry's llm_calls, not in retrieval.

The record carries entry ids and names, never an entry's embedded text, which for a column holds its statistics and sample values. It follows the prompt's rule, "structure yes, data no": a column entry of a table the run's role cannot read keeps its name, rank and whether it was picked, and its scores are null with a withheld note, because a similarity to text that contains sample values says something about those values. The record is built from the numbers MMR computes anyway, so it is always there and costs no extra search.

The file records what happened. A sub-query's status reflects its final attempt, so one that recovers on retry reports "success"; the failed attempts stay in the node entries and in the result's warnings.

docs.title: Redaction
docs.text:
Every trace is redacted before it is written, with no setting to turn it off:

  • every value any secret reference resolved to (${env:...} and the other secret providers), the configured API keys, and the values of environment variables whose names contain KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, CREDENTIAL, CONNECTION_STRING or AUTH;
  • anything shaped like a secret even if the engine never saw the value: sk-... style keys, Bearer ... tokens, the password in scheme://user:password@host, and password=, pwd=, secret=, api_key=, AccountKey=, token= pairs;
  • the string value of any key named like api_key, password, secret, authorization, access_key, connection_string or credential(s);
  • the settings snapshot is the settings section only, which holds no credential: keys live in the llm, embeddings and datasources sections as references, and their resolved values are redacted as above.

A test runs a real question with the fake key sk-test-not-a-real-key-1234 in the environment and asserts that string appears nowhere in the file. Redaction is pattern and value based, so treat a trace as internal: it contains your prompts, schema and a sample of result rows.

docs.title: Capping
docs.text: Node inputs and outputs, and the result, are capped so a trace stays readable: result rows (rows, and the aggregator's terminal_results) keep settings.traces.sample_rows rows, other lists keep 200 items, and strings keep settings.traces.max_field_chars characters. Every cut leaves a [truncated] marker saying how much was dropped. LLM messages and raw responses are never cut, because replay needs them whole; a planner prompt on Chinook is about 12 000 characters, and a whole trace is typically a few hundred kilobytes.

docs.title: Reading a trace: nl2sql trace show
docs.text:
nl2sql trace show traces/20260921T164837755710Z_159afe1f-....json
nl2sql trace show 159afe1f-3305-4907-903a-55495d040665   # looks it up in <storage.path>/traces

It prints the question, then one row per node execution (nested SQL agent nodes indented) with sub-query, attempt, duration, tokens and status, then each error or warning, and marks the first failing node with >. A run with no failing node but a retry marks the first warning instead, since that is what set the retry off.

docs.title: Replaying a trace: nl2sql trace replay
docs.text:
nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml trace replay 159afe1f-3305-4907-903a-55495d040665

Replay runs the real pipeline again for the recorded question, roles and datasource, but every LLM call is answered from the trace. The engine's chat clients are pointed at an in-process transport, so no request reaches a model provider and no key is needed; the command reports how many recorded calls it served. It then compares the replayed QueryResult with the recorded one (ignoring ids, timings, usage and artifact paths) and says whether it matches.

  • Keying. Recorded answers are looked up by (node, sub_query_id, attempt, call_index), never by question text: a retried planner asks the same question twice and gets the answer it got the first time for that attempt, and parallel sub-queries cannot take each other's answers.
  • Divergence. If the replayed run asks for a call the recording does not have, or sends a prompt whose hash differs from the recorded one, replay stops at that call and reports Replay diverged at <node>, sub-query <id>, attempt <n>, LLM call <k>, with a diff of the prompt when it changed. If the run finishes without using a recorded call, that is reported too. This is information, not a crash: everything before that point ran as recorded.
  • Plan cache. Replay makes the LLM calls the recording made. If the recorded planner called the model, replay turns the plan cache off so that call is replayed rather than answered from a plan cached since. If the recorded run used the cache, replay uses it too, and reports a divergence (missing) when the cached plan has since been cleared.
  • Date. The planner and refiner prompts carry today's date, and the trace records it as request.today. Replay pins settings.pipeline.today to that date, so a trace recorded yesterday replays without diverging. A trace written before the date was recorded replays with the current setting.
  • Its own runtime. The pinned date, the plan cache choice and a zero retry back-off go into a config derived from the engine's (Runtime.derive), and the replay runs on a runtime built from it, with its own playback clients. The engine's config and LLMs are never changed, so a query running on the same engine meanwhile is unaffected. The replayed result is capped with that runtime's settings.traces sizes, as the recording was.
  • Exit code: 0 when the replayed result matches the recording, 1 on a divergence, a different result, or a datasource that cannot be reached.

docs.title: What replay can and cannot tell you
docs.text:
• Replay tests the code downstream of the model: parsing, validation, SQL generation, execution, aggregation. It is how you check a fix to that code against a real failure without spending tokens.
  • After a prompt change the recorded response is stale. Replay reports the node where the prompt diverged; one real run is needed to record a new trace.
  • The datasource must be reachable from where you replay, with the same configuration (the same --config). Replay says so and stops if it is not. Queries run again, so a database whose data changed gives a different result, and replay reports the difference.
  • The datasource resolver and schema retriever still run their vector search, which embeds the question with the configured embedding provider (the local model in the demo; with EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai that is an embeddings API call, not a chat model call).
  • Redaction applies to the recorded answers too: a model answer that contained something secret-shaped is replayed redacted.

docs.title: The playground
docs.text:
With Debug on, the per-node table under Cost & time puts a bar beside each node's time, sized to the slowest node, so the slow step stands out. Each node name opens that node's record from the trace: every attempt and sub-query, its errors and warnings, what it read and returned, and for LLM nodes the exact prompt, the raw response and the parsed result. Long text is folded. For the datasource_resolver and schema_retriever nodes it also shows the retrieval record as a table: the pool nearest first, picks marked with their MMR order, dropped entries greyed, the picks in order as a row of chips, and a second row naming the entries MMR passed over because they repeat an earlier pick. The Retrieval inspector at the top of the page runs the same search for any text (see the demo guide). The page fetches the trace from GET /api/trace/{trace_id}, which reads it with engine.traces.get: only files directly inside the engine's traces folder, and any id that is not a plain token is rejected, so ../ or an absolute path never reaches the filesystem.

Below the run, Was this answer right? records a rating keyed by the same trace id; nl2sql feedback stats reads the ratings together with the traces in <storage.path>/traces. See Feedback and Signals.

docs.title: Error Handling + Circuit Breaker
docs.text:
NL2SQL represents failures as structured PipelineError objects and propagates them through state. Retries are managed at the subgraph level, and a single circuit breaker provides fast-fail safety for vector retrieval.

One case cannot use state: LangGraph conditional-edge routers may only return routing decisions, so route_scan_layers() reports "no compatible subgraph found" by raising PipelineExecutionError (nl2sql.common.exceptions), an NL2SQLError carrying the PipelineError payload on .error. This propagates out of the router and is caught by run_with_graph(), which unwraps it and returns its PipelineError payload unchanged in GraphState.errors — preserving error_code (INVALID_STATE), severity, node and is_retryable; only unrecognised exceptions become UNKNOWN_ERROR.

docs.title: Error contract
docs.text:
PipelineError includes:

  • node, message, severity, error_code
  • provider and provider_response, set on a PROVIDER_* error (below), otherwise None
  • is_retryable derived from severity and error code

A query the database rejects is EXECUTION_FAILED when the adapter says the query itself was wrong (retried through the refiner) and DB_EXECUTION_ERROR when the database refused or could not run it (fatal). Common error codes include MISSING_SQL, EXECUTION_FAILED, PIPELINE_TIMEOUT, SECURITY_VIOLATION, QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE. VALUE_NOT_FOUND marks an empty result whose filter named a value its column does not have: retried once when a close value exists, otherwise a warning the answer reports (see ExecutorNode). RESULT_TRUNCATED marks a combine input that reached its datasource's row cap: an error for a join or compare, a warning for a union (see row cap before a combine).

ErrorCode carries only codes something can produce. Eleven members that no code path raised were removed (MISSING_GROUP_BY, INVALID_ALIAS_USAGE, JOIN_MISSING_ON_CLAUSE, INVALID_DATE_FORMAT, INVALID_NUMERIC_VALUE, EXECUTION_ERROR, PERFORMANCE_WARNING, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, PHYSICAL_VALIDATOR_FAILED, EXECUTION_TIMEOUT, INTENT_VIOLATION); a code nobody can emit is a promise to a caller the engine never keeps. SAFEGUARD_VIOLATION is kept although nothing raises it yet: it has a caller-facing message in SAFE_ERROR_MESSAGES, so it is a declared refusal path. test_boundary_tidy_ups.py asserts the rule.

A run that hits the global timeout returns PIPELINE_TIMEOUT and an answer: the apology is written where the answer synthesizer writes its own, so QueryResult.final_answer carries it. It used to be written to a top-level state key that result_from_state never read, so every caller through the SDK and the REST route saw final_answer: null with only the error code.

QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE (severity ERROR) comes from the datasource resolver when its answerability check finds that no datasource the role may read can answer the question, such as "what is the weather in Paris?". The run ends before the decomposer: no decomposer, planner, refiner or synthesizer call is made, QueryResult.status is error, and the message tells the user the question can't be answered from the connected data. The check is told to answer "answerable" when unsure. See DatasourceResolverNode.

docs.title: Provider failures
docs.text:
When the model provider refuses or fails a call, the LLM node that made it (datasource resolver, decomposer, AST planner, refiner, answer synthesizer) reports it through nl2sql.llm.failures.provider_error instead of its own failure code, so every caller (SDK, REST API, playground) gets the same entry. classify_provider_error reads the OpenAI and Anthropic SDK exceptions by shape (the anthropic SDK is an optional extra, so it is never imported), looking through what the exception was raised from:

error_code when message (for OpenAI) PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED HTTP 401, or 403 "OpenAI rejected the API key." PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED HTTP 429 "OpenAI rate limited the request." PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED HTTP 429 with insufficient_quota "OpenAI says this API key has no quota left." PROVIDER_TIMEOUT the SDK's timeout, or HTTP 408 "OpenAI did not answer in time." PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE a connection error, or HTTP 5xx "OpenAI could not be reached." / "OpenAI had a server error and could not answer." PROVIDER_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE HTTP 404, or model_not_found "OpenAI does not offer the configured model to this API key."
  • message is one sentence naming the provider. It never carries the key (masked or not), a Python repr, or the node's own label.
  • provider is the provider as a person names it (PROVIDER_LABELS in llm/providers.py): Anthropic for the Anthropic SDK, otherwise the preset whose endpoint the call went to. A base_url no preset names is "The model provider".
  • provider_response is the provider's own words, such as HTTP 401 (invalid_api_key): Incorrect API key provided: [redacted key]. ..., for a "provider response" disclosure. redact_keys replaces anything key-like (a bearer token, an sk-/pk-/rk- key whole or masked, any unbroken run of 32 or more letters, digits, - or _) with [redacted key]. The error of a failed call in usage.calls is redacted the same way.
  • Every PROVIDER_* code is fatal (is_retryable is false): a refinement retry would make the same call to the same provider with the same key.
  • An HTTP 400 is not classified. It is a request the engine built wrongly, or a model refusing a parameter, and the node's own error explains it better.

run_with_graph()'s fallback applies the same classification, so a provider failure that escapes its node is not UNKNOWN_ERROR.

docs.title: Circuit breaker
docs.text:
create_breaker() configures pybreaker.CircuitBreaker instances with observability hooks. The system defines exactly one:

  • VECTOR_BREAKER (fail_max=5, reset_timeout=30)

Retrieval calls in VectorStore are wrapped with VECTOR_BREAKER. It is the only breaker instance the system defines: LLM calls and SQL execution are not breaker-guarded, and their failures surface as PipelineError values in state.

docs.title: Failure flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Node[Pipeline Node] --> Error[PipelineError]
    Error --> State[GraphState.errors]
    State --> Retry{is_retryable?}
    Retry -->|yes| Refine[RefinerNode / retry loop]
    Retry -->|no| Stop[Terminate branch]

See ../architecture/failure_recovery.md for failure domains, retry scope, and recovery limitations.

docs.title: Cancellation and timeouts
docs.text:
• run_with_graph() enforces a global timeout (Settings.global_timeout_sec).
  • Cancellation is honored through a per-run nl2sql.common.cancellation.CancellationToken, passed to the graph via config["configurable"]["cancellation_token"], so cancelling one run never affects another.
  • run_with_graph() never raises: cancellation, timeout, routing failures and unexpected crashes all come back as PipelineError values in state. A PipelineExecutionError is unwrapped so its original error_code survives; only genuinely unrecognised exceptions become UNKNOWN_ERROR.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Error contracts: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/errors.py
  • Circuit breaker: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/resilience.py
  • Retry logic: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/sql_agent.py
  • Cancellation: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/cancellation.py

docs.title: Feedback and Signals
docs.text:
Nothing in the engine can tell on its own whether a live answer was right. Two small signals help: a person's rating of an answer in the playground, and the guardrail rates the engine already records for every run. nl2sql feedback reads both. Thumbs-up runs can then be exported as draft entries for the gold set, and thumbs-up generated answers as proposed verified queries.

The playground and nl2sql feedback are both built on engine.feedback (record, list, stats, export, clear), which any Python caller can use too: see the public facade.

docs.title: Rating an answer in the playground
docs.text:
After a run, below Cost & time, the playground asks Was this answer right? with two buttons, 👍 Right and 👎 Wrong. A click saves the rating at once. A note is optional: pick Wrong number, Wrong table, Wrong filter or Missing rows, or type a few words (up to 280 characters), then Save note. Rating the same run again replaces the earlier rating.

The page sends only the run's trace id, the rating and the note. The server stores what it answered for that run, from its own copy of the last 200 runs, so a page cannot put a question or SQL into the table that the engine never produced. A run the playground did not answer is refused with 404.

Route Gate GET /api/feedback Whether feedback is on (and why not), the counts and the last 50 ratings. The ratings are returned only where the gate below passes. POST /api/feedback {"trace_id", "rating": "up" \| "down", "note"}. Local only, the same gate as Settings, Rebuild and the Retrieval inspector: on a non-loopback --host it answers 403 unless nl2sql demo --allow-settings, and it refuses another site's page (a foreign Origin), a non-loopback hostname and anything but JSON.

Feedback is available in the playground that nl2sql demo starts, and on by default. settings.feedback.enabled: false turns it off: the control then says so and POST /api/feedback answers 403.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
One row per run in a feedback table inside the SQLite schema store (<storage.path>/state.db, nl2sql-demo/.nl2sql/state.db in the demo), beside the schema snapshots and the plan cache. No new service or file.

Column Holds trace_id The run's id (primary key), the same id as its trace file. created_at Unix time of the rating. rating, note up or down, and the optional note. question, role, status The question as asked, the role it ran as, and the result status (success, plan_only, error). sql The generated SQL per sub-query, as a JSON list. Empty for a run the role was refused (SECURITY_VIOLATION). error_codes The blocking error codes, as a JSON list. Codes only, never messages. retries, validator_failures, plan_cache_hits, sub_queries The run's guardrail counters (below). models The provider and model each LLM node ran on, as JSON. engine_version The nl2sql-engine version, plus the git commit when run from a checkout. datasource_ids The datasources the run's sub-queries ran on, each once, as a JSON list. source Where the answer came from: verified (a verified query from curated.yaml) or generated.

datasource_ids and source were added after the table first shipped. A store from before them gains both columns, empty, the next time it is opened; the rows already in it keep their ratings and read the two as null.

Privacy. A row never holds result rows, the written answer, sample values, error messages or keys. It holds only what the run showed the role it ran as: the SQL of a refused run is dropped, and error messages (which can name a forbidden table) are not kept. nl2sql feedback clear deletes every row.

docs.title: Guardrail rates: nl2sql feedback stats
docs.text:
nl2sql feedback stats          # a table
nl2sql feedback stats --json   # the same numbers as JSON
nl2sql feedback stats --traces other/traces

stats counts every recorded run once, keyed by trace id: the feedback rows, plus every trace in <storage.path>/traces when settings.traces.mode kept them (the demo's config sets always). When a run has both, its counters come from the trace, which also sees a validator rejection a retry then fixed, and its rating from the row.

Signal Counted as Thumbs up / down Ratings; the rates are over rated runs. Refused, by code Runs that ended with SECURITY_VIOLATION or QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE. Refiner retried Runs with at least one retry (retry_count summed over sub-queries). Validator rejected a plan Runs where the logical validator rejected a plan at least once. Errored, by code Runs with any other blocking error code. Plan cache hits Sub-queries whose plan came from the plan cache, over all planned sub-queries.

Every other rate is over all runs. From canned data (four rated runs, three more traces):

7 runs, 4 rated (feedback table plus traces in traces)

  Signal                                 Runs             Rate
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Thumbs up                                 2   50.0% of rated
  Thumbs down                               2   50.0% of rated
  Refused                                   2            28.6%
    SECURITY_VIOLATION                      1            14.3%
    QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE                 1            14.3%
  Refiner retried (3 retries)               2            28.6%
  Validator rejected a plan (2 times)       2            28.6%
  Errored                                   1            14.3%
    DB_EXECUTION_ERROR                      1            14.3%
  Plan cache hits (2 of 5 sub-queries)      2            40.0%

nl2sql feedback list prints the ratings, newest first, with their notes.

docs.title: Growing the gold set: nl2sql feedback export --good
docs.text:
nl2sql feedback export --good                     # feedback_gold_drafts.yaml
nl2sql feedback export --good --out drafts.yaml

Each thumbs-up run becomes a draft entry in the shape of chinook_gold.yaml (GoldQuestion in nl2sql/evaluation/gold.py): the question, the run's SQL as the gold_sql candidate, empty tags, needed_tables and needed_columns, difficulty: medium, expected set to allowed for the role it ran as, and no gold_result. A run with no SQL, or with more than one statement, is skipped: gold_sql is one query. The drafts go to their own file; export never writes the gold set, and refuses an --out that points at it.

A person must review every draft before it joins the gold set. A thumbs up says an answer looked right, not that its SQL is the reference answer. Check the SQL answers the question, fill in difficulty, tags, needed_tables, needed_columns and expected (add the roles that must be refused), copy the entry into chinook_gold.yaml, and run the gold generator to write its gold_result:

python -m nl2sql.evaluation.gold

docs.title: Proposing verified queries: nl2sql curated proposals export
docs.text:
A thumbs-up on a generated answer can also become a proposed verified query for curated.yaml, for a person to review and commit:

nl2sql curated proposals export --out curated.proposals.yaml

Runs answered by a verified query, failed runs, runs on more than one datasource and runs with no SQL are skipped, and rows rated before the table recorded the datasource are skipped too. See From feedback to verified queries.

docs.title: Turning it off and clearing it
docs.text:
• settings.feedback.enabled: false stops the playground recording ratings.
  • nl2sql feedback clear deletes every rating (--yes skips the prompt). Schema snapshots and the plan cache are kept, and nl2sql cache clear never touches the ratings.

docs.title: Observability Stack
docs.text:
NL2SQL provides structured logging always, per-question token and time telemetry on every run, plus OpenTelemetry metrics and audit events.

Read the scope literally, because it is narrow:

  • Every run reports its cost and timings in the result. run_with_graph() always attaches NodeTimingCallback (wall-clock seconds per node, into QueryResult.timings) and TokenUsageCallback (LLM calls, input / cached / output / reasoning tokens and model seconds per node and per question, into QueryResult.usage). That covers the Python API, the REST API, the CLI and the demo playground. See the query API.
  • The token counter is recorded on every run; the node-duration histogram is CLI-only. TokenUsageCallback records nl2sql.token.usage for every caller. nl2sql run records nl2sql.node.duration from the node_finished events of engine.stream_query, the same events any caller can read.
  • Metrics are off by default. OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER defaults to none, which installs no meter provider, so every recording is discarded. The supported values are none, console and otlp.
  • There is no tracing. No span is ever started anywhere in the codebase, and there is no Jaeger exporter and no Prometheus exporter. opentelemetry-exporter-otlp is the only exporter dependency, and it is used for metrics over gRPC.
  • The audit log records exactly one event type, llm.changed, written when engine.llm.replace swaps the LLM. It is not a record of queries executed, roles, validation decisions or row counts.

docs.title: Telemetry flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pipeline as run_with_graph()
    participant Usage as TokenUsageCallback
    participant Stream as stream_query events
    participant Run as nl2sql run (CLI only)
    participant Metrics as OpenTelemetry metrics
    participant Result as QueryResult

    Pipeline->>Usage: always attached
    Usage->>Metrics: nl2sql.token.usage
    Usage->>Result: usage
    Pipeline->>Stream: node_started, node_finished
    Stream->>Run: each event
    Run->>Metrics: configure_metrics(), nl2sql.node.duration

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
configure_metrics() installs an OpenTelemetry meter provider. Exported metrics include:

  • nl2sql.node.duration (histogram), attribute node. CLI only.
  • nl2sql.token.usage (counter), attributes node, model, datasource_id and type: one point per LLM call for each of input, cached_input, cache_write_input, output, reasoning and total. Every run.
  • nl2sql.plan_cache.lookups (counter), attributes result (hit or miss) and datasource_id: one point per plan cache lookup by the AST planner. Every run with PLAN_CACHE_ENABLED on. The per-question view is QueryResult.usage.plan_cache_hits and sub_queries[].plan_source; see Determinism → The plan cache.

configure_metrics() is called by nl2sql run, with the exporter the config's settings.observability names, so outside the CLI no meter provider is installed unless the embedding application installs one; the counter is then recorded against OpenTelemetry's no-op provider and discarded. Token usage is not kept in a process-wide list; read it from QueryResult.usage.

docs.title: Audit logging
docs.text:
EventLogger writes JSON events to a rotating log file at logs/audit_events.log (relative to the working directory, 10 MB × 5). Payloads are sanitized to redact sensitive keys.

The only event written anywhere in the codebase is llm.changed, from engine.llm.replace (the Python API, PUT /api/v1/settings/llm and the playground's model switch). Its payload is who made the change (via, and the user id and roles when known) and each agent whose provider or model changed, old and new; never a key. The llm_interaction event the CLI's monitor callback used to write went with that callback, when nl2sql run moved onto the public API. Treat the log as a record of model changes, not as a compliance audit trail.

docs.title: Structured logging
docs.text: The library does not configure logging on import; the application entry point calls nl2sql.configure_logging after loading the .env next to nl2sql.yaml, so a NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL there applies (the REST API does it in its lifespan, the CLI before every command, nl2sql demo again once the demo project's .env is loaded). JSON formatting is enabled when Settings.observability_exporter == "otlp". Trace and tenant context helpers exist (trace_context, tenant_context), but the pipeline does not set them; callers must establish context if they want trace/tenant IDs in logs.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Metrics: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/metrics.py
  • Audit logging: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/event_logger.py
  • The CLI's step timings: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/cli/commands/run.py
  • Token usage: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/services/callbacks/token_handler.py
  • Logging: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/logger.py

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
What each release is for, in plain words. The full list of commits is in CHANGELOG.md. How a release is cut is in Releasing.

  • 0.5.0: Configuration v2, one nl2sql.yaml, an extension registry, a namespaced Python API and per-engine config; a clean break from 0.4.
  • 0.4.1: admin-only REST routes, opt-in enrichment, schema-aware policies and a datasource that fails no longer stops startup.
  • 0.4.0: curated answers, where a question that matches a verified query runs its reviewed SQL and is labelled verified.
  • 0.3.0: results at any size, paged and downloadable, with a 20-row preview for the answer and a streamed run.
  • 0.2.4: a cached plan is reused only on the day it was made, so relative dates stay current.
  • 0.2.3: the model knows today's date and its data, and wrong or empty queries are retried or explained.
  • 0.2.2: correct answers or clear refusals for multi-sub-query questions, and the demo at nl2sql.codewithnk.com.
  • 0.2.1: the release image on Python 3.12, and a reliable Space deploy.
  • 0.2.0: the hosted demo, with or without a key, and pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]".
  • 0.1.2: a merged release PR publishes to PyPI on its own.
  • 0.1.1: fixes for nl2sql doctor, the Docker demo, pipeline errors and the API image.
  • 0.1.0: the first release, as three packages on PyPI.

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.0
docs.text:
The first release: the NL2SQL engine, its REST API and the adapter SDK on PyPI as three packages that share one version.

Released 2026-08-28.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• pip install nl2sql-engine gives you the engine and the nl2sql CLI. nl2sql-api serves it over REST, and nl2sql-adapter-sdk is what a third-party database adapter builds against.
  • The model writes a typed plan, never SQL. The plan is checked against the schema and your role before any SQL is generated.
  • A DuckDB adapter joins PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and SQLite.
  • The Docker demo now starts the application as well as its databases, so it can answer a question with nothing else installed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• A DuckDB adapter, installed with the nl2sql-engine[duckdb] extra (#57).
  • The Docker demo runs the application next to its databases. SQL Server is now opt-in, so the first start skips a 1.6 GB download (#59).
  • Releases are automated: release-please writes the changelog, and a merged release PR publishes to PyPI (#58).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Cancelling one run no longer cancels every other run in the process (#48).
  • The REST API needs its CORS origins listed. It no longer accepts any origin together with credentials (#49).
  • The minimum versions of pydantic, langgraph and chromadb are now correct (#50).
  • Importing nl2sql no longer changes your application's logging setup (#51).
  • The NL2SQL facade builds its settings API correctly (#52).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README and architecture docs now describe only code that exists (#54), and the docs cover the three-package layout (#60).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No API image was published to GHCR for 0.1.0, because the image build failed. 0.1.1 fixes the build.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install "nl2sql-engine==0.1.0"

Breaking changes: nine earlier distributions are now three, nl2sql-engine, nl2sql-api and nl2sql-adapter-sdk, and the dialect adapters ship inside the engine (#56). The import name is still nl2sql.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.1.1, with fixes for the CLI, the Docker demo and the release pipeline.

Full changelog: CHANGELOG.md

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.1
docs.text:
A fix release for 0.1.0: nl2sql doctor, the Docker demo and pipeline errors now work as documented, and the API image builds.

Released 2026-09-07.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• nl2sql doctor, the command you run when something is wrong, no longer crashes.
  • The Docker demo can reach its databases and survives a terminal that cannot show prompts.
  • A question that no subgraph can answer ends with a clear error code, not a crash.
  • The API image builds and is published to GHCR.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• nl2sql doctor checks connectivity again instead of failing on an import (#72).
  • A secrets config with every provider commented out is read as "no secret providers", not an error (#73).
  • The Docker demo's datasources are reachable: only passwords are treated as secrets when a config is resolved (#74).
  • nl2sql setup --demo --docker no longer crashes under Git Bash on Windows (#79).
  • When no subgraph matches a question, the pipeline raises a real error (#75), and its error code reaches the caller (#78).
  • The API image is built from the repository root, which fixes the GHCR publish that failed on 0.1.0 (#70).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The docs match the code again (#77).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Tagging 0.1.1 did not publish it, because the PyPI upload failed in CI. The packages and the image went out about an hour later, by a manual re-run once the fix that shipped as 0.1.2 was on main.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.1.1"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.1.2, which fixes publishing to PyPI from the release workflow.

Full changelog: v0.1.0...v0.1.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.2
docs.text:
A release-pipeline fix: a merged release PR now reaches PyPI on its own. The packages are the same as 0.1.1.

Released 2026-09-07.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Merging the release PR publishes all three packages to PyPI with no manual step. On 0.1.1, that upload failed.
  • Library code has not changed since 0.1.1.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • The release workflow publishes without PEP 740 attestations. Through the called workflow, PyPI rejected them (#80).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Released packages have no PEP 740 provenance attestations. That is the cost of this fix.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.1.2"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.0, the hosted demo.

Full changelog: v0.1.1...v0.1.2

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.0
docs.text:
The hosted demo release: try NL2SQL in a browser, without a key or with your own, or run the same playground locally with pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]".

Released 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• A public demo on Hugging Face Spaces (https://nadeem4nk-nl2sql-demo.hf.space). It asks three linked sample databases in plain English and shows the plan, the checks, the SQL and the rows.
  • No key needed to start. Twenty guided questions replay real recorded answers. For anything else, bring your own key; it stays in your browser tab and is used for that one request only.
  • pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]" and nl2sql demo run the same playground on your machine. It has a home page, an answer-first Ask page, a Pipeline page and a Retrieval inspector.
  • Claude is supported natively alongside OpenAI-compatible providers, and each step can use its own model.
  • A release now runs end to end on its own: tag, PyPI, a fresh install check, then the Space at the same version.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Hosted mode: a public demo where each visitor brings their own key and the server holds none (#165), plus the Dockerfile and Space config to run it (#168).
  • Try the hosted demo without a key, on recorded runs (#197), with real recorded answers for the 20 guided questions (#205).
  • The React playground and nl2sql demo (#93), now with a home page (#198), an answer-first Ask page (#186) and a Pipeline page (#171).
  • Support and web-analytics sample databases, linked to Chinook customers (#157).
  • Native Claude support, and a provider per pipeline step (#124). In the hosted demo, each step can use its own model, with a key per provider (#173).
  • QueryResult exposes the plan, the validation checks, a row sample, the status and timings (#88).
  • Every run can be recorded to a trace file, viewed, and replayed without the model (#104).
  • Validated plans are cached by question and schema version, and checked again on every use (#122).
  • An evaluation harness: a Chinook gold dataset (#114), a tier 1 check on every PR (#119) and a tier 2 benchmark against real models (#126).
  • Each tagged release deploys the Space, pinned to the version on PyPI (#196).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The validator rejects a plan whose tables cannot be joined before SQL is generated, so the model can try again (#161). Only known function names are allowed in plans (#137).
  • Role checks refuse without leaking data from forbidden tables, and deny unknown or empty roles cleanly (#112).
  • API keys and connection secrets are held as SecretStr, so they never print (#113).
  • When a sub-query fails, you get a structured result, not a crash or a loop (#84). The pipeline timeout is enforced (#87).
  • The aggregator combines sub-query results correctly when join keys carry a prefix (#144, #162).
  • Many smaller fixes to the generator, the decomposer, the CLI and the demo. See the changelog below.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README is organised around a quickstart, results, the CLI, the REST API and screenshots (#131), and links the live demo (#191).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No API image was published to GHCR for 0.2.0: its Dockerfile used Python 3.11. The first Space deploy also failed, on a PyPI index that had not caught up. Both are fixed in 0.2.1.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.
  • A question that needs several sub-queries can be answered wrong without an error. 0.2.2 fixes the known cases.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.0"

Breaking changes: Chinook is now the only demo dataset. nl2sql setup --demo --lite, --demo --docker and nl2sql demo --dataset are removed, and nl2sql setup --demo sets up Chinook (#98).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.1, which fixes the release image and makes the Space deploy reliable.

Full changelog: v0.1.2...v0.2.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.1
docs.text:
A release-pipeline fix for 0.2.0: the API image is built on Python 3.12, and the hosted demo deploys reliably. The library is unchanged.

Released 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api is published again. 0.2.1 is the first image of the 0.2 line.
  • The Space deploy waits until PyPI serves the new version, and retries its install.
  • A Space deploy only passes when the Space is actually running.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The release image moves to Python 3.12, which every package requires. A new PR check builds the image, so a broken Dockerfile fails before release (#208).
  • The Space deploy waits for PyPI to list the version before it pushes, and the Space's install retries up to ten times (#208).
  • A redeploy that pushes nothing asks for a rebuild, and the job fails unless the Space ends up running (#208).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• There is no nl2sql-api:0.2.0 image. Use 0.2.1 or later.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.
  • A question that needs several sub-queries can be answered wrong without an error. 0.2.2 fixes the known cases.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.1"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.2, with correctness fixes for questions answered from several sub-queries.

Full changelog: v0.2.0...v0.2.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.2
docs.text:
A correctness release: a question answered from several sub-queries now gets the right answer or a clear refusal, never a silently wrong one. The live demo also moves to https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com.

Released 2026-10-11.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Each sub-query writes its own result file. Before this, two sub-queries of one question could overwrite each other, and a join could combine a result with itself.
  • A join or compare is refused if it lost one of its inputs, for example to a role restriction, instead of being answered from the side that remained.
  • A join or compare is refused if one input was cut short by the row cap. Missing rows mean missing matches.
  • The hosted demo has its own domain, https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: • The link preview and the release checks use nl2sql.codewithnk.com, the Space's custom domain (#212).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• One result artifact per sub-query, at <tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet. A failed aggregation now ends the run instead of asking the model to explain an empty result (#213).
  • A join or compare that lost one of its inputs is refused with PLANNER_FAILED, before any query runs. The message does not name the restricted datasource (#214).
  • A join or compare on a sub-query that hit the row cap is refused with RESULT_TRUNCATED. A union on a capped input still runs, with a warning (#215).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README and docs link the live demo at nl2sql.codewithnk.com (#210).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Questions across several databases are not yet supported end to end. Each database answers its own sub-query and the results are joined in memory. This release makes that safer, not complete.
  • Each sub-query returns at most 1,000 rows by default (the datasource's row_limit). A join over a larger input is refused rather than answered.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.2"

Breaking changes: none. The default result artifact path gains a <sub_query_id> level. A custom RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATH_TEMPLATE keeps working: the sub-query id is added to its file name.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: cross-database queries, so one question can be answered from several databases.

Full changelog: v0.2.1...v0.2.2

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.3
docs.text:
A correctness release: the model now knows today's date, what values a column holds and where its data starts and ends, and a query that comes back wrong or empty is retried or explained instead of answered as fact.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• "This year" and "the last 30 days" are resolved against today's date, not a year the model guessed. When the period falls outside the data, the planner uses the latest period the data has and says so.
  • A filter on a value the column does not hold, such as 'Metal' for 'Heavy Metal', no longer turns into a confident "none". A close match is retried once; a missing value is named as a warning in the answer.
  • A query the database rejects as wrong (an unknown column, a type mismatch, bad syntax) goes back to the refiner for another try, instead of ending the run.
  • A column the plan names but the schema does not have is caught before the query runs, and the planner is asked to fix it.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Strict column checking is on by default: an unknown column is a retryable COLUMN_NOT_FOUND. LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS=false restores the old warning (#219).
  • The plan's offset is rendered, so "rows 11 to 20" no longer returns rows 1 to 10. An offset without an order is refused before generation (#221).
  • A query the database rejects as wrong is retried through the refiner. A refusal (permission, timeout, connection) still ends the run. Retry feedback carries only the latest error, with no SQL echo or stack trace (#223).
  • An empty result that filtered on a missing value is checked: a close stored value sends the plan back once, otherwise the answer carries a warning such as "There is no Genre with Name 'Polka'." (#226).
  • DATE and DATETIME leave the function allow-list, which now matches the planner prompt. STRFTIME is still accepted as a legacy name (#218).
  • The planner and refiner are told today's date. NL2SQL_TODAY pins it; unset, it is the UTC date (#220).
  • A text column with 50 or fewer distinct values keeps all of them in the index, not five samples (#222).
  • Date and numeric columns carry their data range in the prompt, with a rule for relative periods outside it (#224).
  • Two gold questions cover data ranges and value matching. The gold set is now 47 questions (#225).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • Every version has a release page, written by a skill and required in CI before a release (#216).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Each query returns at most 1,000 rows by default, and the answer model sees the whole result.
  • A cached plan for a relative-date question ("this month") can be reused on a later day. 0.2.4 fixes this.
  • "Rows 11 to 20" reaches the planner only through the question text.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.3"

Breaking changes: none. Two behaviour changes: an unknown column is now a retried error rather than a warning (set LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS=false for the old behaviour), and a plan calling DATE or DATETIME is refused. Re-index an existing demo folder to pick up the full column values: nl2sql setup --demo or nl2sql --env demo index.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.4, starting with cached plans for relative-date questions.

Full changelog: v0.2.2...v0.2.3

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.4
docs.text:
A cache fix: a cached plan is now reused only on the day it was made, so a relative-date question such as "the last 30 days" is never answered with an earlier day's dates.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• "This year", "the last 30 days" and "yesterday" are planned against today's date, even when the same question was asked on an earlier day. Before this, the plan cache could serve an earlier day's plan with that day's dates.
  • Every cached plan carries the date it was made, not only plans that look date-relative, because nothing reliably tells which plans depend on today. A plan is reused for the rest of that day, or for as long as NL2SQL_TODAY pins the date.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • The plan cache key includes the run date (#228).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Each query returns at most 1,000 rows by default, and the answer model sees the whole result.
  • "Rows 11 to 20" reaches the planner only through the question text.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.4"

Breaking changes: none. Plans cached before the upgrade no longer match and are planned again once.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.3.0, starting with larger results.

Full changelog: v0.2.3...v0.2.4

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.3.0
docs.text:
Results at any size: a question can now return up to 100,000 rows by default, the whole result is saved and can be paged through or downloaded as CSV, and the answer model reads a 20-row preview instead of every row.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• The default row cap rises from 1,000 to 100,000 (10,000 in the demo). A result that hits the cap is flagged, and the answer says it is incomplete and asks you to narrow the question.
  • The answer model sees the first 20 rows and the total count, not the whole result, so a large result no longer fills the prompt.
  • Every run's result is saved whole. Page through it or download it as CSV from the SDK, nl2sql-api or the playground, where each result gets its own tab and every sub-query is shown.
  • A run can stream its progress and its answer as Server-Sent Events. The playground lights up each step as it finishes and writes the answer as it arrives.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The answer model gets a 20-row preview and the row count (ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS). RESULT_ROW_LIMIT (default 100,000) replaces the 1,000-row cap, and a result cut at the cap is flagged in truncated and in the answer's warnings (#231).
  • Results are fetched in batches of RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE rows through a new optional StreamingAdapterProtocol; adapters without it work unchanged. Each run's combined result is saved as parquet in its artifact folder (#234).
  • A run writes a manifest.json of its results, returned as QueryResult.result_manifest. get_result_manifest, get_result_page and export_result_csv read a result back, and nl2sql-api and the playground serve the same as page and CSV routes (#235).
  • The playground pages through the saved result 100 rows at a time, shows a tab per result, downloads the full CSV and shows every sub-query in the Plan and SQL steps (#236).
  • NL2SQL.stream_query, POST /api/v1/query/stream and the playground's /api/ask/stream send a run's progress, its result manifest and its answer token by token as Server-Sent Events. The playground falls back to the non-streaming call if the stream fails (#237).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • A datasource's row_limit, statement_timeout_ms and max_bytes written beside connection, as the docs show, are now honoured; they were silently ignored. If a limit is set both there and under options, the lower wins (#233).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Anyone with a role who knows a run's id can read its saved result. There is no access check beyond the tenant's folder.
  • The downloaded CSV does not guard against spreadsheet formulas in cell values.
  • A join, sort or group-by across results may still hold its inputs in memory (as polars columns, not Python rows).
  • When a stream breaks, the playground asks the question again without streaming, so it is run a second time.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.3.0"

Breaking changes: none. Three behaviour changes:

  • The default row cap is 100,000, not 1,000. To keep a lower cap, set RESULT_ROW_LIMIT or a datasource's row_limit.
  • terminal_results now holds only the 20-row preview. The full result is the saved artifact; read it with get_result_page or export_result_csv.
  • Every run writes its combined result as parquet and a manifest.json in its artifact folder. On S3 or ADLS, the manifest needs s3fs or adlfs installed.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.4.0.

Full changelog: v0.2.4...v0.3.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.4.0
docs.text:
Curated answers: a data team can write verified queries, reviewed SQL with typed parameters, and when a question matches one the engine runs that SQL with the values bound instead of generating new SQL, and labels the answer as verified. Any other question is answered by generated SQL, as before.

Released 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Write verified queries in configs/curated.yaml: a description, the phrasings people ask, typed parameters and the SQL. When a question matches one, its reviewed SQL runs with the values bound by the driver, never pasted into the text.
  • An answer from a verified query says so. QueryResult.source is verified or generated in the SDK, the REST response and the trace, and the playground shows a "Verified" badge with the query's id and values.
  • Point the planner at the tables your team trusts with preferred_tables in datasources.yaml. The built-in adapters now index views as well as tables.
  • Thumbs-up feedback on generated answers can become proposed verified queries with nl2sql curated proposals export, for a person to review and commit.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• configs/curated.yaml, its settings CURATED_CONFIG and CURATED_ENABLED, and nl2sql curated validate, which checks every verified query, its parameters and its SQL against the indexed schema (#240).
  • nl2sql index indexes each verified query's phrasings, nl2sql index --curated-only refreshes only those after an edit, and nl2sql doctor warns when curated.yaml changed since the last index (#242).
  • A new first step, the curated matcher, picks a verified query and its values, checks the values and the role's access in code, and runs the saved SQL with bound parameters; anything else goes to the generated pipeline with a reason in the trace (#243).
  • preferred_tables in datasources.yaml puts those tables first in the schema the planner sees, and the SQLAlchemy-based adapters now snapshot views (#244).
  • The playground's "Verified" badge, six verified queries in the demo, and nl2sql curated test, which runs every verified query once with its defaults or examples (#245).
  • Feedback records the datasources a run used and the answer's source, and nl2sql curated proposals export turns thumbs-up feedback into proposed verified queries (#246).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The design for curated answers: verified queries, preferred tables and feedback proposals, with business metrics deferred (#239).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Matching runs once, on the whole question. A question with two parts falls back to generated SQL, even if one part matches a verified query.
  • A question missing a value a verified query needs falls back to generated SQL; it does not ask a follow-up question.
  • The match threshold (CURATED_MATCH_FLOOR) was calibrated with the local embedding model only.
  • Business metrics are parsed and checked in curated.yaml but not used yet.
  • PostgreSQL materialized views are not indexed.
  • Feedback given before this release cannot become a proposal, because it did not record its datasource.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.4.0"

Breaking changes: none. Curated answers are off unless a curated.yaml exists at the default path or CURATED_CONFIG names one. Two behaviour changes:

  • Views now appear in the schema snapshot of the built-in adapters, so a re-index picks them up.
  • If CURATED_CONFIG points at a missing or broken file, startup fails with a message naming every problem.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.5.0, questions across several databases.

Full changelog: v0.3.0...v0.4.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.4.1
docs.text:
A hardening release: the REST routes that change the server need an admin role, indexing no longer calls the model unless you ask it to, table access is checked by schema as well as table, and one broken datasource no longer stops the engine from starting.

Released 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Adding or removing a datasource, changing the LLM and rebuilding the index over REST now need an admin role. With no role source configured, only clients on the same machine may call them.
  • nl2sql index and the indexing SDK calls no longer spend model tokens by default. Ask for descriptions with --enrich or enrich=True, and the comments already in your database are never overwritten.
  • Policies can name a schema: ds.schema.table and ds.schema.*. A grant on sales.orders no longer lets a plan read audit.orders.
  • A datasource that fails to start is marked unavailable and the rest keep working; a secret provider that fails to start stops startup with a message saying which one and why.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Passwords and user names with @ : / # % now work for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server, and statement_timeout_ms is now enforced on SQL Server and DuckDB too (#249).
  • The REST admin routes require an admin role, a failed POST /datasource no longer echoes the connection string, and nl2sql-api pins the engine release it ships with (#250).
  • A secret provider that cannot start fails startup with a clear error; a datasource that cannot start is listed by list_unavailable_datasources() and in index_health() warnings instead of stopping the engine (#251).
  • Routing respects the answerability check's choice of datasources, and the decomposer now sees each datasource's description and table names (#252).
  • Enrichment is opt-in for every indexing entry point, only fills blank descriptions, logs a failure as one line, and a datasource added in code keeps its description (#254).
  • Tier 2 benchmarks run with curated answers off unless --use-curated is passed, and each case records whether its answer was verified or generated (#255).
  • Indexing profiles each column on its own, so a boolean, UUID, JSON or date column, or one failing query, no longer fails the whole datasource (#256).
  • Table access is decided on datasource, schema and table, the same way in the validator, schema retriever, executor and curated matcher (#257).
  • nl2sql setup checks and offers the right driver for bring-your-own PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB databases, offers DuckDB as a type, and nl2sql install postgres installs the right extra (#258).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• A reverse proxy on the same host makes every request look like it comes from loopback. Set NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER in that case.
  • The REST indexing routes do not take an enrich parameter, so they always index without enrichment.
  • There is no strict mode that fails startup when one datasource cannot start. Use nl2sql doctor as a deploy check.
  • The SQL Server timeout counts whole seconds, so statement_timeout_ms is rounded up.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.4.1"

Breaking changes / behaviour changes: four, each of which needs a look before you upgrade.

  • REST admin routes need an admin role (#250). POST /datasource, DELETE /datasource/{id}, POST /llm, POST /index/{id}, POST /index-all and DELETE /index now need a role listed in NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES (comma-separated, default admin). With no role source configured, only loopback clients are allowed. What to do: set NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER behind a proxy, or NL2SQL_API_ROLE=admin for a single-user deployment. In Docker, requests arrive from the bridge gateway rather than loopback, so one of these is needed.
  • Indexing enrichment is opt-in (#254). index_datasource, index_all_datasources and nl2sql index no longer call the LLM unless you pass enrich=True or --enrich, and enrichment never overwrites table or column comments from the database. What to do: if you relied on generated descriptions, add --enrich or enrich=True to your indexing calls.
  • Two-part policy entries mean the default schema (#257). ds.table now grants that table in the datasource's default schema only (public on PostgreSQL, dbo on SQL Server, the connected database on MySQL, main on SQLite and DuckDB). Three-part ds.schema.table and ds.schema.* entries are supported. What to do: for a table outside the default schema, write ds.schema.table or ds.schema.*. Policies on SQLite datasources, including the demo's, mean what they did before.
  • Startup failures (#251). A configured secret provider that fails to start now stops startup with an error naming it and the reason. A datasource that fails to start no longer stops the engine; it is reported as unavailable. What to do: fix or remove a broken entry in the secrets config, and check list_unavailable_datasources(), GET /api/v1/index/status or nl2sql doctor for datasources that did not start.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.5, Configuration v2 and the extension registry.

Full changelog: v0.4.0...v0.4.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.5.0
docs.text:
Configuration v2: one nl2sql.yaml configures the engine, the CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo, an extension registry loads adapters, LLM, embeddings and secret providers by name, and every engine owns its config. This is a clean break from 0.4, with no compatibility layer: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One config file. nl2sql.yaml replaces the 0.4 files and about 48 environment variables. It can be one file or split into datasources/, llm.yaml, embeddings.yaml, policies.yaml and storage.yaml. nl2sql init writes that layout for you (--demo adds the demo databases). nl2sql config check checks every file, name, driver and secret without starting the engine, and with --connect it also connects to each datasource. It fits a CI job.
  • An extension registry. Registry.default() finds adapters, LLM providers, embeddings providers and secret providers through entry points, and imports none of them until the config uses one.
