Register your own with add_adapter, add_llm, add_embeddings, add_secrets or a decorator (@registry.adapter("name")). A wrong interface version, a missing driver or a misspelled name is reported when the engine is built, with the fix. The SDK they build against is now nl2sql-sdk (import nl2sql_sdk).
  • A tidier Python API, with a model switch at runtime. run_query and stream_query stay at the top level. Everything else is in namespaces: engine.datasources, index, llm, policies, curated, results, traces and feedback, plus about(), check() and close() (or with). engine.llm.replace(...) and the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm swap the model in a running engine. Queries already running finish on the old model, and the change is logged without keys.
  • Each engine owns its config. There are no process-wide settings and nothing writes os.environ, so two engines in one process share nothing. import nl2sql takes about 15 ms instead of about 2.2 s, because it loads no heavy library.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• nl2sql-adapter-sdk is renamed nl2sql-sdk, with the import package nl2sql_sdk (#262).
  • import nl2sql loads no database driver, vector store or model library, and a test holds it under budget (#263).
  • The typed config models, load_config, file: includes, ${env:...} references, strict keys with "did you mean", and one ConfigError that lists every problem (#264).
  • The SDK defines the adapter and secret provider interfaces, with interface versions, driver lists and install hints. Secret provider settings are checked strictly (#265).
  • The extension registry: Registry.default(), add_*, decorators, and the entry point groups nl2sql.adapters, nl2sql.llms, nl2sql.embeddings and nl2sql.secrets (#266).
  • nl2sql init [DIR] [--demo] [--provider NAME] [--force] writes the split config layout and checks it (#267).
  • The engine is built from a Config: NL2SQL(config), NL2SQL.from_config(path), NL2SQL.demo(), check() and close(). Building never connects, and all results are written under storage.path (#268).
  • The pipeline reads its settings from its own engine, so two engines in one process each keep their own row limit, plan cache and model (#269).
  • engine.llm.replace, with LLM clients cached per engine, and a plan cache key that includes the planner's model (#270).
  • Indexing, tracing, replay and benchmarks run on run-scoped settings and never change the engine they run on (#271).
  • The CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo start from nl2sql.yaml with a single --config flag. nl2sql setup and every 0.4 config path are removed (#272).
  • nl2sql config check [--connect], which is also callable from Python as nl2sql.config.check.check_config (#273).
  • The namespaced facade and PUT /api/v1/settings/llm. The CLI now uses only the public API (#274).
  • engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about() and engine.llm.providers(). The playground now uses only the public API (#275).
  • The process-wide settings object is deleted. The library writes no environment variables and reads only an allow-list of them (#276).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Secrets in the config are masked when it is printed, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL set in .env takes effect, and the scripts no longer write the environment (#277).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The design for Configuration v2 and the extension registry (#260). The Configuration pages are rewritten for nl2sql.yaml in the PRs above.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Running several nl2sql-api replicas is not supported for a model switch. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm changes only the process that receives it, and the change is not saved: a restart reads llm.yaml again.
  • There is no migration command. You map 0.4 files and variables by hand, using the table.
  • Results are stored locally only. The S3 and ADLS backends are gone until the results-store interface in Phase 2.
  • nl2sql init is not interactive, and its --provider accepts openai, anthropic and openrouter only (Ollama has no default model). The guided setup flow comes in Phase 4.
  • A datasource's connection block is checked by the adapter only, not by a typed model, and check() gives a generic reason when a connection fails. Typed connection models and connection-test stages come with SDK v2 in Phase 2.
  • After engine.datasources.remove(id), the datasource's index entries stay until the next full index.build or index.clear.
  • This release is Phase 1 of five. Phase 2 brings SDK v2, storage interfaces and policy globs, Phase 3 the event bus and evals, Phase 4 the guided setup and the web app on nl2sql-api, and Phase 5 glossaries and knowledge sources.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.5.0"

Adapter and secret provider authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.5.0" and uninstall nl2sql-adapter-sdk.

Breaking changes: many. 0.5 is a clean break with no compatibility layer, and the engine refuses a 0.4 config. Start with nl2sql init, then move your values across with the 0.4 to 0.5 mapping.

  • One config file (#264, #272). configs/datasources.yaml, llm.yaml, policies.json, secrets.yaml, curated.yaml, sample_questions.yaml and about 48 environment variables are no longer read. What to do: run nl2sql init (or nl2sql init --demo) and move each value to its new place using the mapping table. Sample questions now sit on each datasource, policies are YAML, and LLM agents are keyed by node name (ast_planner).
  • Environment variables (#276). Only NL2SQL_CONFIG, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL and the provider keys (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) are read directly. What to do: write any other value in the YAML, as ${env:VAR} where it should come from the environment.
  • .env loading (#272). Only the CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql demo load a .env, and only the one next to nl2sql.yaml. They never override a variable that is already set. The library never reads .env. --env, --env-file, ENV, APP_ENV and ENV_FILE_PATH are gone. What to do: put .env next to nl2sql.yaml. From Python, call nl2sql.load_env_file(path) before building the engine.
  • nl2sql setup is removed (#272). What to do: use nl2sql init, or nl2sql init --demo in place of setup --demo.
  • One CLI flag (#272). nl2sql --config PATH/nl2sql.yaml <command> (or NL2SQL_CONFIG, or ./nl2sql.yaml) replaces every per-command path flag (--llm-config, --secrets-config, --policies-config, --vector-store, and the curated and policy path flags). What to do: pass --config once, before the command.
  • nl2sql-api settings (#272). The NL2SQL_API_* variables are removed. What to do: set api.role_header, api.role, api.trust_body_role and api.cors_origins (a list) in an api: section, and the admin roles in policies.admin_roles. The API image reads NL2SQL_CONFIG=/etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml, so mount your config folder there.
  • REST LLM route (#274). POST /api/v1/llm is replaced by the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm, whose body is the llm section as JSON. A bad body gets a 422 with the config error. POST /api/v1/datasource takes the datasource in the nl2sql.yaml shape, and the datasource routes return DatasourceInfo. What to do: update your clients.
  • Result storage (#268). The S3 and ADLS backends and the RESULT_ARTIFACT_* settings are removed. Results are written under storage.path/results/. What to do: set storage.path and copy anything you need from a remote store yourself.
  • Secret providers (#265). hashi is renamed hashicorp, with no alias. The VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN and AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL fallbacks are removed, and an unknown provider setting is an error. What to do: write type: hashicorp and give url and token (for example token: "${env:VAULT_TOKEN}"), or vault_url for Azure, in the provider's block.
  • The SDK package (#262). nl2sql-adapter-sdk / nl2sql_adapter_sdk is now nl2sql-sdk / nl2sql_sdk. Adapters also declare interface_version, driver_modules and install_hint (#265). What to do: rename the dependency and the imports, add the three class attributes, and register through the nl2sql.adapters entry point or Registry.add_adapter.
  • The Python facade (#274, #275). The flat methods, engine.context, engine.query, get_adapter, configure_llm, reload_llm_config, the auth, settings, policy, indexing and datasource sub-APIs, and the QueryAPI/DatasourceAPI/LLM_API/... exports are removed. NL2SQL() is built from a Config or NL2SQL.from_config(path). What to do: call the namespaces (engine.datasources.add, engine.index.build, engine.llm.replace, engine.policies.validate, ...). The public facade page lists them.
  • Hosted demo (#276). nl2sql demo --hosted refuses to start if OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in its environment. NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED and NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_* are replaced by --hosted, --questions-per-minute and --questions-per-session, and the demo's key file is <dir>/.env instead of .env.demo (#272). What to do: remove provider keys from the hosted server's environment and use the flags.
  • Startup errors (#268). Anything wrong that can be found without connecting is now a ConfigError when the engine is built. This includes an unknown datasource type and a secret that does not resolve, which in 0.4 only marked that datasource unavailable. A datasource that cannot connect still runs degraded unless it is required: true. What to do: run nl2sql config check before you deploy.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.6, datasources and adapter SDK v2, then the web app on the API and Docker Compose.

Full changelog: v0.4.1...v0.5.0

docs.title: Schema & Metadata Layer
docs.text:
The schema layer provides authoritative, versioned snapshots and structured retrieval to ground planning. It is split into:

  • Schema contracts: structural schema (tables, columns, foreign keys).
  • Schema metadata: descriptive enrichment and statistics.
  • Schema store: versioned persistence with fingerprinting.
  • Schema retrieval: staged lookup via schema chunks.

docs.title: Schema contracts and metadata
docs.text:
Schema contracts are defined in nl2sql_sdk.schema:

  • SchemaContract: datasource_id, engine_type, tables
  • TableContract: table ref, column contracts, foreign keys
  • ColumnContract: name, type, nullability, primary key flag
  • ForeignKeyContract: constrained/referred columns, cardinality, business meaning

Metadata complements contracts:

  • SchemaMetadata: datasource description/domains, table metadata
  • TableMetadata: table description, row_count, column metadata
  • ColumnMetadata: description, stats, synonyms, PII flag
  • ColumnStatistics: distinct counts, min/max, sample values (for a text column: every distinct value when there are at most 50, else the five most frequent; most frequent first, ties by value). A column the adapter could not profile has no statistics; see Column statistics

docs.title: Snapshotting and fingerprinting
docs.text:
Each SchemaSnapshot (contract + metadata) is versioned using a deterministic fingerprint:

  • Fingerprint uses datasource ID, engine type, sorted tables, sorted columns, and sorted foreign keys.
  • Resulting hash is used to deduplicate identical snapshots.

docs.title: Schema store backends
docs.text:
build_schema_store() constructs a store based on settings:

  • InMemorySchemaStore: in-memory, versioned snapshots.
  • SqliteSchemaStore: persistent storage with indexes on fingerprint and timestamps. One connection serves every thread, and each use of it holds one lock, so a server reading the schema and the index health on two workers at once is safe.

Schema versions are timestamped and include a fingerprint prefix (e.g., YYYYMMDDhhmmss_<fp8>). Old versions are evicted beyond schema_store_max_versions.

The store also holds the plan cache: validated, executed plans keyed by (normalised sub-query intent, run date and planner model, datasource_id, schema_version), in the plan_cache table of the SQLite store (a dict in the in-memory one). Evicting a schema version deletes its cached plans; nl2sql cache clear deletes them all and keeps the snapshots. See Determinism → The plan cache.

The same SQLite file holds the playground's answer ratings, in a feedback table (one row per rated run; questions and SQL, never rows). It is written whatever SCHEMA_STORE_BACKEND is, at SCHEMA_STORE_PATH; nl2sql feedback clear empties it and nothing else. See Feedback and Signals.

The fingerprint covers structure only (tables, columns, keys). Registering a snapshot whose structure matches an existing version returns that version unchanged, so anything keyed on it (the plan cache) stays valid, but the stored metadata (statistics, descriptions, enrichment) is replaced by the new snapshot's and the version becomes the latest again. The snapshot store and the chunks built from the same snapshot therefore always agree.

docs.title: Retrieval and authority
docs.text:
Schema retrieval resolves authoritative tables/columns from SchemaStore, not from the vector store. Vector store chunks are only used to identify candidates; final schema is resolved via snapshot. If retrieval yields no candidates, the retriever falls back to the full snapshot. schema_version_mismatch_policy governs mismatches between chunk versions and store versions.

See ../architecture/indexing.md for retrieval stages, chunk types, and vector store behavior.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: Authorization is enforced at planning time, by the logical validator, before any SQL exists. That is the one security property this engine provides. It is not authentication, it is not containment, and it is not row- or column-level security.

docs.title: The role is supplied by the caller
docs.text:
There is no authentication anywhere in this project. Where the role comes from depends on the client:

  • CLI: nl2sql run --role <id>, defaulting to admin.
  • Python API: UserContext(roles=[...]), whatever the calling code passes.
  • REST API: the get_user_context dependency (packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/auth.py). It reads a header set by a trusted proxy (api.role_header in nl2sql.yaml) or a static role (api.role), and answers HTTP 401 when neither gives one. The body's user_context counts only with the dev flag api.trust_body_role: true, which logs a warning at startup. See Caller role. The routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index also need one of the roles in policies.admin_roles (default [admin]), else HTTP 403; with no role source configured they answer loopback clients only. See Admin routes.

The REST API still does not verify who the caller is. If you expose this service, put your own authentication in a proxy in front of it, derive the role from that, and have the proxy overwrite the role header on every request; otherwise any client can send the header itself. An empty roles list denies everything, which is the correct default for an unauthenticated caller.

A role name that is not present in the policy file grants nothing, exactly like an empty roles list. RBAC skips it, so the caller is refused with a normal SECURITY_VIOLATION, not a crash: through the pipeline the datasource resolver refuses first (no datasource is allowed), and the validator on its own refuses every table with its policy check failed. An unknown name listed beside a known one is ignored, and the known role's permissions still apply.

docs.title: Strict refusal
docs.text:
If a question needs a table the caller's role cannot read, the run is refused. Tables are never hidden from the planner, because a planner that cannot see a table quietly answers a different question from the tables it can see, and a confident wrong answer is worse than a refusal. The validator refuses the plan before any SQL exists, and the run ends there.

  • Structure yes, data no. The planner and the refiner still see every table's name, columns, types, primary key and relationships, so a plan can name the forbidden table and be refused. For a table the role cannot read, the column statistics are stripped: sample_values, min_value, max_value, distinct_count and null_percentage never reach the prompt, the LLM provider or the run trace. The schema retriever decides this with the same rule the validator enforces (table_allowed in auth/rbac.py), on both the full-snapshot path and the vector-retrieval path. Column and table descriptions are kept: they are structure. (For tables the role can read, the prompt carries sample_values and, for a date, time or numeric column, its [min, max] as range; the other statistics stay in the snapshot.) If you let an enrichment step write descriptions from real values, those descriptions are not stripped.
  • A generic message for the user. The refusal the caller sees is "You do not have permission to see the data this question requires." It names no table, because naming one tells an unauthorised user that it exists. The table and the role are logged as a warning and recorded in the error's details (datasource_id, table, roles), which the run trace keeps and the QueryResult error summary does not carry. The validator's policy check is still present with passed: false, so a UI can show the gate firing.
  • Naming tables is an opt-in. Set policies.refusal_names_tables: true to put the role and table in the user-facing message ("Role 'viewer' denied access to 'chinook.Customer'. ..."). The demo's config (nl2sql init --demo) sets it, because showing the refusal is the demo's point.
  • The decision is deterministic code. Only the validator decides, from the policy and the plan's table list. Nothing the model writes (its reasoning, a claim that the role is allowed) is read by the policy check, so a crafted prompt cannot turn a refusal into an allow.

This is a table-level allowlist with data stripping. It is not column masking and not row-level security: a role that may read a table reads every column and every row of it. A downloaded trace of a permitted run holds real rows, and the playground serves any trace by id with no login, so restricting a trace to the user who produced it is left to a multi-user deployment.

docs.title: Security controls
docs.text:
• RBAC policies: the policies section of nl2sql.yaml, evaluated by RBAC. A policy is a per-role allowlist of datasources and of tables (datasource.schema.table, with schema and datasource wildcards) — nothing finer. There is no column masking and no row-level security.
  • Logical validation enforces schema constraints and policy-based table access.
  • Audit logging records llm.changed events only: each engine.llm.replace (the Python API, PUT /api/v1/settings/llm, the playground's model switch), with who made it and each agent's old and new model, never a key. Queries are not audited. See ../observability/stack.md.
  • Bounded execution: a global timeout and a per-run cancellation token cap each run. There is no process sandbox — the engine runs in-process (see ../execution/isolation.md).

docs.title: What keeps the SQL read-only
docs.text:
The model never writes SQL. It emits a typed plan whose query_type is Literal["READ"] — pydantic rejects anything else before a node sees the plan, which is the whole enforcement — and the generator renders that plan with sqlglot starting from exp.select(). A statement that is not a SELECT therefore cannot be produced, and free text from the model is never executed.

What is not in place: database connections are not opened read-only on any dialect, and the executor has no statement-kind or statement-count gate of its own. The read-only property is structural, not defended in depth. Grant the engine a read-only database user.

flowchart TD
    User[UserContext] --> RBAC[RBAC]
    RBAC --> Validator[LogicalValidatorNode]
    Validator --> Executor[ExecutorNode]
    Executor --> Audit[EventLogger]

docs.title: RBAC enforcement details
docs.text:
LogicalValidatorNode enforces strict namespacing:

  • Allowed tables must match datasource.*, datasource.schema.*, datasource.schema.table or datasource.table. The schema counts: a grant of sales.orders does not allow audit.orders, and a two-part datasource.table means that table in the datasource's default schema only (see Policies).
  • If no datasource ID is present, validation fails closed.
  • Wildcard access is supported via * in policy lists.
  • An unknown role, or no role, allows nothing and is refused like any denial.
  • One SECURITY_VIOLATION per forbidden table, with the generic message unless RBAC_REFUSAL_NAMES_TABLES is set, and details naming the table and roles.

docs.title: Validation gates
docs.text: Validation rules are enforced by LogicalValidatorNode and documented in ../architecture/invariants.md and ../architecture/nodes/logical_validator_node.md.

docs.title: Multi-Tenant Isolation Model
docs.text: Multi-tenancy is enforced through context propagation, artifact partitioning, and policy filtering. Tenant identity originates from Settings.tenant_id and is passed through execution requests and artifact paths.

docs.title: Tenant context propagation
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Settings[Settings.tenant_id] --> Context[Runtime.tenant_id]
    Context --> Executor[ExecutorNode/ExecutorRequest]
    Executor --> Artifacts[ArtifactStore.create_artifact_ref]

docs.title: Storage isolation
docs.text:
Artifacts are persisted under a tenant-partitioned path on every backend, driven by RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATH_TEMPLATE (default <tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet):

<backend root>/<tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet

This ensures per-tenant isolation for artifacts, and downstream aggregation only reads referenced artifacts from the current request.

Tenant isolation is not applied to indexing; the vector store and schema store are global in the current implementation (see ../architecture/indexing.md).

docs.title: Authorization model
docs.text: RBAC evaluates UserContext.roles against the policies section of nl2sql.yaml. The validator enforces datasource/table scope at planning time.

docs.title: Artifact Store Architecture
docs.text:
Execution results are persisted as artifacts. A single ArtifactStore writes Parquet files under the engine's results folder, <storage.path>/results/, and emits ArtifactRef metadata used by aggregation and downstream consumers. Each sub-query's result is one artifact, and the run's combined result is another, beside them.

Results are local files only. The S3 and ADLS backends, and the RESULT_ARTIFACT_BACKEND, RESULT_ARTIFACT_S3_* and RESULT_ARTIFACT_ADLS_* settings, were removed in 0.5: they were untested and unreachable from the new config. The Phase 2 results-store interface brings remote stores back.

docs.title: Storage lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Adapter[Adapter: execute_batches or execute] --> Batches[ResultFrame batches]
    Batches --> Store[ArtifactStore.write_batches]
    Store --> Parquet[Sub-query Parquet object]
    Parquet --> Ref[ArtifactRef]
    Ref --> Aggregation[EngineAggregatorNode: polars scan]
    Aggregation --> Combined[ArtifactStore.write_lazy]
    Combined --> Result[Combined result Parquet object]
    Result --> Computed[AggregatorResponse.computed_artifacts]
    Combined --> Manifest[manifest.json beside the results]
    Manifest --> Reader[ResultReader: page or CSV by request id]
    Result --> Reader

docs.title: Batched writes
docs.text:
A result is written a batch at a time, so a large one is never held whole as Python rows. The executor reads it from the adapter's execute_batches when the adapter has one (the SDK's optional StreamingAdapterProtocol; every SQLAlchemy adapter does) in batches of settings.results.fetch_batch_size rows (default 10,000), and from execute, as one batch, when it does not.

ArtifactStore.write_batches writes a single batch straight to the artifact, exactly as before. From the second batch on, each batch is written to its own part file in a temporary folder as it arrives, and polars then streams the parts into the artifact (sink_parquet), concatenated with vertical_relaxed so a column that is empty in one batch and text in the next is text. At most one batch is in memory at a time. If the adapter reports a failure between batches, nothing is written, the parts are removed, and the sub-query fails as it would have from execute. create_artifact_ref(frame, metadata) is write_batches([frame], metadata).

docs.title: The combined result
docs.text:
The aggregator reads each sub-query's artifact as a polars scan (ArtifactStore.scan_parquet), so combines and post-combine operations build one lazy plan, and writes each terminal result of the DAG to its own artifact with ArtifactStore.write_lazy, which streams the plan into the file and reads the row count and columns back from the file's metadata. It is rendered from the same template as the sub-query artifacts, with result_<node_id> as sub_query_id and dag_node_id, so the default template puts it in the run's folder:

<tenant_id>/<request_id>/result_<node_id>.parquet

A combined result has no subgraph or schema version of its own: a template that names <subgraph_name> or <schema_version> gets aggregator and result. Its ArtifactRef (with sub_query_id unset) is recorded in AggregatorResponse.computed_artifacts under the terminal node's id, and its row_count is the whole result's. AggregatorResponse.terminal_results holds only the first settings.results.preview_rows rows of it, read from the saved file, for the answer model.

docs.title: The result manifest
docs.text:
After saving a run's results the aggregator writes a manifest beside them with ArtifactStore.write_manifest: which results the run produced, never their rows.

{"request_id": "0f1c...", "results": [
  {"node_id": "combine_g1", "columns": ["genre_name"], "row_count": 25, "truncated": false}]}

truncated is true when a sub-query upstream of that node in the DAG was cut at its row cap. The same entries are AggregatorResponse.results and QueryResult.result_manifest.

Its path is the artifact template rendered like a saved result's, with manifest as the name and .json for .parquet, so the default template puts it at:

<tenant_id>/<request_id>/manifest.json

A template without <sub_query_id> or <dag_node_id> gets -manifest added, as any file of the run would (see One artifact per sub-query), so a flat template still gives each run its own manifest.

docs.title: Reading a result back
docs.text:
ResultReader (execution/artifacts/results.py), behind engine.results (manifest, page and csv) (see Query API), reads one tenant's results by request id:

  1. The request id and the result id must be plain tokens (letters, digits, _, -; up to 128 characters). Anything else is ResultNotFound, before any path is built.
  2. The manifest is read from the path rendered for the reader's tenant and that request id (ArtifactStore.read_manifest). No file there is ResultNotFound, so another tenant's run is not found, not refused.
  3. The result id must be a node_id the manifest lists. The parquet path is then rendered from the template, exactly as the aggregator wrote it (ArtifactStore.scan_result); the manifest never supplies a path.
  4. A page is scan.slice(offset, limit).collect() on a polars scan, so only that slice is read. A CSV export collects one CSV_CHUNK_ROWS (10,000) slice at a time and yields it as CSV text, header first.

docs.title: Where the files go
docs.text:
An artifact's path is <results folder>/<rendered path>, and its parent folders are created as it is written. For an engine built from a Config the results folder is <storage.path>/results/ (see Public Facade → Creating an engine), so the default template gives:

<storage.path>/results/<tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet

The store is exercised by real read/write round-trip tests (packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_artifact_store.py).

docs.title: ArtifactRef fields
docs.text:
ArtifactRef contains:

  • uri, backend (always local), format
  • row_count, columns, bytes
  • content_hash, created_at
  • optional schema_version
  • optional sub_query_id, the sub-query whose result this is
  • path_template, the template actually rendered (see One artifact per sub-query)

docs.title: Path templating
docs.text:
The path template defines the artifact path relative to the results folder. It defaults to:

<tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet

Each <key> placeholder is substituted from the metadata the executor passes to write_batches. The SQL executor supplies these keys:

  • tenant_id
  • request_id (the trace ID, shared by every sub-query of a run)
  • sub_query_id (the sub-query's id, which is also its scan node's id)
  • dag_node_id (the same value as sub_query_id)
  • subgraph_name
  • schema_version

A template referencing any other placeholder raises a ValueError naming the placeholder that could not be filled. A path is never written with an unrendered placeholder in it. Adding placeholders therefore requires threading the corresponding metadata through the executor first.

docs.title: One artifact per sub-query
docs.text:
A question that decomposes into several sub-queries runs them under one trace ID, often side by side, and each must write its own file. When they shared <tenant_id>/<request_id>.parquet, concurrent writes produced one corrupt Parquet file (AGGREGATOR_FAILED: parquet: File out of specification), and sequential writes kept only the last sub-query's rows, so a join combined a result with itself and returned a wrong answer with no error.

A template that names neither <sub_query_id> nor <dag_node_id> is therefore made unique rather than rejected: the store adds -<sub_query_id> to the end of the file name, before its extension, so <tenant_id>/<request_id>.parquet writes <tenant_id>/<request_id>-<sub_query_id>.parquet. The ArtifactRef records the template actually rendered in path_template and the sub-query in sub_query_id. A store used directly, with no sub_query_id in its metadata, renders the template as written.

docs.title: Tenant-aware paths
docs.text:
Because the default template starts with <tenant_id>, artifacts are partitioned per tenant:

<results folder>/<tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet

docs.title: Testing Architecture
docs.text: Tests are organized by scope and live under packages/**/tests. The core engine has unit, integration, and end-to-end tests.

docs.title: Test layout
docs.text:
packages/nl2sql/tests/
  unit/             # Node-level tests, registries, stores
  integration/      # Pipeline components with real data
  e2e/              # End-to-end flows
  cli/              # CLI command tests
  adapters/         # Cross-dialect adapter contract tests
  sqlalchemy_base/  # SQLAlchemy base adapter tests
packages/api/tests/ # FastAPI route and service tests (stubbed engine)

pytest.ini is the single source of truth for pytest configuration - test paths, markers, and addopts. Do not add a [tool.pytest.ini_options] table to pyproject.toml: pytest reads only one config file, and pytest.ini wins, so such a table is silently ignored. Dev/test tooling lives in the root pyproject.toml under [dependency-groups] dev (pip install --group dev).

docs.title: Markers and what CI runs
docs.text:
Two independent things can make a test unrunnable in CI, so they are two markers. A test may carry both.

Marker Means Provided by integration Needs external resources: the demo's SQLite databases - vendored Chinook and the generated support and webanalytics, read from the installed package (nl2sql.testing.config.make_demo_config) - or the downloaded ONNX embedding model. The package; tests/e2e writes its own project with nl2sql init --demo llm Needs a real OPENAI_API_KEY. Costs money per run. Nothing in CI - never selected.

Everything under packages/nl2sql/tests/integration/ is marked integration automatically by packages/nl2sql/tests/conftest.py. The llm marker is declared per module, next to a comment saying which call needs the key. Only four modules carry it - test_ast_planner_real_data.py, test_decomposer_real_data.py, test_logical_validator_real_data.py and test_answer_synthesizer_real_data.py - all of them nodes that call a chat model directly. Nothing else in the directory needs a key: indexing skips its optional enrichment pass when no LLM is available, so tests that index real data run key-free.

.github/workflows/test.yml has two test jobs over the source tree:

  • test runs pytest -m "not integration" across Python 3.12 and 3.13. This is the fast job and must stay fast.
  • integration runs pytest -m "integration and not llm" on one Python version, after writing and indexing a demo project (nl2sql init --demo demo-ci and nl2sql --config demo-ci/nl2sql.yaml index), key-free with the local embedder. The ONNX model is cached across runs. That subset covers schema indexing, datasource resolution, schema retrieval, aggregation and the local embedder against the real Chinook database; run it with --collect-only -q for the current list.

Three more jobs test the package rather than the source tree:

  • api-image builds packages/api/Dockerfile from the repository root, the image the release pushes to GHCR, without pushing it, and imports nl2sql_api.main inside it. tests/unit/test_docker_images.py separately checks that every Dockerfile's FROM python:X.Y satisfies every package's requires-python.

  • build builds the three wheels and sdists, installs them into a clean virtualenv and runs import nl2sql and nl2sql --help.

  • fresh-install takes those wheels and installs them the way a user does, pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]", into an empty virtualenv outside the checkout. It then boots nl2sql demo --hosted (the command the Hugging Face Space runs) with no API key, and passes only when the playground page, /api/meta, /api/schema and /api/index all answer from that install. It is what catches a wheel that imports but ships without the built playground, the sample databases or a dependency the demo extra forgot. scripts/fresh_install_check.py is the whole check, so it runs the same on a laptop:

    pip install build
python scripts/fresh_install_check.py --build   # builds into dist/ first

Any *_API_KEY in your environment is dropped for the run, so a key you exported cannot make it pass where CI would fail. The decisions it makes are unit-tested in tests/unit/test_fresh_install_check.py. After a release the same script runs twice more, from publish_pypi.yaml: with --pypi X.Y.Z to install the published version from PyPI itself, and with --url https://nadeem4nk-nl2sql-demo.hf.space --expect-version X.Y.Z to wait for the live Space to serve it, then once more with its custom domain as --url (see Releasing).

Nothing selects llm. Those tests are run by hand with a key:

OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... pytest -m integration

Collection is not enough to keep these honest. Every test in the directory imports cleanly even when it calls a method that no longer exists, so rot shows up only at call time - which is the point of running the key-free subset in CI rather than gating on --collect-only. The subset is worth keeping wide: every test that can run without a key should, because the ones that cannot are never run by CI at all.

docs.title: Randomised test order
docs.text: pytest-randomly shuffles the order of tests on every run, which turns order-dependent tests - shared class-level caches, leaked globals, fixtures that do not unwind - into loud local failures rather than intermittent CI ones. Each run prints the seed it used; reproduce a failure with pytest -p randomly --randomly-seed=<seed>.

docs.title: Settings in tests
docs.text:
The engine reads its settings from its runtime, not from a process global (configuration v2, section 8), so a test sets them on the runtime it builds:

  • One node or service: nl2sql.testing.runtime.fake_runtime(settings=..., policies=..., traces_dir=..., **attrs) builds a stand-in runtime with a real config. Settings are written as in YAML: settings={"traces": {"mode": "always"}}.
  • A whole engine: Runtime.from_config(make_config(tmp_path, ...)). An Embeddings(instance=FakeEmbeddings(size=8)) keeps it free of any model.
  • One run with different settings: ctx.derive({"settings.pipeline.plan_cache": True}) returns a run-scoped runtime with a derived config, its own curated answers and its own LLMSet, sharing the stores and the engine's LLM client cache. Evaluation and trace replay use it the same way; the runtime it came from never changes. tests/unit/test_run_scoped_runtime.py pins that down.

There is no process-global settings object to monkeypatch, and no module writes os.environ: a test sets what it needs in the config it builds. The architecture tests keep it that way (An Engine Owns Its Config).

flowchart TD
    Unit[Unit Tests] --> Core[Core Components]
    Integration[Integration Tests] --> Pipeline[Pipeline Nodes]
    E2E[End-to-end Tests] --> Orchestration[Full Orchestration]

  • Subgraph orchestration (test_sql_agent_subgraph.py)
  • DAG layering (test_graph_layers.py)
  • Registry and store behavior (test_*_registry.py, test_schema_store.py)
  • REST contract (packages/api/tests/) via FastAPI TestClient with the get_engine dependency overridden, so no datasource, LLM or network is needed

docs.title: Deterministic validation
docs.text:
Tests enforce deterministic behavior by:

  • using structured output schemas for planner/decomposer
  • validating stable IDs and DAG layering
  • running logical validator checks for expected schema alignment

docs.text: The SDK includes testing utilities to validate schema introspection and result contracts for new adapters.
